coat's sharp reflections -- as the first transfer had, under no coat. The
paint is OpenPBR at metalness 1 over a base of 0.05, and a gaussian reflected
every metal as a conductor of the artistic index (`mxArtisticIor` of the
colour and an edge of the specular colour, white here), which is
standard_surface's metal. OpenPBR's is MaterialX's `generalized_schlick_bsdf`
-- the colour head on, the specular colour at 82 degrees -- and for a dark
metal the two part by twice at an angle:

| angle | conductor (n 0.91, k 0.41) | Schlick from 0.047 |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.046 | 0.047 |
| 45 | 0.077 | 0.049 |
| 60 | 0.172 | 0.077 |
| 70 | 0.312 | 0.165 |
| 80 | 0.560 | 0.414 |

A gaussian now knows which its metal is: `StageMaterial::schlickMetal` for
OpenPBR and glTF, one int a gaussian in the stage
(`primvars:athenea:splat:schlickMetal`), a mark of 4 on the transmission the
streams kernel hands the decode (beside a thin wall's 2), bit 25 of the `pbr`
word, and `SplatSurface::schlickMetal`; `environmentBrdfOf` then reflects a
metal with the DFG fit of its own two ends and their compensation
(`ggxEnvSchlickMetal`). A light's lobe was a Schlick already. A cloud without
the primvar, and every standard_surface or UsdPreviewSurface metal, is
reflected as before.

Checked (pending the GPU turn): the Schlick never above the conductor, between 30 and 75 degrees, for the
paint's base, its colour head on, a white metal white ([schlick] in
athenea_render_tests); the paint ball and the Corvette's paint again.

### A conversion measured by the engine itself

The Corvette was measured material by material with three scripts outside
the tree (a map of materials to meshes parsed out of a conversion's log, a
mask by the depth difference of two frames, oiiotool's crops and `athenea
compare` once a material), which only worked for that car and needed someone
to drive them. `athenea mesh2splat --validate DIR` is the same measurement as
a feature of the conversion, for any stage:

- **The groups** are the stage's bindings, read on the processor
  (`usd::stageMaterialGroups`): every visible mesh whose binding, or a
  GeomSubset's, names a material. A mesh of two materials is in both groups.
- **The conversion** is the command's own (`runConversion`), run once a
  group with every mesh outside it hidden, so every option asked of the
  conversion is what is measured.
- **The GT** is path traced once and kept (`DIR/gt.exr`); the stage is
  rasterised once as meshes with its Cryptomatte.
- **The mask** is the mesh frame's matte: the coverage of every rank whose id
  hashes one of the group's meshes (`validateMask`), with its sum and box by
  atomics. It replaces the depth difference, which needed a frame a material
  and missed what the two frames share.
- **The numbers** are the Measure effect's over the mask's box, of both frames
  multiplied by the mask, the error's sum divided by the mask's: relMSE, p99,
  the means. The mesh rasterised is measured the same way beside it.

What it does not do: a material whose meshes are all inside another's box
still reads its own pixels only, but a GeomSubset's material is masked with
its whole mesh. The relit and baked modes are measured the same way, since
the conversion is whatever was asked.

Checked (pending the GPU turn): two balls and a ground
(`tests/data/validate`), the three materials measured and the table written
(`mesh2splat_validate`).

### The filter took sixteen entries, and was handed thirty-two

The balls of the TX test in the tx-next run showed the chrome's lower half
black, where the ground stands in its mirror: the reflected field read
nothing. The bounced halves went through `SplatBakeFilter` as one picture of
the indirect half's sixteen coefficients and the field's sixteen, thirty-two
entries a gaussian, and the effect's `coefficients` parameter stops at
sixteen (its hard maximum): it read gaussian k at 16 k, and wrote the
answer back over the wrong entries. The two halves now go through it apart,
sixteen entries each (`TransferFilterIo::part`); step 2's measurement, made
before the filter, had the field whole.

### Maps on the layers

A gaussian carried its specular, coat and sheen as constants of the material;
a map on any of them was logged and its constant stood, so a coat painted on
in places, or a fuzz with a pattern, converted flat. The maps are now sampled
as the base's are: `StageMaterial::layerMaps` keeps, for the first three a
material has, which input a map stands for (specular weight or colour, coat
weight or roughness, sheen colour, weight or roughness) and the map; the
conversion hands them to the Mesh2Splat effect as clips `Layer0`..`Layer2`
with `layer<k>Target`, `Channel` and `Uv2`, additively; and `m2sLayersAt`
reads each at the gaussian's coordinates in place of the constant -- the
sheen, carried as its colour times its weight, multiplying a map on one by
the other's constant (`sheenWeight`, `sheenColourAlone`). An index and the
coat's darkening stay constants: the first is a byte a gaussian of 1 to 3,
the second a switch. The effect's uniform block grows by 112 bytes at its
end (544), which a bundle that does not set them reads as no maps.

Checked (pending the GPU turn): a card whose coat weight is half nothing and
half whole converts to gaussians a third or more of each
(`a_map_on_a_layer_is_sampled_per_gaussian`).

`--validate-sky white` (or an image) draws every frame -- the GT, the mesh,
the clouds -- under another sky with the stage's other lights off: a layer
over the stage (`DIR/sky.usda`) that sets each dome's image and colour and
deactivates every other light. Under a constant white dome a transfer's
error is its occlusion's and its reflection's alone, with no sky detail to
hide in -- the experiment proposals 030 and 031 ask for. The conversion is
the stage's own; a transfer does not depend on the light it is baked under.

### The direct half without grain (proposal 032's first part)

A TX transfer traces one ray a cell of its grid over the sphere for the open
directions, and that set of rays is a quadrature: each cell is worth its
solid angle, which for the octahedral map is `4 / side^2` over `|p|^3`, `p`
the point of the octahedron the cell's centre decodes from (an area element
of the facet, `sqrt(3) dx dy`, seen from the centre at `|p|` along a
direction at `1 / sqrt(3) |p|` to the facet's normal). With the cells, the
direct half is now `sum V Y_k cos dOmega / pi` over them instead of the
stratified paths' escapes: deterministic, so the grain the direct light
carried -- the shadows' -- is gone, at 256 directions a gaussian (1024 at
32 cells), half of them above the surface. The indirect half and the field
are still the paths'. Checked (pending the GPU turn): the unoccluded
point's sixteen coefficients against the clamped cosine's, at 16 cells
(`[degree3]`).

## The ground under a dome, without grain and without its 480 ms (task PLAY-G)

The whole TX Corvette played back in raster at 1920 x 1080 in 158 ms a frame
alone and 637 ms on its mesh ground (`/World/Ground` of `corvette_scene.usda`,
a 60 m plane of OpenPBR grey), and the ground was grain: one dome sample a
pixel with its shadow ray, std/mean 2.7 over a patch of it against the path
traced frame's 0.12. `ATHENEA_STAGES=1` now says where a mesh layer's time
goes, a line a frame -- its preparation and the cloud map in it, visibility,
lobe directions, shadow rays, shading, the domes -- and it said: the map 77
ms, the lobe directions 109 (a second evaluation of the material, for the
lobe samples' shadow rays), the shading 150 to 220, the splat blend 30 more
than without a ground. Four changes, each where the time was.

### The dome, read prefiltered (`athenea:domePrefiltered`, on)

A surface whose lobes all reflect, under a dome the frame prepared
(`Environment`, up to four), takes the dome in closed form instead of by a
sample: its diffuse lobes the irradiance of the sky's nine harmonics at the
normal plus the sun `env_sun` took out of them, its glossy lobes the dome's
own image along the mirror direction at the mip whose texels are as wide as
the lobe (4 pi alpha^2 against 4 pi / (w h)), each weighed by its directional
albedo -- the split sum. The cloud's shadow is the map's six dome directions,
each read by `shadowMapReadSoft`: a blocker search over nine texels of the
nearest-caster depth and the transmittance chain read at the penumbra that
distance gives under a source as wide as the region of sky the direction
stands for (tan 30 degrees), weighed by the direction's cosine and the sky's
brightness there. No sample and no ray.

It is two kernels. The shading kernel leaves what the lobe stack says of a
pixel (the two albedos, the glossy alpha, where it stands and its normal) in
three textures, and `dome_shade.slang`, which holds no lobe stack, adds the
domes. Written into the shading kernel the read overflowed what Metal keeps
of a thread: rows of garbage across the ground, and a pipeline that would
not compile without the cloud map. A device that still refuses the kernel
with the G-buffer samples its domes, said once.

What it does not do: a mesh shadowing another mesh from a dome (there is no
ray); a stack with a lobe that transmits (glass, a thin wall) or a fibre
keeps the dome sampled; a fifth dome is its image's mean. The six
directions are a coarse sky: a low horizon is shadowed by the ring forty
degrees up.

`--no-dome-prefilter` samples the dome as before. The path tracer, and so
the ground truth, is untouched.

### The cloud map is built when what it shows changes

It is the casters' and the lights', not the camera's: seven passes over 14.7
million gaussians re-measured a car that did not move. A frame whose clouds
(their buffers and `revision`, which a pose counts up), transforms, lights
and map settings are the last map's reads that map again. A frame with levels
of detail always builds: its cut's clouds are the camera's.

### Under domes alone, no ray and no second evaluation

Where every light of the frame is a prefiltered dome, the lobe directions and
the shadow rays are not drawn at all; a surface the prefiltered read cannot
answer (glass) samples its domes shadowed by the clouds' map alone.

### A material the same everywhere is shaded from a table

Most of what was left was the OpenPBR graph itself, evaluated at every
pixel of the ground: layers and mixes of sixteen-lobe BSDFs in thread
memory, 150 ms. A material whose inputs are all values and whose graph reads
no texture coordinate, position, primvar or noise (`kMaterialUniform`, found
in the generated source) returns, on a flat patch, what depends on the angle
to the eye alone. Under prefiltered domes alone such a material is
tabulated once a frame (`tabulateMaterials`, 32 angles: the two albedos, the
alpha, the opacity, the emission) and its pixels are shaded from the table by
a kernel of their own (`shadeTabled`); the shading kernel steps aside for
them.

### A material that varies, under domes alone, without the lights' code

A texture on a UsdPreviewSurface's diffuse colour makes it vary, so the
table cannot stand in for it, and it went back to the shading kernel: 35 ms
of shading at 1920 x 1080 on an RTX 3070 (CUDA) for a room of five textured
quads under a dome, against 1.3 for the same room in plain colours. Not the
texture: a kernel that never reads it took the same. Nsight Compute: 255
registers, an occupancy of 16%, the DRAM 82% busy -- thread memory, about
5 KB a pixel, the lobe stacks and the BSDF values the graph passes between
its nodes.

Three changes. Under prefiltered domes alone, a pixel whose lobes all reflect
is shaded by `shadeEvaluated`, which evaluates its material and writes what
the shading kernel would have (the emission, the coverage, the two albedos
for `dome_shade.slang`) with none of the lights' code; it writes a mask, 1
where it shaded and 0 where it left the pixel (a lobe that transmits, a dome
linked away), and the shading kernel skips the 1s. A frame whose meshes all
draw with materials the table answers does not run it (`MaterialFrame::varying`,
the rows the frame's meshes resolved to): over a whole frame it still reads
every pixel's visibility and writes the mask, 0.3 ms of shading on the RTX
3070 for a stage of plain-coloured cubes and cards. And UsdPreviewSurface's
lobes are built by one node (`athenea_preview_bsdf`) where its graph made a
dozen BSDF values of sixteen lobes each: the same lobes pushed in the same
order, the same weights, the same layer marks. And the lobe stacks are as
deep as the frame's materials need: `kBuildLobes` and `kMaxLobes` are
link-time constants the materials' dispatch module exports, counted from the
generated source (a BSDF node's call one lobe, the preview node five, a graph
function's what its calls push; both sides of a branch count, and never past
the device's 16 and 8). A room of UsdPreviewSurfaces builds and keeps five; a
kernel that imports no materials keeps the defaults. The stack is finished in
place (`atheneaFinishStack` writes `gAtheneaResult`), one copy of it fewer.

| the room, textured, under a dome (RTX 3070, CUDA, `ATHENEA_STAGES=1`) | shading | median a frame |
|---|---|---|
| before | 35.0 ms | 53.1 ms |
| `shadeEvaluated` | 29.7 | 48.5 |
| and the preview surface as one node | 27.7 | 47.1 |
| and the stacks five deep, finished in place | 12.1 | 30.9 |
| the room in plain colours (the table) | 1.3 | 20.3 |

**Checked**: the frame against the graph's, in the room as it is and with a
metal floor under a coat, a specular-workflow wall, a coated one, a metal
one and an ior of 2.2: 8-bit max 2, none over 2, relMSE 1e-9. The kernel
against the shading kernel's frame: identical.

The median a frame is `athenea stage`'s, which reads every frame back; the
GPU's own time for the textured room, by Nsight Compute, went from 33.6 ms
a frame to 15.9, `shadeEvaluated` from 28.7 to 11.0.

**Not done**: `shadeEvaluated` is still thread memory -- 2 KB a thread, 128
registers, the DRAM 91% busy: the built lobes and the kept ones are two
copies of 128-byte lobes, and the inputs, the vertex data and the BSDF value
around them. A lobe of fewer bytes, or a stack the material writes once,
is what is left to take.

### A set seen from one place, flattened for a camera's zone

A virtual TV set (an interior of 8 x 4 x 10 m: LED strips, lacquered panels,
a polished wooden floor) played in real time by a standard Gaussian Splatting
rasteriser, with the camera a PTZ head that only turns about its optical
centre. Two changes take its light to a standard file.

**`athenea flatten --baked`** writes every cloud of the stage, its light baked
in, as the frame shows it: the TX-only test let no baked cloud through.
**`--view-box`** fits each gaussian on its own, to directions towards
`--view-box-samples` points of the camera's zone (R3, a low-discrepancy
sequence over the box) with the sphere's `--directions` weighing
`--view-box-outside` of them: its normal equations summed in the kernel and
solved by Cholesky (`flatSolveInPlace`), so degree 3 is spent where the
camera looks. The shared matrix M stays for a cloud without a zone.
A zone seen from far is a few degrees of directions: a set's back wall,
six metres from a zone of thirty centimetres, was fitted from those alone,
its constant term went below black and the wall came out black between its
panels. A cloud whose colour does not turn with the eye -- baked, degree 0 --
is fitted by M whatever the zone.

**`mesh2splat --bake-toward X Y Z`** bakes what a camera standing within
`--bake-toward-radius` of the point sees: every path of a gaussian that faces
the point looks from a point drawn in that ball, and the first vertex keeps
the whole material, polish included (`bakeTowardFaces`), where a bake keeps
only the body. One direction a gaussian, so one colour (degree 0).

**Where the light was lost.** Measured at the set's reference camera
(532 x 263, the path tracer at 512 paths, 3 bounces), the cloud baked over
the hemisphere read a linear mean of 0.315 against 0.416, and 28 to 30 %
dark alike with the LED strips alone (0.164 / 0.232) and the studio's fill
light alone (0.134 / 0.186). The bake's filter is not it: unfiltered, the
display-referred means are the same (0.167 / 0.166). The floor is: 0.024
against 0.081 over a patch of it -- its polish, the strips' reflection in a
roughness 0.4 varnish, which the body drops. Baked from the camera's place,
the patch reads 0.073 and the frame 0.337. What stays dark is detail finer
than the cell: 150 000 gaussians over the set put the back wall at cells
10.5 times what a pixel covers, and a strip 2 cm wide among them.

**The cell a mesh takes is its nearest point's** (`--cell-from-camera`): a
floor that runs from under the camera to the back wall is cut at the
camera's feet, and took 75 % of the budget. The sets' long meshes are split
in bands of a metre along the depth (`scene_bands.usdc`, made by the set's
author), each band the cell of its own distance.

**Where a set's detail is.** Shared in proportion, every piece is coarsened
alike -- 5.7 to 8.1 times what a pixel covers over the three sets at 700 000
gaussians -- and the logos on the back wall, six metres off, read as blurs.
`--detail PRIM=FACTOR` gives the pieces under a prim FACTOR² times their
part, never more than they want, the rest shared again a few rounds, so
their cell is FACTOR times finer than the others'.

**What a turning camera never sees.** In the wide shot (about 50 degrees)
the sets showed horizontal streaks and torn edges at the sides of the
panels and of the reliefs: the side faces that point away from the PTZ.
A camera that only turns about one point never sees them -- the mesh's
own body hides them -- but a gaussian is drawn from both sides and has no
body behind it, so at grazing angles they showed through the faces in
front. `flatten --facing X Y Z` writes every gaussian whose surface faces
away from the point transparent (a thin wall is kept).

### A plate: an image over the frame, mixed by its alpha

A camera image keyed and put into the set, so that what stands nearer than
it is in front and the set shows through where it was green, was a
UsdPreviewSurface emitting its texture: the whole frame evaluated as a
material (11 ms on the RTX 3070), and its alpha either a cut-out -- a hard,
stepped edge -- or a coverage the raster resolves by a lot a pixel, which
draws half a coverage as every other pixel. Neither is a key's edge.

A mesh with `primvars:athenea:plate` (1 straight alpha, 2 premultiplied) is
no longer drawn with the meshes. After the frame is finished -- splats,
domes, exposure -- `plate_composite.slang` finds its pixels by a ray against
its triangles in view space, and where the mesh layer's depth is farther or
empty it lays the first texture of the plate's material over the frame by its
alpha. One texture read a pixel: 0.28 ms over a whole 1920 x 1080 frame on
the RTX 3070.

**Checked**: a room under a dome, a plate in front of the camera whose
texture is keyed out in its left third, a ramp of alpha in the middle third
and opaque in the right, a cube behind the plate and one in front of it: the
room and the cube behind show through the keyed third and mix along the
ramp, and the cube in front stays in front.

**Not done**: splats keep no depth, so a plate covers a cloud wherever it
stands in front of the meshes; the path tracer's frame and the AOVs know
nothing of plates; an instanced plate is not drawn.

### An unlit surface: a lightmap shown as it was baked

A set lit once by the path tracer and played back in raster keeps its light
in textures over a second set of texture coordinates. Shown through its
material, such a surface paid a material's evaluation a pixel (11 ms at
1080p on the RTX 3070 for a textured wall) and was lit a second time by the
frame's domes. A mesh with `primvars:athenea:unlit` is instead drawn as any
mesh -- the visibility pass sees it, it occludes and is occluded -- and its
pixels are shaded by `shadeUnlit` alone: the first texture of its material
(`unlitRows`, a pair of words a material row) at `st_lightmap`, else `st`. The
other shading kernels and the table step aside for its instance flag (bit 1),
and it clears the domes' G-buffer under it so `dome_shade` adds nothing.

Measured on the M5 Pro, `ATHENEA_STAGES=1`, a room under a dome behind an
unlit wall covering the whole 1920 x 1080 frame: shading 2.2 ms with the
shading kernel's pass over the same pixels, which returns at once.

Measured on the RTX 3070 (CUDA, Nsight Compute), 1920 x 1080, an unlit
floor across half the frame: `shadeUnlit` 0.22 ms.

The texture is read with a footprint. Read at level 0 alone, a 4k lightmap's
fine baked detail -- slats, a grille -- seen from across the set came out as
speckle and moire. The footprint is the one a material's texture read takes
(`primvarFootprint`, material_surface.slang): the neighbouring pixels' rays
met on the triangle's plane, carried through the lightmap coordinates of its
corners. Not the quad's differences (`atheneaDdx`): a lightmap atlas is cut
into islands, and a quad that straddles a seam or a silhouette -- the other
lane on another island, another mesh, or nothing -- would ask for a level
the size of the jump and smear every seam. Every texture file is given a
full mip chain when it is loaded, EXR included (`TextureStore`, `MipGenerator`),
and the sampler filters between levels. Checked by a checker of single texels
seen at about six texels a pixel against a texture of its average grey, max
difference within 2 code values, and the same checker magnified, which is
still the checker.

**Not done**: the material's other nodes (a scale, a bias) are not applied;
a level is a box average over the atlas, so far enough away an island's
margin -- the dilated light around it -- bleeds into its edge.

A frame whose every mesh is unlit is `shadeUnlit`'s alone. A set lit once and
played back from its lightmaps still paid the lit kernels a frame -- they ran
over every pixel to find each one flagged unlit and step aside: on the M5 Pro,
1920 x 1080, lobe directions 6.5 ms, shadow rays 1.5, the shading kernel 1.7
and the prefiltered domes 0.8, for nothing drawn. The engine says whether any
mesh it draws is lit (`MaterialFrame::lit`); where none is, `shade` runs no
lobe, shadow ray, table, shading or dome kernel, whatever lights the stage
has, and `shadeUnlit` (`unlitAlone`) writes what the shading kernel wrote
where it found no surface or one not unlit: no colour, depth 0, the light
groups at 0 and the domes' G-buffer cleared, which the reflections read. A
lit mesh anywhere in the frame, even where no pixel sees it, keeps every
kernel as before. Checked by an unlit square seen alone and with a lit square
behind the camera, under a dome and without, with screen-space reflections
and without: the four pairs of frames are equal to the bit.

| stage (M5 Pro, 1920x1080, `--no-readback`, median of 199) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| set A, lightmapped, still | 15.99 ms | 3.84 ms |
| set A, lightmapped, moving (`--drift 0.01`) | 16.29 ms | 5.36 ms |

`ATHENEA_STAGES` on the same frame: lobes 9.3-10.1 ms, shadow rays 1.5, domes
0.4-0.5 before and 0 after; shading 1.2 before, 0.9-1.2 after (`shadeUnlit`
alone, the footprint included); the mesh layer 15.7-16.8 ms before and 5.2-6.3
after. The frame differs from before by the footprint alone: a mean absolute
difference of 0.0012 over the frame.

### Screen-space reflections

A floor that shines in a set lit by a lightmap reflects nothing of the set:
the lightmap holds no direction, and the prefiltered dome is the sky. With
`athenea:screenSpaceReflections`, `shadeReflections` runs after the shading
and the domes: from a copy of the colour (no pixel reads what another is
writing), each pixel that reflects marches its mirror direction in view
space -- 48 steps spaced as the square of their index out to 12 units, then
six of bisection between the last step in front and the first behind a
surface less than 0.25 deep -- and adds the colour found there, weighed by
Schlick's Fresnel from the unlit surface's `athenea:reflectance` (or the
glossy albedo the domes' G-buffer holds for a shaded one), faded by
roughness to nothing at 0.6, by the screen's last tenth and by the distance.

Measured on the RTX 3070 (CUDA, Nsight Compute), 1920 x 1080, a room with an
unlit floor of reflectance 0.5 and roughness 0.05 and a cube on it:
`shadeReflections` 0.98 ms, the colour's copy beside it.

**Not done**: no blur for roughness (it fades instead); no temporal
accumulation; the march's steps show as bands where it grazes a wall; splats
and what lies off screen are not reflected.

### A lightmap: the path tracer's light over a second set of coordinates

`athenea lightmap` bakes a set's light where the unlit surface shows it. On
the device: a thread a triangle walks the texels its `st_lightmap`
coordinates cover in its atlas (`userProperties:lightmap_atlas`), claims each
one by a compare-and-swap (half a texel of slack along the edges, so an
island's border is its own), and leaves the point, the facing and a texel's
width on the surface; the claimed texels are scanned into the path tracer's
bake rays -- three float4 a point, as `mesh2splat`'s -- and baked at degree 0
by `StageRenderer::bakePointsOnDevice`, each sample spread over the texel's
footprint; the answer, `0.5 + Y0 c` in linear light, goes back into its
texel, and eight rings of dilation carry each island's light into the margin
the packer left. A stage beside the atlases sublayers the source and makes
every baked mesh unlit, bound to a material that reads its atlas at
`st_lightmap`.

Measured on the M5 Pro (Metal), the first virtual set (37 meshes, one
atlas): at 256 x 256, 48567 texels of 65536 claimed, 16 paths each, 3
bounces, baked in 25.0 s; the stage then drew at 1063 x 525 in 15.8 ms a
frame. At 16 paths a texel the light is grain.

Then adaptive and denoised: the bake is `bakeSplitOnDevice` -- a first pass
at every texel and passes of `--pass-samples` where the relative variance
for the cost is highest -- and the atlas goes through the engine's OIDN in
lightmap space, guided by the albedo the bake reads back (one path, the
material planes) and the texel's normal, every plane grown into the margins
first and the light grown again from the claimed texels after. At 1024 x
1024, 761016 texels, 32 paths and 32 more on average in 10 passes: 63.4 s
for the bake, 0.47 s for the denoiser, and the floor's grain and the panels'
edges come out clean. At that rate -- 0.77 million paths a second -- a
4096 x 4096 atlas of the same coverage at 64 paths a texel is about 17
minutes.

A camera that only turns about one point -- a PTZ on its head -- sees each
texel from one direction, so a lightmap for it can hold the whole radiance
and not the diffuse alone: `--bake-toward X Y Z` hands the bake the point
(`BakeOptions::toward`, the path `mesh2splat --bake-toward` takes), and a
texel facing it is baked as seen from there, the polish and what it
reflects included. A floor so baked shows its sheen with no reflection pass
and is wrong from anywhere else.

**Not done**: the bake is degree 0, so nothing of the light depends on the view; an
instanced mesh and a GeomSubset's binding are left as they are; on CUDA the
bake's pipeline is not made (an OptiX failure the other bakes share).

### Measured (M5 Pro, release, 1920 x 1080, `athenea stage --frames 20`)

The whole TX Corvette on its mesh ground, the camera of the stage, against
the path traced frame (`athenea_rt512.exr`, 512 paths). The ground's error
is over a mask of where the ground changes the frame (52% of it), the mean
absolute difference over the GT's mean, at full size and boxed down by four
(which takes most of the GT's own grain out):

| | median a frame | mesh layer | under the car (GT 0.182) | the bumper's contact (GT 0.043) | open ground (GT 0.217) | ground error, full / quarter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (sampled, a map a frame) | 637 ms | ~480 | 0.160, std 0.50 | 0.027 | 0.220, std 0.60 | 106% / 50% |
| prefiltered, in the shading kernel | 535 ms | 345 | rows of garbage | | | |
| its own kernel | 537 ms | 348 | 0.170 | 0.023 | 0.223, std 0.0001 | |
| the map cached, no rays | 352 ms | 163 | 0.170 | 0.023 | 0.223 | |
| the material from a table | 200 ms | 11 | 0.188 | 0.075 | 0.213 | 12% / 5.5% |
| the penumbra from the farthest caster | **201 ms** | **11.2** | **0.182** | **0.041** | **0.215** | |
| the car alone, no ground | 156 ms | | | | | |

The mesh layer's 11 ms: visibility 1.7, the shading kernel and the table
1.6, the domes 5.0 -- the six soft reads -- and its preparation 1.8. The
splat blend still costs 30 ms more over the ground than without it (55
against 25): the composite variant of the blend, not looked into.

Under the bumper the contact shadow went from 0.075 to 0.041: measured from
the nearest caster -- seen from the sky, the roof -- every point under the
car was a metre from its blocker and the shadow went as soft as the rest.
The map keeps the farthest caster's depth too now (one word more a texel, an
atomic maximum), and the penumbra is measured from it.

**Checked**: a grey floor under a plain dome reads 0.5000 prefiltered and
0.4998 sampled at 64 a pixel; a slab of gaussians over a floor under a dome
darkens it to 0.132 from 0.800 (the test's patch was reading the horizon
past the slab, and was aimed under it); `[shadowmap]` with the farthest
depth. The two tests about the raster's dome samples (their convergence
through glass, a lobe's shadow under a plate) sample the dome, which they
measure.

## The ground's shadow as gaussians: a shadow catcher (task PLAY-G)

The direction for the ground: its shadows become gaussians, drawn in the same
raster as the car, and the geometric plane stays only as something to
compare against. A catcher is a layer of gaussians lying on the ground under
and around the object, drawn black, each covering what the object takes of
the light reaching it -- so it darkens whatever is behind it: the sky's own
floor, a backplate, a mesh.

### Where it stands, and what it knows

`athenea mesh2splat STAGE --prim OBJECT --shadow-catcher` finds the ground
(`usd/ShadowCatcher.h`: the largest mesh outside the object, flat along the
up axis, whose top is at the object's bottom and which reaches under it;
`--catcher-ground` names one), writes a stage that is the source with a
patch on the ground's plane -- the object's footprint widened by
`--catcher-margin` heights (1.5), a grid of quads about 64 cells a side each,
since a conversion walks at most `--max-cells` cells a triangle and two
triangles left a third of the Corvette's patch unsampled -- and converts the
patch alone, at one cell (`--catcher-cell`, a hundredth of the object's
height), as a TX transfer. The object and the ground stay in that stage as
what the bake's rays meet, so each catcher gaussian keeps, independent of
the sky, how much of every direction is open (the cells), the transfer's
direct and bounced halves, and the sun's share by the same bits. The boxes
are the meshes' authored extents (`UsdGeomBBoxCache` with the hint):
metadata, read.

The Corvette's: /World/Ground/Plane found, a 5.9 x 8.3 m patch, 11 x 11
quads, 309 k gaussians at a 1.26 cm cell, baked in 79 s (64 paths, 3
bounces).

### How it is drawn

`primvars:athenea:splat:catcher` reaches `SplatInstance::catcher`, and the
rasteriser projects such a cloud with a kernel of its own,
`splatProjectCatcher` (`projectSplat<kProjectCatcher>`: no relighting, 68
KB of Metal against the TX kernel's 179), beside TX's choice:

- the light that reaches the gaussian with the object there is its transfer
  dotted with the frame's sky plus the sun at its open share and bounce
  (`transferViewless`'s front); with nothing there it would be the sky's
  irradiance at its normal plus the sun's cosine, over pi as the transfer is;
- their ratio is what is left; the gaussian's opacity is -ln(ratio) / 2 pi,
  since a lattice of gaussians sigma = 1 cell wide sums to 2 pi everywhere
  and a layer of opacity a leaves exp(-2 pi a) of what is behind it. (2.4,
  the coverage a converted surface reaches, was the first guess: the
  shadow came out 2.2 to 3 times as deep as the path traced frame's.)
- black, and marked (`kCatcherMark`), so the blend draws it over an opaque
  layer under it even where its centre's depth reads behind that layer: it
  lies on it.

Light the object bounces onto the ground beyond what it takes is not
drawn: a black layer can only take.

### Under another sky: what was wrong, and the gate

The catcher was baked once, under the stage's own sky, and drawn under
goegap (a desert with a sun of 1.2e5) against the path traced mesh car under
goegap. Three things were wrong, none of them the transfer:

- **It cast into the cloud shadow map.** A catcher is a cloud, so it was one
  of the map's casters, and the ground under it received its patch's outline
  along each of the dome's six directions: straight-edged blocks across the
  ground under a sunny sky, a third of the light gone under a soft one (the
  frames with a mesh car read 0.119 under the car for GT's 0.182). A
  catcher casts nothing now.
- **Its ratio was two projections.** The transfer dotted with the sky's
  harmonics, against the harmonics' own irradiance at the normal: two band
  limits that do not cancel, so a ground nothing stood over did not read
  one. Both sides are one quadrature now -- over the cells of the bake's
  open directions, the sky's radiance times the cosine and the cell's solid
  angle, the open cells for one side and every cell above the surface for
  the other, and the extracted sun on both, read through the same bits on
  the first.
- **Drawn over the layer under it everywhere.** A catcher gaussian is drawn
  past the opaque layer's depth only within a percent and a half of it --
  the ground it lies on -- so a mesh car's body is not painted with its own
  shadow.

And the sun: env_sun had taken goegap's as 0.07 of irradiance where it
delivers 5.8 (next section), so its shadow was the harmonics' smear.

| goegap, 960 x 540 | under the car | the sun's contact | open ground |
|---|---|---|---|
| path traced mesh | 0.354 | 0.016 | 0.352 / 0.348 |
| catcher, first draw | 0.320 | 0.032 | 0.328 / 0.342 |
| catcher, all of the above | **0.357** | **0.024** | **0.356 / 0.360** |

**The gate** (`ctest -R catcher_gate`, `tests/regress/catcher_against_gt.cmake`):
the Corvette's catcher baked, the stage's meshes drawn on the raster route
with it (a prefiltered dome traces no ray, so the catcher is the ground's
whole shadow), against a path traced frame of 256 paths at 960 x 540, in
four windows of the ground measured by `athenea compare --window`: under
the car 0.188 against 0.181, the contact 0.030 against 0.042, the open
ground 0.218 against 0.217 and 0.227 against 0.220. Within 10% of the GT
under the car and on the open ground, and 40% at the contact, where the
catcher is still dark: a gap of a few centimetres under the bumper against
a 1.26 cm cell, with the light coming through a wedge at the horizon.

### The contact under the bumper: what the layer composites

The catcher read the bumper's contact 30% dark (0.030 against the path
traced 0.043 at 960 x 540) whatever its cell (1.26 cm and 0.6 cm alike). Read
off the catcher's file on the CPU, its bits were right -- the cosine-weighted
open share under the bumper, row by row, 0.200 / 0.232 / 0.306 of the open
ground's against the path traced 0.184 / 0.209 / 0.277 -- with no noise to
speak of (0.008 between neighbours) and no bounce (0.3%). Under a plain white
dome, where the expected ratio is exactly the bits', the frame drew 15% dark
at the contact: the layer composites the product of (1 - a g), not of
exp(-a g), and the darker the shadow the further the one falls below the
other. The opacity is now read off a lattice simulated the way the blend
composites -- sigma one cell, each term dropped below 1/255 -- and inverted
at eight ratios (`catcherAlphaFor`): under white, 6% dark at the contact
where it was 15%; under the workshop sky the contact crop 0.034 against
0.043 (0.030 before), under the car 0.184 against 0.182.

What is left is the sky's: the workshop's light is a ceiling of lamps, and
the catcher weighs its open cells by a degree-3 sky that cannot place them.
The gate's contact tolerance is 25% now (40%).

### The sky a catcher weighs its cells by, and its faint gaussians

**The sky per cell from the prefiltered map.** The workshop's light is a
ceiling of lamps that a degree-3 sky cannot place, and under the bumper,
where only the horizon is open, the catcher drew its contact 24% dark of the
path traced frame at the first rows. Each open cell is now weighed by the
prepared octahedral map read at a roughness the size of a cell (about 13
degrees) -- which holds the lamps where they are, with no extractor -- and a
cell within the extracted sun's cone takes the harmonics' residual sky, since
the sun is added apart. At 960 x 540 under the workshop sky, rows 410 / 420 /
430 below the bumper read 0.0348 / 0.0417 / 0.0596 against the path traced
0.0399 / 0.0453 / 0.0601 (0.0304 / 0.0376 / 0.0553 with the harmonics), the
contact window 0.038 against 0.043. Under goegap the sun's contact is still
too bright (0.029 against 0.016): its shadow's edge right under the bumper is
read through 16 x 16 cells.

**A faint catcher is thinned, not culled.** Far from the car the shadow is a
few per cent, and at a grazing view the antialias's payment took those
gaussians under the 1/255 the cull and the blend drop: the open ground under
a white dome read 5% bright (0.249 against 0.236). A catcher gaussian under
kCatcherFloor (0.03) is drawn at it by a lot -- a hash of its index -- with
probability its opacity over that, the same coverage in the mean: 0.2386
against 0.2361.

**A catcher's open directions on a 32 x 32 grid.** Under goegap's sun the
contact under the bumper read 0.029 against the path traced 0.016: the sun's
shadow edge there is narrower than a 16 x 16 cell (11 degrees), and its
share is read through four of them. On 32 x 32 (5.6 degrees, 1024 bits a
gaussian) it reads 0.021, the workshop sky unchanged (0.038 against 0.043),
so `--shadow-catcher` takes 32 unless told. Weighing the four cells nearer
than bilinearly (a smoothstep on the fractions) was tried and left out: rows
430 and 440 came closer, the contact window went the other way (0.023).

## Playing the TX car: where it stands, and the order of what is left (task PLAY, 24 Oct)

The goal is the TX Corvette in raster at an interactive rate, its ground
gaussians as well (a shadow catcher, not a mesh plane). The first figures, at
1920 x 1080 on the M5 Pro: the car alone 168 ms a frame, on its mesh ground
646 ms, 3.1 GB of transfer.

### What is in, and from where

- **The ground** (PLAY-G, above): the prefiltered dome, the cloud map built
  when what it shows changes, the uniform material from a table -- the mesh
  ground from 637 to 201 ms -- and then the ground's shadow as gaussians:
  `--shadow-catcher`, its gate, and `--light-catcher` for the lamps' light.
- **Three catcher changes that stayed on `play-ground`** -- the opacity
  composited as the blend composites, the sky per cell from the prefiltered
  map with the faint gaussians thinned, the 32 x 32 grid -- are merged here.
  This branch reads the cells, the sky and the sun in the cloud's frame (a
  turned stage), so the map along a cell is turned back into the world
  (`transferBack`) before it is read.
- `txf` carries the catcher into `athenea flatten`; TXF is out of the plan
  and that branch is not merged.

### Where a frame goes

| | median a frame |
|---|---|
| the car alone, before the view-independent terms were kept | 158 ms: projection 84.5 (the field and its coupling 24, the cells the lobes read 16.5, the sun's share and bounce 12, the body's transfer 7.5), the two sorts 30, the blend 25 |
| the car on its mesh ground, the ground's four changes | 201 ms (mesh layer 11; the blend 30 more than without a ground) |
| the car and its catcher, no mesh | 147 ms |

The view-independent terms (`transferViewless`) are kept since; the profile
after them has not been taken. The car's frame is the projection's first.

### What the catcher still lacks

1. **Lights that are not the first dome.** A distant light, a sphere or a
   rect cast nothing on the catcher: `catcherOpacity` read the first dome and
   its extracted sun, and a stage without a dome drew no shadow at all. Done
   below, with the thinning of faint gaussians narrowed.
2. **Its patch is the object's footprint and 1.5 heights round it.** A sun
   lower than about 34 degrees throws a shadow past it, which ends at the
   patch's edge. A ring of coarser cells now reaches 3 heights (below).
3. **Light the object bounces onto the ground** (a ratio over one) is not
   drawn: a black layer only takes (LIGHT4).
4. **Its one check on a real asset is the Corvette gate**, a conversion,
   which is not run since 14 Oct; the synthetic test below is the check that
   runs.
5. **Each open cell is one hard shadow**, so a lamp's soft lobe is drawn as
   overlapping discs a few tenths of a per cent deep: a filter of the
   catcher's share on its own plane, at the bake, is the candidate.
6. **A sun's shadow is as soft as a cell** (5.6 degrees for a 0.53 degree
   sun): finer cells, or a sun term of its own, would sharpen it.
7. **A cheaper sky for the sharp lobes** (one level instead of two, 9 ms of the
   blend before the offset in closed form) changes the image, so it waits on
   what judges it: a path traced Corvette at 1920 x 1080 from three views with
   Cryptomatte masks, measured per material (chrome, paint, glass; the glass
   by per-class means and mean-matched smoothed relMSE). Not rendered on the
   shared Mac.

### The order

1. The catcher: other lights (below), then the patch's reach.
2. The frame's cost: `ATHENEA_STAGES` medians on the TX car cloud kept
   locally (no conversion), the projection first, then the blend's composite
   variant over an opaque layer.
3. Compression (proposal 034): the coverage mips rebuilt from the bits when
   a cloud is read (70% of the transfer, no loss), then the indirect
   harmonics quantised after a fixed rotation; each measured against the
   uncompressed frame.
4. Levels of detail: the cut by screen error each frame, carrying the
   transfer, within a resident budget.

### Every light of the frame on the catcher

`catcherOpacity` weighed the first dome and the sun `env_sun` took out of
it, and returned nothing without a dome: a stage lit by a distant light, a
sphere or a rect drew no shadow on its catcher. Every other light of the
frame now goes into both sides of the ratio as a TX gaussian reads it: one
sample at the gaussian (`sampleLight`), its irradiance at the cosine, and on
the side with the object the share of the cone it subtends that the cells
leave open (`splatConeOpen`, held to a cell at least). A light that casts no
shadow is open; one not linked to the cloud is left out. A frame with no
light at all leaves the catcher out.

### A faint catcher drawn whole, and its share kept

**The grain was the thinning.** The frames above, divided by the frames
without the catcher and amplified ten times, showed dots across the whole
patch where the path traced ratio is smooth: catcher gaussians drawn by a lot
at a floor opacity (0.03 as merged, 4/255 after). Read at the pawn's scale,
two pixels a gaussian, a lot of dots does not average out. What the thinning
answered -- a faint gaussian under the 1/255 the projection and the blend cut
at, whose faint shadow went -- is answered without it: a catcher is not cut
at 1/255, neither in the projection (`kCatcherLeast`, 1e-5) nor in the blend
(`kCatcherMark`), and is drawn out to three sigmas at `paid * alpha`, with
nothing paid back. Its opacity table (`catcherAlphaFor`) is read off the
lattice composited that way, nothing dropped: faint, it is -ln(ratio) / 2 pi
(0.0082 at 0.95, where the table that modelled the 1/255 drop read 0.0121).

**The share is kept.** What a catcher gaussian takes depends on the lights,
not on the eye. `splatCatcherViewless` writes it, at an opacity of one, a
gaussian each into the rasteriser's TX cache, under the same key (the
lights' revision, the cloud, its place) and the cloud's light categories;
the projection multiplies its own opacity by it. A catcher keeps it under
any lights, a distant light alone included.

**Checked** (`[catcher]`, the faint case against the backdrop scaled by its
mean, as radiance):

### A ring for the long shadows, and the TX car's frame

**The ring** (`--catcher-reach`, 3 heights). Past the patch's 1.5 heights,
`usd/ShadowCatcher` writes a second mesh, `Ring`: four strips round the patch
out to 3 heights from the footprint, held to the ground, and the catcher is
the Xform with both. The conversion takes each mesh's cell as its longest
side over one resolution, held between the patch's cell and the ring's, so
the resolution is the ring's box over its cell and the patch keeps its own;
the ring's cell is twice the patch's, or less where the patch's longest side
would not keep its own. The pawn: 132 k gaussians on the patch at 0.66 mm,
92 k on the ring at 1.21 mm (1.83 times, held by the boxes), baked together
in 10 s. Under the workshop sky the lamps' lobes reach past the patch's edge,
which no longer shows as a square; the open-ground window reads 0.9970
of the light against the path traced 0.9970. A light lower than about 18
degrees still throws a shadow past the ring.

**The TX car's frame.** The car cloud kept here (`base_tx.usdc`, 5.38 M
gaussians, 8 Oct; no conversion), alone under the scene's dome from
/World/Camera at 1920 x 1080, `ATHENEA_STAGES` medians over 19 frames, the
same on h1eprod-aa's build and this one (no catcher in it):

| stage | median |
|---|---|
| project (the view-independent terms kept) | 29.9 ms |
| counts | 2.2 |
| depth sort | 6.5 |
| emit | 4.0 |
| tile sort (11.8 M pairs) | 8.2 |
| blend | 31.1 |
| frame | 95.8 ms (95.1 on h1eprod-aa) |

The projection and the blend are two thirds of it, a third each; the sorts
and the emit 21 ms. The 158 ms of the first profile were the 14.7 M car;
per million gaussians this is 17.8 ms a frame against its 10.7, the stage
timer's own waits included.

### Where the TX car's frame goes, priced part by part

The car cloud kept here (`base_tx.usdc`, 5.38 M gaussians), alone under the
scene's dome at 1920 x 1080, `ATHENEA_STAGES` medians of 19 frames. Each
part was priced by a shader variant that switches it off (the image then
differs; the variants are measurements, not changes), alternated with the
unchanged shaders in the same run:

| switched off | project | blend | frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| nothing | 29.8 ms | 30.7 ms | 96 ms |
| the shading (the albedo drawn) | 4.6 | 15.1 | 55 |
| the curvature (no slope, no sharp lobe) | 20.6 | 14.3 | 70 |
| the per-pixel lobes in the blend | 29.9 | 14.1 | 79 |
| the reflected field | 23.0 | 30.6 | 91 |

So the projection is 4.6 ms of geometry and 25 of shading, and half the
blend is the sharp lobes it reads per pixel; the sorts (6.5 + 8.3 ms), the
emit (3.9) and the counts (2.2) are the rest. After the two changes below,
the sharp lobes priced again: the polish's sky 8.6 ms, the coat's 3.4, the
sun through them 0.4; the reflected field 6.7 ms of projection, the slope's
two extra sky reads 1.3.

**A level's first texel found once.** `envTexelAt` found every texel's
address by walking the levels below it (`envLevelOffset`) and the domes'
size (`envTexelsPerDome`), sixteen steps a texel, and a bilinear read of two
levels is eight texels. `envLevelAt` finds the level's first texel once and
reads its four from there (`envWordsAt`): the same words.

**What an opaque gaussian weighs by nothing is not computed.** The sky
behind a gaussian and its far face's reflection are multiplied by its
transmitted weight; where that is zero -- all of the car but its glass --
neither is read now.

| | project | blend | frame | against the last commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the last commit | 29.8 ms | 31.0 ms | 97.5 ms | |
| a level's texel found once | 24.0 | 28.2 | 89.1 | relMSE 0, p99 0, max 0 |
| and an opaque gaussian's behind skipped | 22.5 | 28.4 | 86.2 | relMSE 0, p99 0, max 0 |

The images are identical to the bit (`athenea compare`, the whole frame:
`car/frame_before_after.png`, `car/frame_diff_x100.png`).

Tried and left out, the image identical and the time not:
- the blend's group memory at 32 bytes a record (the record's colour, a
  surfel's disc and a slope read from memory where a record covers the
  pixel): 21 KB to 9 KB a group, 30.9 ms against 30.7;
- a sharp record's polish loaded with the batch rather than read at every
  pixel: 28.5 / 28.8 against 28.0 / 28.3.

What is left is arithmetic: two bilinear reads of two levels of the sky at
every pixel a sharp record covers, and the shading's 18 ms.

**A level's offset in closed form.** Priced again by switching parts of the
sky read off in the blend: one level instead of two, 28.4 -> 19.3 ms; the
texel reads replaced by arithmetic, 26.9; the texel's address replaced by a
constant, 19.9. The address was the cost: `envLevelOffset` walked the levels
below the one read, at every bilinear read. Where the base is a power of two
-- every map `Environment` prepares -- the levels above the floor halve, and
their squares sum to (4^(b+1) - 4^(b-m+1)) / 3; the walk stays for any other
base. The two agree for every base from 1 to 32768 and every level.

| | project | blend | frame | against the last commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the last commit | 22.5 ms | 28.3 ms | 86.8 ms | |
| the offset in closed form | 21.4 | 25.3 | 80.9 | relMSE 0, p99 0, max 0 |

What the constant address saved beyond that (a further 5 ms) is the texels
all falling in one place, which a real lookup cannot have.

**Shading only the gaussians the blend reaches** would be exact: whether a
pixel reaches a record depends on the opacities before it, never on a
colour, so a walk with the geometry alone finds exactly the records the
frame's blend weighs. A probe (the blend's own contribution count, not kept)
counted them: 873 k of the 5.38 M from the scene's camera, 842 k from behind
on the other side, 508 k from the side -- 9 to 16%. Shading those alone would
save about 15 of the projection's 17 ms of shading, but finding them is a
second walk of every pixel through its tile's records, the blend without its
colours: 13.9 ms. The two cancel on this car; it is not built.

The sorts run at the tiled radix route's own rate (12.4 ms for four passes
over ten million pairs, above): the depth sort is three passes of 8 bits over
the 5.3 M visible (6.5 ms), the tile sort two over 11.8 M pairs whose 13 bits
of tile already take the fewest passes (8.3 ms). The pairs are counted with
the blend's own test, so there are none to drop without changing the frame.

### Compression (proposal 034) and levels of detail: what applies

**034's first step does not apply.** Its lossless saving -- rebuild the
coverage mips from the bits at load instead of storing them, 70% of the
transfer it priced -- is against the layout of proposals 028-032, which kept
341 f16 mip values a gaussian beside the bits. The engine never stored them:
a TX gaussian carries its bits and its harmonics, and every reader takes the
bits directly (`splatCellsOpen`, `splatConeOpen`). There is nothing to
rebuild. What the TX car is made of (`base_tx.usdc`, 5 380 804 gaussians,
3.0 GB; 16 x 16 cells):

| block | in the file (float32, int32) | on the device |
|---|---|---|
| transfer: direct 16, indirect 48, reflected field 48 | 448 B | 224 B (halves) |
| open directions, 256 bits | 32 B | 32 B |
| position, orientation, scales, opacity, colour | 44 B and up | 36 B |
| material and layers (metallic ... sheen, specular, coat) | ~92 B | 12-24 B |
| normal, curvature, Cryptomatte id | 28 B | 20 B |

The transfer is two thirds of the device's bytes and four fifths of the
file's. The file's floats are halves on the device already, so writing them
as halves would halve the file losslessly against what is drawn; that is a
format change, and on-disk coding is the `.athz` work's (pages a GPU decodes,
transfer transforms, branch `athz`). The first frame of the car takes 10 to
15 s, the stage read, the upload and the kernels' compilation together.

**Levels of detail.** A `.athc` carries a TX transfer (bit 5), the material
and the layers, and `LodBuilder` merges them (the transfer averaged, the bits
by majority); the cut and the streaming pool draw it. What is missing for the
TX car: no command writes a `.athc` from a USD ParticleField (`athenea convert`
reads splat files, `mesh2splat -o x.athc` refuses `--transfer`), and a `.athc`
keeps no curvature, so its sharp lobes would be drawn flat. (Both done below: `athenea convert` reads a USD field, and bit 6 keeps the
curvature.) The `.athz` pages
hold the same record as a pool slot, transfer included (layer T), so the two
lines meet in that record.

### The TX car's levels of detail: a `.athc` from its USD, measured

**A USD ParticleField into a `.athc`** (`athenea convert cloud.usdc out.athc`,
`usd::uploadParticleField`): the field read with every array hdAthenea's
ParticleField reads, uploaded as a frame uploads it, its levels built and
written. It repacks, it converts nothing. The car: 3.0 GB of `.usdc` into
2.6 GB of `.athc` in 11 minutes, most of it reading and writing the file.

**Curvature in the levels and the file** (bit 6): one word a gaussian,
`packCurvature` -- three bytes of a sign and 7 bits of log2 over the 16
octaves under the fourth byte's top octave, half a step 4.5% -- what
`.athz`'s geometry layer can carry the same way. A merged group of more than
one is flat: a member's shape operator is in that member's axes. Checked by
`athenea_lod_tests "[athc]"`: 196 608 components from 1e-3 to 1e4, both signs,
all back within half a step or flat; a curvature through the levels and a
`.athc` and back.

**A streamed cloud is drawn as its prim asks.** The cut's instances carried
the clouds and nothing of the prim: a streamed TX car drew its albedo, unlit.
They now take the prim's relight, lit body, light categories, index and
catcher flags, and the frame's transfer and reflection settings. And a cut
gathered anew counts its cloud's revision up, so terms kept for the last
cut's gaussians (a TX cloud's view-independent ones) are not read for this
one's.

**Measured** (1920 x 1080, medians of 11 frames, against the full cloud from
its USD, `athenea compare`):

| view | threshold | gaussians drawn | frame | 8-bit p99 / max | relMSE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| scene camera | full | 5.38 M | 80.6 ms | | |
| | 1 px | 5.38 M | 114.0 | 1 / 41 | 9e-6 |
| | 2 px | 2.02 M | 61.9 | 45 / 239 | 0.35 |
| | 4 px | 0.86 M | 40.4 | 102 / 248 | 2.6 |
| rear | full | 5.38 M | 85.7 | | |

At 1 px the cut is the whole cloud (no group spans a pixel at 1920 x 1080):
the image is the full one but for the packed curvature (p99 1), and the frame
a third slower -- every frame gathers every drawn gaussian's 330 bytes into
the cut's own cloud, two thirds of it the transfer. At 2 px the merged groups
show: rings across the doors and the bonnet where a sharp lobe reads a
group's averaged normal, white patches at the headlamps and the sills; at 4 px
the glass is a lattice (`car/lod_*_thresholds.png`). What is next:

- the cut gathered again only where it changed, and the payload read from the
  store through the cut's indices rather than copied;
- a merged group of a TX cloud that does not mix what faces apart (the
  normals averaged across a panel's two faces), and glass and sheets kept
  out of merges or merged as sheets;
- then the threshold the car can play at, against the path trace.

### A cut that reads its payload where it is, and merges that keep apart what faces apart

**The payload stays where the levels keep it.** A `.athc` read whole has its
store's extras and every level's joined into one buffer each (`joinPayload`:
the store first, level k's group g at `payloadBase[k] + g`). A cut gathers
positions, shapes, harmonics, normals and emission, 44 bytes a gaussian, and
writes for each where its material, layers, ids, transfer, open directions
and curvature are (`GpuSplats::payloadIndex`, `lodPayloadIndex`); the
projection reads them there (`payloadOf`, `params.payloadIndexed`), the TX
cache too, at that index. And a cut whose counts and selection are the last
one's (`lodSelectionChanged`) is not gathered at all: its cloud keeps its
revision, and what was kept of it. Checked by `athenea_lod_tests "[athc]"`: a
cut read through its index is word for word the cut gathered -- a material,
a transfer, its open directions and a curvature different for every gaussian
-- at a threshold that draws splats and one that draws merged groups; and the
same cut again keeps its revision. On the car the images are the gathered
cut's to the bit.

**Merges that do not spoil.** A TX cloud's levels sort a class above the
Morton code (`lod_class.slang`, 33-bit keys) and a level's group holds one:
the axis the shading normal leans most along and its sign, so a panel's two
faces are never averaged into one normal -- the rings across the doors -- and
glass and sheets (`lodKeptApart`: transmission over a half, or a thin wall
that transmits), which the cut never draws merged (`params.pbrs`). Both read
from the cloud. Checked: splats at the same places facing +z and -z give no
merged normal under 0.9 along z at any level; the same cloud all glass, cut
with every cell under the threshold, draws every splat and no group.

**Measured** (1920 x 1080, medians of 11 frames; against the full cloud from
its USD; the file 2.86 GB, its more numerous groups):

| view | threshold | gaussians | frame | p99 / max | relMSE | before (gathered, unclassed) |

| scene camera | full | 5.38 M | 81.8 ms | | | 80.6 ms |
| | 1 px | 5.38 M | 87.2 | 1 / 41 | 9e-6 | 114.0 ms |

| | 4 px | 1.41 M | 41.9 | 42 / 185 | 0.0136 | 40.4 ms, p99 102, 2.6 |
| rear | full | 5.38 M | 86.1 | | | 85.7 |
| | 1 px | 5.38 M | 92.8 | 1 / 21 | 8e-6 | 118.0 |
| | 2 px | 2.91 M | 66.7 | 18 / 203 | 0.0036 | 70.5, 39, 0.12 |
| | 4 px | 1.47 M | 46.8 | 36 / 238 | 0.0084 | 46.5, 63, 0.22 |

The payload index alone, on the unclassed file: 1 px 90.0 / 94.3 / 79.0 ms,
2 px 46.3 / 60.6 / 56.4, 4 px 33.2 / 38.7 / 38.1, the images the gathered
cut's. At 1 px the cut still costs 5 to 9 ms over the full cloud: the cut's
kernels and its two waits for counts. At 4 px the doors are softer and grained
where groups of one side's splats meet (`car/lod_*_thresholds_classed.png`).
Which threshold the car plays at is for the path trace to say, per material;
that reference is blocked (above).

### A merge tree read as its leaves

The Corvette v8.2b master (`car5120`, 25 panels) is kept as merge trees
(`athenea decimate --tree --tree-pages`): each panel's leaves and every merge
over them, in page order, `lodTree` set. Drawn or repacked whole, the merges
would stand over their leaves. `usd::uploadParticleField` (and so `athenea
convert x.usdc y.athc`) keeps a tree's leaves alone: the gaussians whose
`lodSize` is 1, marked and compacted on the device (`usd/tree_leaves.slang`,
a prefix sum and a gather of every buffer the cloud carries), the CPU reading
the count. Checked by `athenea_usd_tests "[tree]"`: six leaves and two merges
written far from them give six gaussians, none far, their transfer kept. The
bonnet's panel (`car_pan5120_5a.usdc`, 6 267 263 gaussians): 3 133 783 leaves,
the count its tree's log gives, into a 1.09 GB `.athc` in 434 s, 1.9 GB of
memory at most. The whole master is about 69 M leaves, some 23 GB on the
device at a TX gaussian's 330 bytes: more than this Mac's GPU holds at once.

### The whole car streamed: merges that cover, one store, a cut that does not wait (25 Oct)

**A merge keeps its members' mass.** The coarse levels of a `.athc` are built
from moments (`lod_finalize`), and a merge's opacity was its members' mass
over its own area held under 0.99. A cell of a converted surface is covered
two to eight times over by its members, so the cap dropped most of it, and a
single gaussian at 0.99 falls off towards its cell's edges: on a grid of merges
about 3.5 sigma apart, half way between two of them the frame showed about 40%
of what was behind. Wherever a region's chunks were not on the device, the
finest merged level drew the car see-through and grey, in rectangles that were
the chunks' Morton runs. The cap is now `LodBuildSettings::mostMergedOpacity`,
5 by default (`athenea convert --merged-opacity`): over 1 the merge is Spark's
harder kernel (`falloffAlpha`), flat to about its cell's edge. On a floor of
discs as wide as their spacing, ten to a cell, with no chunk on the device, the
merges held under one differ from the floor by p99 166 and keep their mass by
p99 0 (`athenea_lod_tests "a region whose chunks*"`). The cost is in volumes:
on the random cloud of "far away, a dense cloud...", whose members lie behind
each other and whose summed mass is more than their union, p99 at 2 and 4 px
goes from 9 and 29 to 14 and 41. The car's 25 panels were converted again
(`--max-group-fraction 0.1`, 24.1 GB, about 80 minutes).

**Glass not on the device draws nothing, and comes first.** A glass group
whose chunks were missing drew its merge, which is no glass: black blocks over
the cabin at 1 px, the whole windscreen black at 4 px. The finest level now
selects nothing for it, and its chunks are wanted as a cell four times the
threshold is (`lodChunkNeeds`), ahead of what a merge stands in for. From the
camera the windscreen then draws the same at 1 and 4 px, its own splats at
both (`f01m/glass2/cam_1_4_crop.png`).

**One store for every streamed prim** (`lod::StreamingShare`). A pool opened
with a share takes no store of its own; the first cut that asks for a cloud
lays one out for all of them -- slots for the sum of their budgets, the payload
joined with every pool's levels after the slots -- and each frame the share's
update gives its slots to the chunks most wanted, whichever prim's they are,
evicting the least wanted as one pool did. The engine opens every streamed
prim into one share; a file with another chunk size or other payloads keeps a
store of its own. Two copies of a cloud, one thirty units behind the other,
each with the 8 slots that alone left chunks missing: the near one takes 13 of
the 16, the far one none (`athenea_lod_tests "a .athc reads back*"`).

**A frame that changes nothing waits for nothing.** The cut's kernels for every
instance go in one batch with one read of all counts; cuts whose counts are
the last frame's compare their selections in a second batch, one counter a
cut; changed cuts are gathered in a third that is not waited for. A call with
the same view over clouds whose residency is unchanged returns the last cut
without touching the device. A cloud's residency starts at a number no other
cloud of the process started at, and a cut regathers when it changed: a cloud
made where a freed one stood was taken for it, and a slot that took another
chunk kept the old one's gaussians. The steady frame's cut makes no host wait
(the test counts `Device::syncs()`; the car below logs none from `lod/` in its
last frame, `ATHENEA_SYNC_TRACE`).

The whole car (`car5120`, f01m, the stage's 25 x 262 144 splats in one store)
from three views, 1920 x 1080, 8 frames. The GPU was shared with another
session's jobs, and the medians are not comparable between runs: the fastest
frame is given beside them. 2 and 4 px against 1 px, which the budget caps.

| view | px | median / fastest ms | drawn | cut waits | p99 / relMSE vs 1 px |

| cam | 1 | 1426 / 805 | 10.60 M | 0 | -- |
| cam | 2 | 2150 / 1328 | 10.06 M | 0 | 0 / 9e-14 |
| cam | 4 | 751 / 526 | 7.62 M | 0 | 75 / 0.12 |
| rear | 1 | 701 / 323 | 10.51 M | 0 | -- |

and both draw what it holds. Most of 4 px's difference in this table is the
windscreen, which 4 px then drew as a black merge (measured before the glass
change above), and the merges' harder kernel streaking the paint's reflections
where they are drawn over many pixels. The 1 px frame leaves about
1.8 GB of this Mac's memory free.

Not done: the glass change is seen from the camera only, and the table is not
measured again with it; merges keep their
mass but not their members' reflections, which a merge of a curved panel
spreads; and the budget is still the sum of the prims' budgets rather than a
share of the device.

## The sun is the texels that are it

env_sun found a dome's sun on a grid of 1.8 degree cells, measured its
profile in two degree rings and then summed it on the projection's texels
within the ring it ended at: on goegap the sun is sharper than the rings,
and its irradiance came out 0.07 (1%) of the 5.8 it delivers, the rest left
in nine harmonics that cannot hold a disc. Now the sun is the texels that
are it, on the level the harmonics are projected from (`sunRegionOf`): a
sky has one where its brightest texel is over 32 times its median (a
histogram of log luminance over the projection's own measure, which the sun
cannot drag as it drags a mean), and its texels are those over 16 times the
median and 2% of the peak, within ten degrees of the peak. The irradiance
is their radiance times their solid angle in the projection's quadrature,
the direction their luminance's centroid, and `env_project` skips the same
texels by the same test (`sunHolds`): what leaves the harmonics is what
arrives as the light. The buffer keeps its stride: (direction, the half
angle of the cone its texels fill) and (irradiance, the luminance they were
cut at); every reader asked only whether the first w was positive.

goegap: a sun of 1.86 degrees and 5.8 of irradiance. autoshop: a lamp of
6.35 degrees and 0.28, where the rings had found another at 0.11. The two
`[environment][sun]` tests hold: a disc of nine texels taken whole (0.1084
against its closed form 0.1084), the residual sky within 2.1%, an even sky
left alone.

## A TX cloud as standard Gaussian Splatting files: `athenea flatten` (task TXF)

The TX transfer is the master (the user accepted the TX bake on 4 Oct 2026).
What leaves the engine for other viewers is a flattening of it: the transfer
under one sky and one set of lights, as the degree 3 harmonics every 3DGS
viewer reads, with no bake again (proposals 033 and 070). The mesh is not
needed; only the TX cloud and the lights.

### What is fitted, and how

- **The signal is what the viewer will show.** A viewer evaluates
  `0.5 + sum c_k Y_k(v)`, clamps at zero, and blends sRGB-encoded values, so
  by default the fit's target along each direction is the sRGB encoding of
  the light the raster computes for an eye there (`--referred scene` fits
  linear light, for PLY and USD). Exposure is applied before the encoding.
- **The shading is the raster's.** The relit part of `projectSplat` became
  `relitToward`, called by the projection for the camera and by
  `splatFlatten` for each direction: the surface built from the cloud, the
  overrides, the lobes, the cached view-independent terms, `relitSplat`. The
  only differences are the ones a frame has and a direction does not: no
  slope across a footprint (that is a screen-space ramp), and the roughness
  floor below.
- **Directions and weights.** N Fibonacci directions (256 by default) in the
  gaussian's frame, +z the facing its transfer was measured for. A surface
  weighs its back hemisphere 0.01; a thin wall weighs the whole sphere. In
  that frame M = (YᵀWY + λ diag(l²(l+1)²))⁻¹ YᵀW is the same for every
  gaussian of a class, so it is solved once (`flattenGram`, `flattenSolve`)
  and a gaussian's fit is a 16 x N product with what it showed, accumulated
  as it is shaded -- no buffer of samples.
- **Into the file's frame by quadrature.** The local fit is read at the 26
  points of Lebedev's rule in the file's frame and projected back onto the
  harmonics there. A product of two degree 3 harmonics is degree 6 and the
  rule is exact to degree 7, so the turn is exact; no Wigner rotation.
- **Positive where seen.** A viewer clamps at zero, and a ring of negative
  values round a highlight reads as a dark halo. After the fit, the higher
  bands are scaled by the largest factor that keeps every front direction
  (every direction, for a thin wall) at or above zero, channel by channel;
  the constant part is held at zero or above first. The share of gaussians
  shrunk is printed.
- **The roughness floor.** Degree 3 cannot hold a sharp reflection; fitting
  one rings. Before evaluating, the polish and the coat take
  `max(roughness, floor)`, the floor being the least of 64 candidates whose
  GGX reflection lobe keeps all but 5% of its square integral in bands 0 to 3
  (`flattenRoughnessFloor`, Legendre projection on the device). It blurs
  instead of ringing, and keeps the highlight's energy. `--no-roughness-floor`
  is the variant to measure it against.
- **A shadow catcher** is flattened as what the frame draws: black (the DC
  is `-0.5/C0`) at `catcherOpacity`'s opacity under the export sky, so a car
  and its ground shadow leave as one standard file.

### The files

One fit, several files, all Y up and in metres whatever the stage's axis and
unit (three.js, Spark, SuperSplat and glTF take that as it is), the same
coordinates in every one:

- **PLY**, INRIA's layout, float32, 248 B a gaussian, nothing else in it.
- **SPZ**, version 3 by default because Spark 2.3.1 reads 1 to 3 and not 4
  (measured by sysop on athenea.lucab.co.uk); version 4 (ZSTD) on request.
  Harmonics at 8/8 bits, not the packer's 5/4: a flattened reflection lives
  in bands 1 to 3. The bytes are worked out on the device exactly as
  Niantic's `packGaussians` works them out; harmonics past SPZ's [-1, 1] are
  scaled whole rather than clipped; the fixed point is chosen from the box
  (one bit to spare, never past 20; Niantic's packer always writes 12).
- **glTF** `.glb`, one POINTS primitive with `KHR_gaussian_splatting`, in
  `extensionsUsed` only. The attribute names follow the ratified extension as
  proposal 070 reads it; no viewer has opened one yet.
- **USD**, a ParticleField as `athenea convert` writes it.

Scales: Spark keeps ln σ in [-12, 9], and a converted pawn's thin axes are far
below that in metres. Floored at -12 in PLY and glTF (a few micrometres:
invisible), SPZ's own byte floors at -10; both fractions are printed.

### Why not an AOFX bundle

The data-processing steps of a conversion are bundles (mesh2splat, the bake
filter, the zonal fit). Flattening is not one: what it evaluates is the
engine's own relit shading under the frame's prepared sky -- the prefiltered
dome, the cached terms, the lights' records -- which only a frame has. The
fit and the packing could move into a bundle later; they would have to take
the radiance samples as an input, which the fused kernel never stores.

### Measured in the engine

`athenea flatten --validate` reads the written file back through this
engine's own readers (SPZ through Niantic's decompression), puts it where the
meshes stand, rasterises it with `athenea:splatDisplayBlend` -- each splat
sRGB-encoded before the blend and the pixel decoded after, as Spark draws --
and measures it material by material against the meshes path traced under
the same sky, with mesh2splat's validation (level A of proposal 070).

Measurements (the pawn and the Corvette under the baked sky and under
table_mountain, flatten times, file sizes) are queued for the GPU and not in
yet.

**A measure narrowed to one material frames the whole stage.** What a frame
leaves out -- the meshes kept out of a material's conversion, and the meshes
switched off where the written file stands in for the stage -- is worked out
over every material group of the stage, and `--validate-material` only
chooses which groups are measured (`apps/athenea/src/ValidateFrames.h`). It
used to be worked out over the chosen groups alone, so a flattened set
measured on its back wall's LED material was drawn with every other mesh of
the set still standing among the gaussians: the panels and the back wall came
out black, and the side walls striped where meshes and gaussians fought for
depth. That read as the SPZ (and the PLY) coming back wrong. It was not: the
same file read by `athenea render` and through `athenea convert` into a
ParticleField stage draws the panels and the wall as the bake does, and its
streams decode, by the format's own definitions, to the set's geometry (each
wall's gaussians flat across it, all of them opaque). `mesh2splat --validate
--validate-material` had the same fault the other way: the other materials'
meshes were converted along with the one measured. `athenea_usd_tests
"[validate]"` holds both on a stage of two meshes and two materials. Measured
on the set (M_led_fondo, 16 paths a pixel, 1063 x 525): relMSE 0.522 before,
0.380 after; the mean over the material's pixels 1.17 before and 1.96 after,
against 6.88 path traced.

### Not done

- The convention battery of proposal 070 §7.3 (one coefficient a gaussian, in
  each viewer): the axes and signs are checked against this engine's readers
  only (`athenea_render_tests "[flatten]"`), not against Spark, SuperSplat,
  Blender or three.js.
- Quantisation by the Gram metric and positivity checked after quantising
  (070 §4.3, §4.5); a fit weighted by the cells' own visibility (031 bits) or
  by a camera distribution; degree per gaussian; SH4; SOG; lobes in an
  `ATHENEA_gaussian_splatting` extension; a 3D mip filter baked into the
  covariance.
- A cloud a skeleton carries is flattened in the pose of the frame; levels of
  detail are flattened as the frame's cut.
- Non-uniform object scales are taken as their axis lengths, which is right
  for the rigid transforms clouds stand under and only approximate otherwise.

## mesh2splat inside hdAthenea, and the colour a host copies

A host that draws through hdAthenea has loaded a USD of its own, and the
plugin is built against it. Blender cannot load a second (its `libusd_ms` is
in a namespace of its own, and a second USD in the process is two type
registries), so converting a model there with `athenea mesh2splat` meant a
separate process with a separate USD and an exported stage between them.

**The command in the plugin.** With `ATHENEA_HYDRA_COMMANDS` (on by default
where `ATHENEA_BLENDER_LIB` is set, off elsewhere) hdAthenea also compiles
`CmdMesh2Splat.cpp` and exports two C functions (`apps/athenea/src/
Embedded.cpp`): `athenea_embedded_abi()` and `athenea_mesh2splat(argc, argv,
sink, user)`, which builds the same CLI11 subcommand, parses the arguments
and runs it. One implementation, so the add-on and the command cannot
disagree, and every option is there. The plugin then compiles the stage
reading and writing the command uses (`StageRenderer`, `Export`,
`MeshStage`, `BindingPurposes`) beside the delegate's sources, rather than
linking `athenea_usd`, whose copies of the delegate's sources would collide
with its own; and it links `aofx_host` and CLI11. One slang-rhi still: the
conversion opens its device through the process's `gpu_host::Context`, as
the command does, and the delegate keeps its own device on the same GPU.

The command's lines were `printf`s, which a host shows nobody. They now go
through `cli::out` / `cli::err` (`Output.h`): stdout and stderr in the
binary, the host's sink in the plugin. The entry serialises conversions (a
second call while one runs returns 2); the command's options and the sink
are process state for its duration. A parse error comes back as CLI11's exit
code with its message through the sink.

**Blender's 26.03.** `StageRenderer` used four things newer than the USD
Blender 5.3 ships: `UsdHydraRenderPassAPI` (its `hydra:rendererName` is read
by name where the header is missing), `HdRenderSettings::GetCamera` /
`GetDisable*` (the report leaves them unset before 26.08), the
`rayHitDistance` sorting hint (not counted) and the display-style scene
index's `SetRefineLevelFallback` (26.03's `SetRefineLevel` with its
`OptionalInt`). All behind `PXR_VERSION >= 2608` or `__has_include`; the
26.08 build compiles what it did.

**The colour a host copies.** Blender's viewport shows a delegate other than
Storm by mapping its colour buffer and uploading the bytes to a texture,
every frame (`DrawTexture::create_from_buffer` in Blender's
`render/hydra/viewport_engine.cc`). `athenea:colourHalf` (a host's
setting, read when the AOV's format is asked for) makes the `color` AOV
`Float16Vec4`: the conversion kernel already wrote halves, and the read back
and the host's upload carry 8 bytes a pixel instead of 16. And
`Engine::writeAov` keeps its conversion buffer and its placeholder between
frames instead of allocating both on every map.

**A converted cloud brought in as Blender points** is linear light, and a
`Points` prim said nothing of its colours' space. `HdAtheneaPoints` reads
`primvars:athenea:splat:linear` as a ParticleField does.

Not measured yet (a GPU turn): the conversion through the entry against the
binary on the same stage, which should be the same file; the half colour's
readback against float.

## hdAthenea inside Blender: phase 2

**Meshes into gaussians, in Blender** (`integrations/blender/athenea_hydra/
convert.py`). An operator, `athenea.mesh_to_splats`, and a sidebar panel
(*Athenea > Gaussian Splats*) with mesh2splat's main options (operations
manual 4.1.1). It runs the command inside Blender through the plugin's entry
point (*mesh2splat inside hdAthenea* above), which was the point: the
alternative, the `athenea` binary as a subprocess, is a second USD in a second
process and a binary to ship beside the plugin. Weighed and not taken:
- *the AOFX effect called from Python*: the effect knows triangles in a
  picture, not a stage; everything around it (reading the meshes and
  materials, textures, the budget, the bake, the export) is the command's
  2 000 lines, which would have had to be written again in Python or moved;
- *a second library beside hdAthenea* with `athenea_usd` in it: a second
  slang-rhi and a second copy of the delegate's classes in the process.

What the add-on does is bookkeeping: it exports the selection with Blender's
own USD exporter (the meshes; the armatures that deform them for a skinned
conversion; the scene's visible lights and its world for a bake under the
scene's light), hands the arguments over, and relays the lines. The worker
thread is Python's; ctypes lets go of the GIL for the call, and the sink,
called on that thread, only queues. A modal timer drains the queue into the
panel and the status bar (a progress estimated from the lines: a level's
textures, its meshes, its bake, its file), so the window stays live; without
a window (`-b`) the operator runs to its end. mesh2splat has no way to be
stopped, so neither has the operator.

**Bringing the cloud in.** Two ways, because Blender keeps less of a cloud
than a conversion writes:
- *Referenced USD* (default): an Empty whose custom property names the file;
  the add-on's USD export hook defines `cloud` under the Empty's prim with a
  reference to it (a `.athc` through a ParticleField with
  `AtheneaStreamedAssetAPI`). Hydra's USD export method composes it, and
  hdAthenea draws what the file holds: rig, levels of detail, relit material,
  normals, emission, Cryptomatte. The Empty moves the cloud. Blender's own
  engines see a box.
- *Gaussian-splat points*: `wm.usd_import` of the ParticleField, which
  Blender reads into its own GAUSSIAN_SPLAT point cloud: positions, sizes,
  rotations and harmonics, nothing else (no relit material, no normals, no
  rig). The conversion's colours are linear light and the import keeps no
