frame against `athenea-mcp`'s own render of the same camera (translate 0.4 0.3 6, rotate -3 4 10 in ZXY, 50 mm,
36 mm aperture) is identical -- relMSE 0, 8-bit max 0. A warm frame costs the server 16 ms at that size.

### Layers and the sky (19 Oct)

The user asked for every layer out of the node and as much of the comp as it can reach, and for the pawn's sky to
be changed inside Nuke or Natron.

**What a gaussian frame holds.** Measured on the processed sparrow (`sparrow-web/ref_cloud.usda`, 512 x 512): the
splats fill the colour, the depth and the Cryptomatte's three layers; `primId`, `instanceId`, `elementId`, `Neye`
and `normal` stay at their clear value, since only meshes write them. So the layers are colour, depth, `P` and
`CryptoObject00..02`.

**P is made on the device.** `StageRenderer::worldPosition` puts each pixel's view z back through the camera that
drew it (`athenea/usd/aov_position`: the pixel's centre unprojected as `splat_project` projects, then the rows of
view to world). Against the depth, on the sparrow at 480 x 270 from a camera of the tool's own: P's distance along
the view axis matches the depth to 7e-8 relative, every covered pixel reprojects onto its own centre (0.000 px),
and P's alpha agrees with the depth's coverage at every sampled pixel. It needs the tool's own camera, `xform` or
`eye`: a stage camera's projection is the delegate's, and a lens's window roll and distortion are not undone.

**The Cryptomatte crosses as Hydra holds it**, float4 (id, coverage, id, coverage) a layer, read from the render
buffer the delegate already converts on the device; the manifest crosses as a line of the answer. OpenFX carries no
metadata, so it stops at the plugin: a matte in the comp is picked by id.

**Planes, through Natron's OpenFX.** The official OpenFX carries no planes. Natron's fork of it -- the one
openfx-misc and openfx-io build on, which load in Nuke and Resolve as well -- has the Foundry multi-plane extension
in its support library and Natron's custom planes beside it, so `third_party/openfx` now points there. A host that
takes planes gets colour, `depth` (Z), `P` (XYZA) and the three Cryptomatte layers as planes of the one output, all
drawn in one call (`setRenderAllPlanes`) and only those it asks for. Nuke takes from an OpenFX node only its own
planes (motion vectors, disparity), so there an `output` knob picks the layer RGBA shows. The test host stays
without the extensions: a host that knows nothing of planes, which is the plainest case.

**The sky.** `render` takes `sky` (an image for every dome; a stage without one gets the default dome first),
`skyRotation` and `skyVisible`, and sets a dome only where it differs, since each set is a session edit Hydra syncs;
the node has the same three knobs. On the pawn (`pieces/pawn/cut_lod2`, a transfer cloud baked under autoshop_01),
1024 x 1024: kloofendal at 120 degrees relights the marble and puts the new sky in the glass; the first frame after
a change costs about 0.4 s (the sky's harmonics and prefiltered chain), the frames after it 50 ms; giving back the
stage's sky (`sky` empty) draws a frame identical to the stage's own (relMSE 0).

Through the plugin, the unit sphere's frame against `athenea-mcp`'s own is still identical (relMSE 0) after the move
to Natron's OpenFX.

**In Natron itself** (Niik-l's 2.6 fork, built on this Mac by the natron session; NatronRenderer with openfx-io's
WriteOIIO, every plane, 32-bit float): the node lists colour, `depth`, `P` and `CryptoObject00..02` among its
layers, and the pawn at 1920 x 1080 under kloofendal turned 120 degrees writes one EXR of 21 channels whose colour
and P are identical to the test host's frames of the same camera (relMSE 0; P's every pixel within 1e-6). Natron
spells a custom plane with a channels label the node does not write (`..._ChannelsLabel_XYZA_...`), so a plane is
matched by its name (`OFX::extractCustomPlane`), not by the whole string. Natron's writer defaults to half floats,
which would round a Cryptomatte id into another: the matte wants `bitDepth` 32f.

**One server for the host.** Natron renders a sequence on several threads and makes an instance of the node for
each, and the server was an instance's: 24 frames of the Corvette's transfer cloud (`corvette-lights/clouds/base_tx`,
3 M gaussians, 2.9 GB) started 12 servers, each loading the car, and most frames took 11-12 s. The server is now the
plugin's, one for the process under one lock. The same 24 frames at 1920 x 1080, every plane, from the scene's
camera, NatronRenderer to 32-bit multi-layer EXRs (server times, `ATHENEA_OFX_DEBUG`): the first frame 7.5 s (the
stage opened and uploaded), frames 2-12 with a still sky 120-170 ms, frames 13-24 with the sky turning every frame
190-220 ms; the 24 frames 14 s from the first render to the last write. Natron also handed the node a pixel aspect
of NaN from some threads (`getProjectPixelAspectRatio`), which made the vertical aperture NaN; the node now takes
the image's own aspect, and refuses a request with a number that is not finite, naming it, rather than sending it.
The server, for its part, answers an argument of the wrong type as the call's error instead of ending on the JSON
library's exception.

Not done: the order of Nuke's rotations is read from its documentation, not yet checked in Nuke; Nuke's own camera
input (its OpenFX camera extension) in place of linked knobs; normals and motion vectors of gaussians, which the
rasteriser does not write (the skinned wings' motion first); the sky as an image input of the node rather than a
file; `.ply`/`.spz` opened directly rather than converted first; Linux and Windows builds and a signed bundle.

## A transfer the stage turns, and the gaussians' parameters drawn (19 Oct)

**The bug.** A TX transfer -- its harmonics, its reflected field, its open cells -- is a set of directions of the
file it was baked in. The raster read them as directions of the world, which they are only while nothing turns
the cloud. In Blender the pawn's clouds (Y-up) were stood up into the Z-up scene by a quarter turn on their
Empties, and the glass head drew in fragments; the same clouds under an Xform turned 90 degrees in a Z-up stage
drew the same fragments in the engine itself. A zonal transfer was already right: its lobes turn with each
gaussian (`splatTransferFrame`).

**The fix.** `relightCloudFrame` takes the cloud's frame from the rows that put it in the world (their linear
part's columns made unit), and `transferAlong` puts a direction of the world into it before the field, the
indirect half, the sun's share or a cell is read; a dot product with the sky reads the sky turned into the same
frame, which `splat/sky_turn.slang` makes once an instance and a frame, where the instance turns a non-zonal
transfer: the world's domes first, then the turned ones (`skyCloud` entries on). The turn is a projection of
`L(R w)` onto the sixteen harmonics by a product rule exact for their products (four Gauss-Legendre nodes in z,
eight steps in phi). A cloud nothing turns binds the sky as before and reads nothing turned.

Measured: the pawn (`pieces/pawn/cut_lod2`) turned 60 degrees about up with its camera, under the sky turned 60
degrees, against the pawn unturned, 768 x 768: relMSE 9e-6, PSNR 61 dB, SSIM 0.9999 (the turn the other way: 11
dB, so the comparison tells the frames apart). The suite's TX balls (`[tx_turned]`, hidden, after the
`mesh2splat_tx_*` conversions), turned with camera and sky, the background hidden: glass relMSE 1.6e-4, paint
1.0e-4 against unturned, where under a sky left unturned they read 0.13 and 1.5e-2; the 99th percentile is not
held, since a percent of those pixels is the ball's rim, where the turned transform rounds a footprint a little
differently. With the shaders from before the fix the same test fails. The `[glass]` cases pass after it; the
`[transfer]` and `[zonal]` cases and the rasteriser's suite fail after it exactly where they failed before it: the posed cloud's refit, the
skinned zonal transfer against a turned still cloud, the TX ball against the mesh path traced and the thin sheet
at a low index -- none of them new. Six test kernels built a `SplatSurface` without setting every field; they
now say the cloud is not turned.

Not done: the ray traced route turns its directions but dots its harmonics with the world's sky
(`rt_shade.slang`, `skyCloud` 0): a turned TX cloud traced still reads the wrong sky in its body.

**The parameters, drawn** (`athenea:splatView`, `render`'s `splatView`). For a dataset of what a relit cloud is
made of, each gaussian's parameter is drawn in place of its light and blended by its opacity, as the light is:
albedo, roughness, metallic, transmission, ior, the normal, opacity, size, the transfer's sky visibility, its
bounce, its open cells, its reflected field, emission, the light the cloud carries and the material's own
roughness (`splatParameterColour`). On the pawn at 768 x 768 a view costs 20-60 ms. Values that are not colours
are scaled to be seen -- a size on a logarithmic ramp, a normal as `n / 2 + 1/2` -- and a cloud that is not relit
has only its light, opacity and size to show.

## A clone of the public repository builds (19 Oct)

The repository is public, and a clone of the trunk did not build: the aopenfx and gpe pins were commits that
existed only on the machine that made them, and genlock, a submodule, is a private repository. The pins are now
pushed to their branches (gpe `lrt-fixes`, aopenfx `cuda-half`, which `.gitmodules` now names) before they move
here. genlock is optional: `ATHENEA_WITH_GENLOCK` is on when `third_party/genlock` is checked out, and its
`.gitmodules` entry has `update = none`, so a recursive clone skips it. Only `athenea live` follows a PTP master
and stamps ST 2059-1 timecode -- the sched module, the subcommand and their tests -- so without genlock that one
subcommand is missing and everything else builds as before.

What the public tree no longer carries, in the same pass: the paper (its sources, kept privately, and its
PDFs, assets of the `docs-2026-10-19` release) and the presentations' PDFs, ignored here; the production notes of
the Corvette on an iPhone (`docs/pieces.md`); `remote-test.sh` takes its host as an argument or `ATHENEA_REMOTE` rather than defaulting to a machine on a
private network; the sparrow film's scripts read `SPARROW` and `ATHENEA` instead of one machine's paths, which made
a copy per machine; the Blender tests and the MaterialX bench write under the build tree and `~/athenea-renders`.
The macOS package identifier is `uk.co.lucab.athenea`, the order the OFX bundle already used. Every first-party
source, script and CMake file carries the copyright line.

## The Blender add-on and the OpenFX node on Linux and Windows (19 Oct)

Built and run on one laptop (RTX 3070 Laptop, 8 GB): Linux under WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 12.9) and Windows natively
(MSVC 14.44), against the Blender 5.3 beta of 19 Oct, whose USD is the same 26.08 in `pxrBlender_v26_08` on every
system.

- **Linux.** Blender ships `lib/libusd_ms.so` and the rest by SONAME, so `cmake/BlenderUsd.cmake` names each library
  by its base and links the file; Python's symbols are left undefined, as a shared library on Linux may.
  `build-usd-blender.sh` runs there with `BLENDER_LIB`. GCC 13 rejects the constructor of
  `HdRetainedTypedSampledDataSource<bool>` written with its template arguments, which `build-usd.sh` already rewrote;
  the Blender script now does too. `tests/blender`: `test_module` passes whole; `viewport_readback` passes (half
  draws what float draws, p99 0) at 2.5 s a frame; `tx_module` is refused, because WSL has no OptiX and a bake
  traces.
- **Windows.** Blender ships DLLs without import libraries and links OpenSubdiv into `usd_ms.dll`:
  `build-usd-blender.ps1` makes a `.lib` from each DLL's exports (`dumpbin /exports`, `lib /def`; 23 548 for
  `usd_ms.dll`) and builds OpenSubdiv for USD's configure alone. Python is `python313.dll`, linked by its import
  library. USD opens a plugin with `LoadLibrary`, which does not look beside it: the plugin carries Slang's and
  zlib's DLLs and the add-on puts their folder on `PATH` before registering it. The embedded commands' attributes
  are macros MSVC reads (`__declspec(dllexport)`). `test_module` passes whole; `viewport_readback` passes at
  2.7-4 s a frame; `tx_module` bakes (1313 s cold, 460 s with OptiX's cache) and its catcher, comparison with
  Cycles (relMSE 0.036), export and cancel pass, but the cloud against the path traced reference is relMSE 0.72
  and p99 193 where macOS passes (#40), and Blender exits with 0xC0000409 after it (#41).
- **OpenFX on Linux.** The bundle builds (`Contents/Linux-x86-64`, `athenea-mcp` in `Resources/bin`) and
  `athenea_ofx_host` renders a frame through it. Its server finds the shaders only in the build tree (#43). The
  server is started on Windows with `CreateProcess` on two pipes, and the bundle is built there (`Win64`): under
  MSVC, OpenFX's support library keeps `std::auto_ptr` (`_HAS_AUTO_PTR_ETC`), leaves out the HWND interact the
  node does not draw, and the test host's expat is fetched and built static. `athenea_ofx_host` renders the same
  frame through the bundle on Windows as on Linux: the same means in every channel, alpha 0.652 at three units and
  0.404 at eight.

The viewport's readback costs seconds a frame on CUDA (#42) where Metal's costs milliseconds.

The "Not done: Windows" of *A plugin finds its files from itself* is done: `Platform.cpp` finds its module with
`GetModuleHandleExW` since the Windows port.

## A prim placed by the host, a matrix a frame (19 Oct)

A compositor that moves prims -- a manipulator dragging a dome, a transform node animated over time -- wrote a new
layer and reopened the stage at every change, seconds a change. `setPrimTransform(prim, localToParent)` places a
prim as `setPrimVisible` hides one: a session opinion applied through the stage scene index, the file untouched.
The first call makes the prim's op stack one `xformOp:transform` (`MakeMatrixXform`); every call after it finds
that single op and sets its value, so a frame changes one attribute and Hydra resyncs the transform alone.
`clearPrimTransform` removes the session's op order and matrix, and the authored transform is back.

- `athenea_usd_tests "[transform]"`: a square moved by a first matrix and then a second draws what a stage that
  authored the same translation draws, to the last bit (maxRel 0); cleared, it draws the original frame to the last
  bit; the file never names an `xformOp`.

## A frame waits for the device once (23 Oct)

A stage of lightmapped meshes drawn unlit took 10.4 ms a frame on CUDA (RTX 3070, 1920x1080, drawn and not read
back) for 3.5 ms of kernels; a one-quad stage took 3.8 ms for 1.6 ms. The host waited for the device ten to
twenty-two times a frame, at three kinds of place, which `ATHENEA_SYNC_TRACE=1` now names by file and line:

- **Batches submitted and waited for between passes.** The mesh layer, the points' composite, the domes, the
  exposure, the light groups and the plates each waited for their own batch, and the splat rasteriser waited
  twice in a frame that had no splats. They are submitted and not waited for: each pass comes after the last on
  the one queue, which is the only order they need. The frame waits once, at the end of
  `StageRenderer::execute`, where a host takes the image. The visibility pass is submitted as soon as it is
  recorded, so the device runs it while the host records the shading.
- **Work rebuilt every frame that had not changed.** `LightTable::set` uploaded the lights and rebuilt their
  tree -- a dozen waits, two of them readbacks -- for lights the byte comparison it already made found identical;
  it now returns there. The tree over the instances (`BvhScene`, the CUDA route's visibility) read the
  instances' bounds back, and refitted in rounds of eight passes, each round a readback: the bounds now stay on
  the device for the codes' kernel, the refit is one group's dispatch that passes until nothing changes
  (`bvhRefitGroup`), the buffers stand between frames, and the tree is not rebuilt at all while the instance
  records -- the view is in them -- are the last frame's (`GpuScene::instancesRevision`).
- **Copies that were synchronous.** slang-rhi's CUDA backend copied a buffer with `cuMemcpy` on the queue's
  stream, which blocks the host until the stream has run everything before it, and every upload is such a copy
  from the staging heap: patched to `cuMemcpyAsync` (`cmake/patches/slang-rhi-cuda-async-copy.patch`). A device
  buffer made with data up to 16 MiB is now made empty and filled by a queued upload, where slang-rhi's CUDA
  `createBuffer` copied it with `cuMemcpy` as well.

| stage (RTX 3070, 1920x1080, `--no-readback`, median of 199) | before | after, still | after, moving (`--drift 0.01`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| one quad, unlit (`suelo.usda`) | 3.84 ms | 3.42-3.60 ms | 3.71 ms |
| set A, 37 lightmapped meshes | 10.38 ms | 3.78-3.81 ms | 5.49 ms |
| set B, 40 lightmapped meshes | 10.43 ms | 3.60-3.77 ms | 5.93 ms |

Before, the lights and the instances' tree were rebuilt every frame whatever the camera did, so a moving camera
cost what a still one did. After, a moving camera rebuilds the tree each frame and a still one does not.

Waits in a steady frame: 10 on the quad and about 22 on set A before, one after (`ATHENEA_SYNC_TRACE`). nsys over 300
frames of set A: `cuMemcpy` 1391 calls before the patch, 135 after (loading only); kernel time unchanged, 3.5 ms a
frame. The images are identical before and after (`oiiotool --diff`, all three stages).

What a frame still waits for: a frame with splats reads its visible and pair counts back to size its buffers;
a frame that asks for its splat counts (a panel) waits for them; `ATHENEA_STAGES` waits to time. A CUDA fence in
slang-rhi is a value the host sets at submit, not when the device gets there, so a readback is never known
finished without a wait.

### Not done

- The splat rasteriser's count readback, which an indirect dispatch sized on the device would remove.
- The host's own cost: about forty launches a frame, each with its constant buffer copied, are 2-3 ms of driver
  calls on set A; the instances' tree takes half of them when the camera moves.
- `TextureStore::bind` rebinds every slot and sampler at each dispatch that reads textures.
- The ray route's TLAS (`RayTracingScene`) is still rebuilt and waited for every frame where the device traces
  inline; CUDA does not take that route. (Done: see "What a frame still waited for", 24 Oct.)

## What a frame still waited for (24 Oct)

An inventory, from the code, of every place the host waits for the device on the per-frame path of
`StageRenderer::draw` -> `Engine::render`, for the mesh routes lit and unlit, after "A frame waits for the device
once": a batch submitted with `submit(true)`, a buffer read back (`Buffer::read`, which waits for idle), a
`waitIdle`, a count read to size a later dispatch. `ATHENEA_SYNC_TRACE=1` confirmed it on a one-quad stage unlit, the
same quad lit under a dome and a sphere light, and a 37-mesh set, on the rays and the compute BVH routes, still and
with a camera that moves (`stage --drift`).

| where | when | waits a frame | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `StageRenderer::execute`, `waitIdle` | every frame | 1 | kept: the frame's one, where a host takes the image |
| `RayTracingScene::build`: the instance descriptors, then the top level (its scratch freed on return) | the rays route; and lit frames where shading's shadow rays are inline (Metal) | 2 | 0: the top level stands while the instances' world placement does, and is built without a wait |
| `RayTracingScene::build`: a deformed mesh's bottom level refit | a mesh deformed this frame | 1 a mesh | 0 |
| `MaterialShading`: the copy screen-space reflections read | `athenea:screenSpaceReflections` on | 2 | 0 |
| `GpuScene::update`: positions lerped for a deforming mesh; the bucket records; the instancers' records | under motion blur; any point instancer | 1 each | 0 |
| `GpuScene::refresh` | a mesh deformed in place (same topology) | 1 a mesh | 0 |
| `Engine::writeAov`: the conversion, then the read | each render buffer a host maps | 2 | 1, the read |
| `BvhScene::refit`: a deformed mesh's tree, a readback every eight passes | the BVH route, a mesh deformed | 1-4 a mesh | kept (below) |
| `TileRasterizer`: the visible and pair counts | a frame with splats | 1 | kept (below) |
| `ATHENEA_STAGES` | when asked | one a stage | kept: it waits to time |

Steady-frame waits counted by the trace, before and after, at 640x360:

| stage | route | before, still / moving | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| one quad, unlit | compute BVH | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
| one quad, unlit | rays | 3 / 3 | 1 / 1 |
| one quad, lit (dome, sphere) | compute BVH (shadows by inline rays) | 3 / 3 | 1 / 1 |
| one quad, lit | rays | 3 / 3 | 1 / 1 |
| 37 lightmapped meshes, moving | either | 3 | 1 |

The images are the same: the top level built from the same records is the same structure, and the waits removed
were between passes the one queue already orders.

**The top level stands.** `GpuScene::placementRevision()` counts the frames whose instance records differ from the
last's in anything but the view and the normal matrix -- the world transform, the mesh, the flags, the mask -- or
that the device wrote (instancers, motion buckets), and `RayTracingScene` keeps its top level while that, the pools'
generation and the meshes' positions revision do. A camera that moves changes only the records' view, so it rebuilds
nothing; the compute BVH's tree over the instances is in view space and is still rebuilt (one batch, no wait) when
the camera moves. The scratch the build used to free on return is kept, and the structure replaced is kept one build
longer, for a frame the device may still be tracing.

**A test counts them.** `athenea_usd_tests "[sync]"` draws a quad unlit, and lit under a dome, on every route the
device has, still and moving, and checks that each steady frame adds exactly one to `Device::syncs()`. A pass that
starts waiting again fails it, with no timing.

**What the trace does not see.** slang-rhi's CUDA backend waits in places the engine does not call a wait: a buffer
made with more than 16 MiB of data (noted, loading only), a texture copy (`cuMemcpy3D`, device to array, which does
not wait for the host by CUDA's rules), an indirect dispatch, which reads its arguments back (the engine has none).
None is on a steady frame of these stages.

**On CUDA these stages already waited once.** CUDA takes the compute BVH route, and shading's shadow rays are inline
only, so a CUDA frame built no top level: the waits removed here are Metal's, and CUDA's under motion, instancers and
reflections. A profile of a frame on CUDA with about nine `cuStreamSynchronize` is what the build before "A frame
waits for the device once" did (ten on the quad); one from a build after it has one. What remains of the gap between
a frame's kernels and its time on CUDA is the host's: recording and launching some forty dispatches.

**On an L4 the engine's draw is about 2.9 ms.** A set of unlit lightmapped meshes at 1920x1080, drawn and not read back,
300 frames on the base of this work (Linux, CUDA 12.8): median 2.89 ms, 3.84 ms with `athenea:meshAntialias` 4;
`ATHENEA_STAGES`: visibility 1.0 ms, shading 0.6, the mesh layer 2.2. A render that costs a host three times that is
spending it outside `StageRenderer::draw` -- reading the image back, or setting a frame up per call.

**A frame of no splats counts nothing.** The same `ATHENEA_STAGES` gave the splat stages 0.6 ms with no splat in the
frame: two prefix sums over one element, the tiles' ranges cleared, and the blend that composites the mesh layer.
The sums are skipped where the frame has no splats or points and no panel counts it, and the ranges are cleared only
where a frame of pairs wrote them: a frame of none leaves them empty for the next. The blend stays -- it is what puts
the background and the depth convention on the mesh layer -- and a frame drawn after a frame of splats is the frame
a rasteriser that never drew one draws, to the bit (`athenea_render_tests`, "a frame of no splats over a layer").

### Not done

- A frame of meshes alone still runs the splat blend over the whole image (0.4 ms of the 0.6 on an L4). The mesh
  layer could be the frame's targets where no splat or point is drawn, if the background and the depth it writes
  were the blend's.
- `BvhScene::refit` of a deformed mesh still reads a count back every eight passes. One group's dispatch
  (`bvhRefitGroup`, what the instances' tree uses) would walk a mesh of a million triangles on 256 threads; a fixed
  number of passes needs the tree's depth, read once when it is built.
- The splat rasteriser's visible and pair counts (unchanged from "A frame waits for the device once").
- The host's recording cost per dispatch on CUDA (the constant data copied per launch, `TextureStore::bind`
  rebinding every slot): measured on a CUDA device, not here.
- The compute BVH's tree over the instances is built in view space and rebuilt when the camera moves.

## Mesh edges antialiased from the neighbourhood's triangles (23 Oct)

A stage of lightmapped meshes drawn at one sample a pixel shows its edges as stairs. Drawing it at 1.5 times the
size and filtering it down cost 6-8 ms at 1920x1080 on an L4, for a frame whose budget is 20. What was wanted
was the edges at 1-2 ms, and on every visibility route: on CUDA nothing rasterises, and the ids come from rays
(OptiX) or the compute BVH, so a multisampled raster target would have done nothing there.

`athenea:meshAntialias` (4, 8 or 16; 0, the default, changes nothing) runs one kernel after the mesh layer is
shaded and before anything composites it (`technique::MeshAntialias`, `technique/mesh_antialias.slang`):

- **Which pixels.** One whose four sides all saw its own (instance, triangle) is left alone, after five id reads.
  The rest read their corners too.
- **What a sub-sample sees.** The distinct triangles of the 3x3 neighbourhood (six at most) are the candidates.
  Each of the sample's rays, at the standard multisample positions, is intersected with every candidate and the
  nearest it is inside wins, as a depth test would; none, and it sees the background where a neighbour saw
  nothing, else the pixel's own colour.
- **What colour.** The one already shaded at the pixel that saw the winner. Nothing is seen or shaded again, so
  the cost is the same lit or unlit, and the ids are only read: every route resolves alike, and with the setting
  off the frame is the one it was.
- **What it does not trust.** A candidate that covers the pixel's own centre nearer than what the centre saw
  was removed there -- a cutout's hole, a hidden instance -- and is left out, so a hole is not filled. Two
  triangles of one instance in one plane are one surface: the sample keeps the pixel's colour, so a flat wall
  is not blurred along the diagonals it was split into.

The colour of a neighbour's centre stands in for the colour at the sample, a pixel away at most: exact for a
flat colour, a blur of a pixel along an edge for a texture.

### Measured

The test (`[antialias]`) draws two squares turned against each other and the background, and compares with the
same frame drawn 8x8 times larger and boxed down on the device, on the rasteriser and on the compute BVH (the
two agree to the fourth digit):

| | relMSE | p99 (codes) | max (codes) |
|---|---|---|---|
| one sample a pixel | 6.67e-3 | 78 | 178 |
| 4 samples | 1.45e-3 | 21 | 104 |
| 8 samples | 7.98e-4 | 14 | 91 |
| 16 samples | 3.56e-4 | 11 | 75 |

The pixels beyond 2 codes hardly fall (483 to 429): an edge pixel off its coverage by a sixteenth is still more
than 2 codes in sRGB near black. 1108 to 2729 words of the 76800 change; the interior none.

`athenea stage --frames 200 --no-readback`, 1920x1080, M5 Pro (Metal), the first virtual set (lit: the dome's
lobes dominate the frame), automatic visibility (rays), medians of two rounds:

| | still | moving (`--drift 0.01`) | the resolve alone (`ATHENEA_STAGES`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| off | 15.62-15.71 ms | 15.55-15.77 ms | -- |
| 4 | 16.59-16.65 ms | 16.68-16.69 ms | 1.3-1.5 ms |
| 8 | 16.65-16.66 ms | 16.66-16.71 ms | 1.6 ms |
| 16 | 16.80-16.83 ms | 16.97-17.25 ms | 2.1-2.3 ms |

`ATHENEA_STAGES` waits before and after the resolve, so its figure holds a submit and a wait; the medians say
1.0 ms for 4 samples and 1.2-1.5 for 16. The raster route measured the same within 0.5 ms. Not yet measured on
the L4.

### Not done

- A triangle no pixel centre around it saw -- a wire, a slat thinner than a pixel -- is not found, as it is not
  drawn at one sample; its stairs and its gaps stay.
- The ids, the depth, the AOVs and Cryptomatte stay one sample a pixel; the depth the splats are composited by is
  the centre's, so a splat behind a mesh edge is cut as before.
- The edge of a cutout's hole is not resolved (the candidate is not trusted there).
- Texture aliasing inside a surface is the mip selection's, not this pass's.
- The copy of the layer the kernel reads its neighbours from is a full-frame copy each frame.

## Mesh lights: emitting meshes and MeshLightAPI as lights (LIGHT1, 27 Oct)

Emitting geometry lit the scene only in the path tracer and the bakes that go through it, chosen from a flat
per-triangle power table (`EmissiveTable`, "Emitting triangles as a light" in M5); the raster and the relit
gaussians showed its glow and nothing more, and UsdLux's `MeshLightAPI` was not read at all. The aim is that
LED strips, screens, studio lamps and a car's lamps light meshes and TX gaussians every frame in the raster,
without a bake. The work is staged: A (mesh lights as lights, the path tracer through a tree), B (meshes lit
in the raster, sampled then analytic), C (TX gaussians relit by them), D (groups and dimming), E (the groups' indirect light baked).

### What Hydra hands over for a `MeshLightAPI`

OpenUSD 26.08 makes no `meshLight` prim. A spike over `UsdImagingCreateSceneIndices` on a mesh with the API
showed the prim stays a `mesh`, with a `light` container holding `isLight`, `materialSyncMode` and `filters`,
and a material network of its own whose `light` terminal is a `MeshLight` node carrying `color`, `intensity`,
`exposure` and `normalize`. `HdSceneIndexAdapterSceneDelegate::GetLightParamValue` reads only the container,
so the mesh's Sync reads the inputs from the terminal scene index (`Mesh.cpp`, `meshLightOf`), as `Light.cpp`
reads a dome's colour space. A change to an input dirties the mesh's material. Registering a `meshLight`
sprim type would receive nothing, and is not done.

### The design

**A region, not more buffers.** Every kernel that lights anything binds the light words buffer (`iesValues`),
and the shading and path tracing kernels are at Metal's thirty-one buffers. The mesh lights live in a region
at its front (`LightTable::reserveMesh`), which the table shifts its IES values, tree nodes and motion samples
past. The region keeps its contents while its size holds; a light table upload writes past it in place, or
into a larger buffer the region is copied into on the device. `meshLightWords` (a uniform, 0 for none) says
whether a kernel has one. The plan put the clusters' records after the UsdLux ones in `lights`; they are in
the region instead, since a record count that moves with the UsdLux lights would have moved every cluster's
index, and `lightCount` and every loop over it are untouched either way.

**The region's layout** is `shaders/athenea/light/mesh_lights.slang`'s: a header (counts, offsets, the 32
emission groups' weights, 128 emitter sets), each instance record's first triangle, the emitting triangles'
scene numbers in order with their slots and clusters, then 16 words a triangle (corners in world space, power,
in-cluster cumulative power, radiance, instance and triangle), 32 words a cluster (a rectangle standing in for
it, power, area, its normals' cone, its triangle range, group and tree leaf) and the tree's nodes in
`light_bvh.slang`'s encoding.

**An instance record's flags carry who emits.** Bit 2 says `MeshLightAPI`, bits 3 to 7 an emission group,
bits 24 to 30 the emitter set (a `MeshLightAPI`'s controls, numbered as first met in the frame), bit 31 that
the record may emit at all -- its material row, a subset's or the API (`MaterialCompiler::emits`, a row flag
`kMaterialEmits`). The material row keeps bits 8 to 23: 65535 rows.

**A rebuild decides membership, a refit only moves.** `MeshLights::plan`, before the light table is set,
counts the candidate records' triangles and probes each one's emission on the device -- the material at its
centre with the triangle's whole texture footprint, so a screen is read at the mip that averages it, times the
API's controls -- and counts what passes the threshold (1e-4 of luminance): two waits, which size the region.
`MeshLights::write` then compacts, keys (group, sides, normal octant, a cube of a 16^3 grid over the
emitters' bounds), sorts and cuts the clusters where the key changes, lays out the triangles and builds the
tree with the compute LBVH's `bvh_hierarchy` and the light tree's `lightParents` and `lightSettle`: two more
waits. A frame that moves an emitter, or reweighs a group, refits: corners, powers, each cluster's rectangle
and leaf, and the tree settled in as many `lightSettle` passes as it is deep (measured once at the rebuild),
recorded into the frame's batch with no wait. A rebuild runs when the scene's meshes, the material rows,
the instance count or the emitter key (sets and flags) change, never because something moved.

The plan named an LBVH over the triangles with cluster roots chosen by cone, extent and flatness; the key
cells stand in for that. A cluster is then at most one cube of the grid, all its normals in one octant, which
bounds both what a rectangle has to stand for and the cone; a long strip becomes one cluster a cube.

**The rectangle** lies in the plane of the area-weighted normal through the area-weighted centre, its long
side along the corners' principal direction in that plane, its extent their corners'. It gives off the
cluster's power over its own area, so it carries the light the triangles do. Sampling and the path tracer use
the triangles; the rectangle is for the closed forms (B2, C).

**What a `MeshLightAPI` emits.** One radiance, both seen and casting, so every estimator agrees on it:
`colour x intensity x 2^exposure` (the blackbody of the temperature where enabled) from the front faces, or
both where the gprim is double sided; `materialGlowTintsLight` multiplies it by the material's emission where
the material emits, `independent` adds the two, `noMaterialResponse` drops the material's
(`meshLightEmission`, applied where the path tracer and the raster evaluate a material). UsdLux leaves the
mode's light-ray and camera-ray responses apart; one radiance is the simplification. A material's own emission
stays two-sided, as it always was. `normalize` is not applied.

**The path tracer** chooses its emitting triangles through the tree where there are clusters
(`sampleEmissive`): a cluster by its importance at the point (Conty and Kulla, the UsdLux lights' own),
a triangle by its share of the cluster's power, a point uniform on it, divided by exactly that density.
MIS weighs both strategies by another density they share -- the triangle's share of all the clusters'
power over its area, found through its scene number by a binary search over the emitting ones -- since
weights need only agree between the strategies. The plan weighed by the tree's own density; a second ascent
of a tree in the path tracing kernel (the UsdLux lights' is the first) put Apple's Metal compiler into an
internal error on any UsdPreviewSurface material (`AGXMetalG17X Code=3`, reproduced on the dumped kernel
outside the engine and gone without the ascent). It costs the many-emitter case some of its gain (below).
`EmissiveTable` stays, and is what `athenea:meshLights` off uses: the reference. Its serial power sum was to move to `PrefixSum`; that sum is over floats and `PrefixSum` sums
uints, so it stays as it was.

**A precision fix in the light tree.** `chooseLightBvh` took the far child's probability as `1 - pa`; beside a
near light `pa` rounds to within an ulp of one, and the descent and `lightPdfChoiceBvh` (which takes
`ib / total`) parted by more than 1e-4 for 7 draws in a million. The descent takes `ib / total` now. The
UsdLux lights' tree is affected by rounding only.

### Measured (Metal, M5 Pro)

- A planar cluster of four triangles of three areas, 2^20 samples binned over its rectangle against the area
  density its shares give: chi2 1578.9 on 1505 dof (z 1.35), the density integrating to 1.0000; no sample
  whose density `meshClusterPdf` disputes beyond 1e-3, no tree choice whose probability `meshClusterChoicePdf`
  disputes beyond 1e-4.
- The clusters' power against `EmissiveTable`'s on twelve triangles: 5.294250 both.
- Three frames of an emitter moved and stretched 1.2 to 1.6 times: no rebuild, three refits, the 24
  membership words unchanged; the power 6.353100, 1.2 times the first, as the stretch says.
- The path tracer through the tree against the flat table on a floor under a panel and a strip, 8192 paths
  each: relMSE 1.53e-5, against 1.97e-3 for a 32-path flat frame. At 32 paths the tree's error is 1.20e-3.
- Sixty strips over a floor, 32 paths against 8192 of the flat table: flat 5.88e-2, tree 4.01e-2, 1.46
  times less; the two deep frames part by 1.16e-4. Weighed by the tree's own density it was 1.59e-2, 3.7
  times less: what the compiler's limit costs.
- The same on Vulkan (RTX 3070): the same numbers to the last digit printed; the technique cases on CUDA
  as well (chi2 1578.7 on 1505 dof). The usd cases need rasterisation, which CUDA has not, and skip.
- A `MeshLightAPI` quad of 1 x 1 at intensity 3 against a RectLight of the same, 8192 paths, in each of the
  three sync modes (the third with an emitting material bound): relMSE 2.98e-7, against 6.51e-5 for its own
  32-path frame.

### Not done (stage A)

- `inputs:normalize` on a `MeshLightAPI`.
- More than 127 distinct sets of `MeshLightAPI` controls in a frame: the rest share the last.
- Light linking on a mesh light: its clusters reach every prim.
- Under motion blur the clusters are the shutter's first bucket's.
- A frame with volumes takes no emitting triangle as a light, through the tree or the table, as before.

### Stage B: meshes lit by mesh lights in the raster

**Sampled** (`athenea:meshLightSamples` 1 to 64): each sample is the path tracer's next event estimate --
a cluster through the tree, a triangle, a point -- with no MIS (no lobe sample of the raster meets an
emitter). `traceShadows` traces their rays after the light samples' and every lobe bit the frame numbers,
so the bit of mesh sample `i` is at the same place in every pixel. A shadow ray toward an emitter stops
short of it by more than the ray's origin moves (5e-3 of the scale): stopped at 1e-4 of the distance, the
emitting triangle was its own occluder and the floor under a MeshLightAPI quad drew black. A frame lit by
mesh lights alone has no headlight, in the raster as in the path tracer.

**In closed form** (0, the default), the on-air path:

- *The cut.* `meshLightCut` takes, for each 16 x 16 tile, a cut of up to 16 nodes of the tree from the
  surface at the tile's middle: the most important node split while there is room, every cluster under
  exactly one entry. With 8 entries, as the plan had it, eight 5 m strips (some 90 clusters) left most
  of a floor to aggregates, and the tiles' borders showed as steps.
- *A cluster* is integrated over its rectangle: a diffuse lobe by the form factor, the horizon clipped by
  the sphere of the same vector (Snyder's integral; no clipping code); a GGX lobe -- a conductor, a
  generalised Schlick, a dielectric's reflection -- by the linearly transformed cosine fitted to GGX, times
  the lobe's own albedo in reflection; a Zeltner sheen by its own LTC. Transmission and hair are left out.
- *An aggregate* (a node standing for several clusters) lights the diffuse lobes as a Lambertian point at
  its box's middle: its power, the colour and facing of its most important cluster, the receiver's cosine
  widened by the angle the box subtends. Without that widening a node straddling a surface's horizon gave
  it nothing: the box's front face under strips above and in front of it drew black.
- *The shadow* is a ratio (Heitz, Hill and McGuire 2018): two rays a pixel through the tree, the
  luminance-and-cosine-weighted light that arrived and the light that was there, each summed over 9 x 9
  pixels of the same depth (2%) and facing (cos^16) before they are divided. On CUDA, which has no inline
  rays, there is none.

**The LTC table is fitted on the device.** The published fit's licence file is BSD-like but GitHub
classifies it as "other" (NOASSERTION); unclear, so the table is ours: `ltc_fit.slang` fits Heitz, Dupuy,
Hill and Neubelt's parametrisation (the lobe's mean frame times [[m11, 0, m13], [0, m22, 0], [0, 0, 1]],
Nelder-Mead on the integral of the cubed difference, sampled from both distributions) for GGX with
height-correlated Smith masking, 64 x 64 (roughness, sqrt(1 - cos)), a dispatch a roughness row from the
roughest down, each row starting from the one above. `light::LtcTable` fits it once a process, before the
first frame that needs it.

**A factor of 2 pi.** Hill's rational edge integral returns theta / (2 pi sin theta), not theta / sin theta:
summed it is already the form factor's vector. Taken for the bare one, every closed form came out 1 / (2 pi)
of the quadrature (0.00572 against 0.03594, every case), and the strip's floor read dark.

#### Measured (Metal, M5 Pro)

- The LTC table against quadrature, a rectangle and a GGX lobe over its albedo, four roughnesses (alpha
  0.08 to 0.8) and four angles to the eye: within 9% up to 49 degrees (e.g. 0.3988 against 0.3981, 0.0646
  against 0.0652), 25% at 69 degrees (0.0102 against 0.0136), where an LTC is known to fit worst. The form
  factor against quadrature: 3.6e-6.
- The strip stage (`tests/data/mesh_light_strip.usda`, 384 x 216) against 8192 paths of direct light,
  antialiasing off in both: sampled, 4 a pixel relMSE 6.19e-3, 64 a pixel 3.98e-4 (15.5 times less for 16
  times the samples: no bias); in closed form 5.85e-4.
- A MeshLightAPI quad against a RectLight of the same, the rect path traced: the quad in closed form
  3.37e-5; sampled 64 a pixel 4.41e-5; the rect light in the raster at 64 samples 4.46e-5.
- The showcase (eight strips, a MeshLightAPI lamp, a box; 1024 x 576) in closed form against 1024 paths of
  direct light: relMSE 7.58e-4.
- A still stage drawn twice: 0 words differ.
- An emitter's own triangles are not lit by its cluster: the closed form over a polygon that holds the
  receiving point in its own plane sums to the whole hemisphere, so an emissive quad rasterised read its
  emission plus its albedo times its own radiance (the mapped quad of `emissive_conversions_render_like_the_mesh`:
  mean 0.911 against the path traced 0.782). A point within a thousandth of the rectangle's half size of its
  plane, inside its triangles' box, takes nothing from it, as one in the plane sees it edge on.

#### Not done (stage B)

- UsdLux rect, disk and sphere lights through the same closed form: the plan's "closes LIGHT1 for them
  too". They are still sampled, so that every existing frame stays as it was.
- The cut's hysteresis: a cut is the tile's middle surface's each frame.
- A cluster whose triangles curve is integrated over its plane's rectangle; screens with a varying picture
  are lit by their mean.
- The aggregates' glossy lobes, and their shadows beyond the ratio's two rays.

### Stage C: TX gaussians relit by mesh lights

The splat projection is at its buffers' limit, so what a gaussian reads of the mesh lights is two textures in
the parameter block the sky is already in (`SkyInputs`): the clusters' rectangles (four texels each) and, for
each cell of a 32^3 grid over the relit clouds' box, a cut of up to 4 entries -- each a cluster and the
factor its entry stands for (1, or a tree node's power over its most important cluster's at the cell's
middle). `MeshLights::writeSplats` writes both when the clusters or the box change. The plan cut per chunk of
256 consecutive gaussians; a cut by place needs no pass over the gaussians to make it and is the same for
every cloud, and a chunk of a converted cloud is not a place.

`relitByMeshLights` integrates each entry's rectangle in closed form by the layers `relitByOne` weighs a
light's sample with: the body by the form factor, the horizon clipped by the sphere of the same vector (and,
for what transmits, the form factor seen from behind); the base's reflection and the coat's by the LTC table
at their roughness times their split-sum albedo (the sky's `environmentBrdfOf`); the sheen as a body of its
colour. A TX transfer shadows each entry by its own bits over the cone of that sphere (`splatConeOpen`), and
the bounce is read along the sphere's direction (`splatLightBounce`), once an entry. A cloud whose colours are
light already (`litBody`) is left as it is. What a cloud keeps between frames is keyed on the mesh lights'
revision too.

A first version handed each rectangle to `relitByOne` as a light along the form factor's direction carrying
its whole integral: right for the body, and a chrome ball showed the strip as a round dot.

#### Measured (Metal, M5 Pro)

The balls of tests/data/tx converted with a TX transfer (paint, rubber, chrome; 96130 gaussians each), on
their ground under a 3 x 0.3 strip 2.4 above them, rasterised against the mesh path traced (1024 paths, 6
bounces), 192 x 192; the same strip as a RectLight is what a relit gaussian took before, one sample at its
middle. Cloud shadows off in both raster frames: neither has the ball's shadow on the ground, which is most of
either error.

| | mesh light, closed form | RectLight, middle sample | the mesh rasterised (mesh light) |
|---|---|---|---|
| paint | 0.187 | 0.185 | 0.039 |
| rubber | 0.179 | 0.179 | 0.037 |
| chrome | 0.413 | 1.834 | 0.066 |

#### Not done (stage C)

- A cloud casting a mesh light's shadow onto a mesh (the cloud shadow map's slots are the UsdLux lights'),
  and onto itself beyond its transfer's bits.
- The cache of the view-independent terms (`txCache`): the mesh lights are evaluated every frame.
- The compile-time variant: a cloud without mesh lights runs the same kernel with the loop skipped by a
  constant, not a kernel without it.
- The ray traced route of a frame of splats alone: it has no meshes, so no mesh lights.
- A lamp baked into a cloud's light layer is not told apart from the same lamp as a mesh light.
- The tests the plan named on a converted pawn, K = 4 against K = 64, and the cache's bit-identity.

### Stage D: emission groups and their levels

A mesh's `primvars:athenea:lightGroup` (constant, a string) names its emission group, numbered 1 to 31 as
first met in the engine's life and kept in bits 3 to 7 of its instance records. A group's weight is its
`athenea:lightLevel:<group>` (the delegate reads every such setting), else the lamp rig's weight of a group
of the same name (`setLightWeights`, the car's lamps), else one; it sits in the mesh region's header beside
the output the group's light goes into (`lightGroup:<group>`, 1 + its index among the frame's). The weight
multiplies what an emitter gives off wherever that is evaluated (`meshLightEmission`: the raster's shading,
the path tracer's), and the clusters' power in the refit, so the tree stops choosing a lamp switched off.
A changed level is a header upload and a refit -- no probe, no rebuild. The plan put the weights in
constants every kernel binds; in the header, which every kernel that reads the mesh lights binds already,
they cost no binding and are uploaded the same way.

A cluster's light goes into its group's output: in the raster per cut entry and per sample, shadow
included; in the path tracer, the emission met by a ray and the emission a light step reaches back to the
vertex that chose it. What is seen of the emitter itself goes into its group too, so a frame lit by grouped
emitters alone sums its groups to the beauty -- the amendment above.

#### Measured (Metal, M5 Pro)

- Two strips in groups `a` and `b` over a floor, 96 x 72, nothing else lighting it: the two outputs sum to
  the beauty at all 6912 pixels within 1e-3 (worst 2.3e-7 raster, 2.1e-7 path traced).
- Group `a` at 0.5 against 1 with `b` at 0: none of the 6624 lit pixels other than half, to 1e-3. The change
  of level: no rebuild, one refit, one header upload.
- Both groups at 0 against the same strips with a material that gives off nothing (a sphere light beside in
  both): relMSE 0, max relative 0.

#### Not done (stage D)

- `athenea:lightGroup` on a material, and the MeshLightAPI's own group attribute: the gprim's primvar only.
- A level is one number for the three channels; the lamp rig's weights keep their colour.

### Stage E: the emission groups' indirect light, baked

What a frame computes of a mesh light on a relit gaussian is its direct light (stage C) and one approximate
bounce; the rest -- several bounces, the red a floor sends up onto what stands on it -- is baked once a group
and scaled at run time by the group's level. `mesh2splat --light-groups a,b` traces one more bake through the
conversion's rays with the groups asked for as light group outputs: the tracer already adds each path's light
from a group's emitters into that group's plane of its sums (stage D), so every group is gathered by the same
paths in one pass, and the plain bake's branch now writes those planes' means too. With `groupsIndirect` a
group keeps only what came after a bounce: emission met from the second bounce on, a light step chosen at a
vertex past the first, and none of the UsdLux lights' groups. Each group becomes a layer
`primvars:athenea:splat:lightLayer:emission:<group>` (three floats a gaussian at level 1), the lamp layers'
format, and a frame adds it in `lampLight` at the weight stage D gives the group's emitters (its
`athenea:lightLevel`, else the rig's weight of its name, else one), so a dimmed group dims its direct and its
baked light together. A changed level now also renews the layers' weights.

The plan named a group id on the emitter clusters and per-group accumulators; the light group outputs are
that, already there, and the bake takes them as a frame does. A layer is the group's light where it was baked:
`--skinned` is refused.

`athenea lightmap --light-groups` bakes the atlas with the groups at level 0 and, in one more pass, an atlas
a group (`<name>_emission_<group>.exr`). These hold the group's whole light, direct included, and not its
indirect half as the plan said: a lightmapped mesh is drawn unlit, so nothing else would add the direct light.
`lightmapped.usda` binds the main atlas only.

#### Measured (Metal, M5 Pro)

- Forty points on a white floor by a red wall under two strips, 4096 paths, 3 bounces: groups `a` and `b`
  baked together against both strips baked as one group, indirect only -- none of the 40 apart by 10%
  (worst below 5e-4, the same paths), all 40 lit and red over green by more than 1.5; their whole light
  against the plain bake's colour, the same.
- A white ball beside a strip on a red floor (tests/data/mesh_light_bleed.usda), converted with a TX transfer
  with and without `--light-groups strip` (96130 gaussians; the group bake 68.5 s at 256 paths beside the
  transfer's 82.5 s), 192 x 192 against the mesh path traced (1024 paths, 6 bounces). On the ball, what the
  layer adds is (0.0199, 0.0029, 0.0017) on average against the path tracer's (0.0225, 0.0033, 0.0019) --
  the ball on its red floor less the ball on a black one.
- Level 0.5 against 1: none of 27859 lit pixels other than half, direct and layer together; level 0: no
  pixel lit.
- `athenea lightmap --planar --light-groups strip` over that floor, 128 x 128, 64 paths: the main atlas
  black (the strip is the stage's only light), the strip's atlas red, mean (0.018, 0.0027, 0.0016); the
  group pass 29 s beside the atlas's 34 s.
- On the same ball the frame's direct light is 56% of the path tracer's (green 0.0126 against 0.0226), so
  the ball as a whole is not closer with the layer (relMSE 0.0249 against 0.0237 without): the layer brings
  the red, and the direct light of stage C at this range is what is short.

#### Frame times (Metal, M5 Pro, RelWithDebInfo, 1440 x 810 raster, `athenea stage --frames 40 --no-readback`)

| stage | mesh lights on | `--no-mesh-lights` |
|---|---|---|
| tests/data/mesh_light_strip.usda (sixty strips over a floor) | 10.27 ms | 10.62 ms |
| the TX ball of the bleed test, its layer and the strip (95994 gaussians) | 11.63 ms | 13.57 ms |

With ATHENEA_STAGES on the strip stage: shadow rays 1.4 ms, shading (closed form, cut and filter) 7.2 to
7.5 ms; on the ball, the splat projection with the mesh lights' rectangles 1.1 ms. Mesh lights off, the
emitting triangles are still sampled from the flat table, which is no cheaper.

#### Not done (stage E)

- Stage C's direct light on a gaussian 0.4 units from a strip's edge is short by about half: the cut, the
  transfer's bits over the cone of the equivalent sphere, or both; not yet told apart.
- The lightmap's group atlases are not added at the groups' levels by anything in this engine.
- A radiance-baked cloud (`litBody`) keeps its groups' light in its colours; the layers are for relit clouds.
- The test the plan named on a pawn; the ball stands in for it.

## A volume into volumetric gaussians, and back (VOL103, 31 Oct)

Proposal 103: M9 reads a `.vdb` and only the path tracer draws it; nothing carried a smoke onto the gaussian
route. `athenea vdb2splat` fits a fog volume's extinction with a sum of 3D gaussians, μ_t = Σ σ_i G_i (G_i
of peak one, Condor et al.'s and RayGauss's model), and gives it back onto a grid the path tracer renders
unchanged, which is how the fit is measured today without touching the renderer (proposal 105 §2a).

### The design

**The model is additive, not normalised.** W-VEG's weighted mean Σ w_i v_i G_i / Σ w_i G_i breaks the
closed-form transmittance, so the extinction is the plain sum, and only the attributes (temperature, Cd) are
the density-weighted means Σ c_i σ_i G_i / Σ σ_i G_i, fitted last with the geometry fixed (linear in c).

**A gaussian is its precision's Cholesky factor.** G(x) = exp(−|Aᵀ(x − μ)|² / 2), A lower triangular with a
positive diagonal kept by its log: an evaluation is three dot products, the gradient in A is d_i u_j, and no
eigen-decomposition is needed until the export, which diagonalises M Σ Mᵀ by Jacobi rotations. G stops at
3.5 deviations (G = 0.0022 there), and the fit, the way back and the box a gaussian is culled by are that
one ellipsoid's, so the fit's own error is the way back's.

**The fit is an AOFX effect**, as mesh2splat is (`plugins/vdb2splat`), and the engine lays the grid out for
it: `vsPackLeaves` writes the density's leaves as a picture, 513 entries a leaf, the temperature and Cd read
at the density's voxels through their own trees. The effect needs no tree reader, and the grid's world stays
with the host.

**The initial cut is chosen by error.** Raw moments of every block -- a leaf's 2³, 4³ and 8³ blocks reduced
in group memory over its voxels in Morton order, 16³ and over summed from their children -- give one
gaussian a block (the covariance a voxel box's 1/12 wider). A block's error is what that gaussian alone
leaves of the density, plus the temperature's spread times `--emission-weight`. The cut is the blocks under τ
with every ancestor over it; the host bisects τ on the count. Sharma and Schmalstieg's levels, decided by
error rather than by density.

**Refinement: EM, then Adam, without float atomics.** The forward pass is a group a leaf over the gaussians
whose boxes meet it; whatever a gaussian needs from the voxels is gathered by the gaussian over the voxels of
its box, one group each, reduced in group memory. First 40 EM steps: each gaussian moved to the moments of the
density it is responsible for (ρ w_i / ρ̂), divided by the share of mass and of variance its 3.5-deviation stop
keeps (0.99343, 0.97489), so a step does not shrink what it measures; a mixture that is the grid is a fixed
point. Then 100 Adam steps on (μ, log σ, A) on the L2 loss, the step decaying a hundredfold. The proposal
named Gauss-Newton or Adam alone; Adam alone from the block cut stayed at 0.10 relative L2 on a 16-gaussian
mixture with 64 to fit it, EM then Adam reached 0.016. Densify and prune every 20 iterations: births at the voxels the mixture leaves
most under (the threshold bisected on the count), deaths below 10⁻⁶ of the mass, both through slot lists
compacted in order. Every iteration's writes are the slots' own, so the output order is deterministic.

**What crosses to the processor** is counts: the leaves' box, the cut's count for a τ, the voxels over a
residual threshold, a compaction's total, and the metrics' sums.

**The file.** A ParticleField: the schema's arrays in the grid's world, and `primvars:athenea:volume:sigma`
(half), `:albedo` (color3h), `:temperature` (half), `primvars:athenea:splat:volume`. `radiance:base`'s
opacity is what a standard viewer draws, 1 − exp(−σ √(2π) s) through the middle. The compact layout of the
proposal (23–39 B a gaussian, fp16 relative to the leaf, smallest-three rotation) is 104's.

**The way back** (`VolumeSplats::splatToGrid`) evaluates the mixture at the active voxels of the input's own
topology and writes the values in place; `--back` writes it as a `.vdb` (`io::writeNanoGrids`, NanoVDB to
OpenVDB). A topology of its own -- the gaussians' boxes as bricks -- is not built. `--measure` prints the way back's relative L2 error
over the active voxels and, along random segments of the volume's box, the mixture's closed-form
transmittance (an erf a gaussian) against the mean of ratio-tracking estimates through the input
(`VolumeSplats::rays`, medium.slang's own `mediumTransmittance`).

### How it is checked

The fixtures are made on the device: a box of active voxels (writeVdbBoxes at zero) whose values a kernel
writes -- a known mixture of random gaussians evaluated at the voxel centres, or a smooth noise blob.
`athenea_aofx_tests "[vdb2splat]"` (Metal, debug build):

| Case | Measured | Held to |
|---|---|---|
| one gaussian, a budget of one (40³) | relative L2 3·10⁻⁵ | < 0.005 |
| sixteen gaussians, a budget of 64 (48³) | 0.0114 | < 0.03 |
| the blob (64³), 250 / 1000 / 4000 | 0.100 / 0.063 / 0.038 | falling, the last < 0.25 |
| the fit's own error against the way back's | equal to 10⁻⁹ | < 10⁻³ |
| a mixture's closed-form transmittance against ratio tracking, 2048 rays, 256 estimates each | mean \|ΔT\| 0.0087, none beyond 5 standard errors + 0.01, optical depth up to 3.4 | ≤ 1 in 500 beyond, mean < 0.01 |

`athenea_technique_tests "[vdb2splat]"`: the volume furnace (albedo one under a dome of radiance one) on a
twelve-gaussian mixture given back onto a 32³ box reads 0.99900, 0.94 standard errors from 1.

Two defects the first runs showed: the gradient's last write had four threads read, set and write one float4
each (one component of four kept -- Adam alone then stalled at 0.34 on a 16-gaussian mixture with 64 to fit it and 0.26 with 256 to fit
it); and an EM step whose moments were not a gaussian's ran a box loop for minutes, until a factor's
off-diagonals were held within twice the geometric mean of their diagonals and a box to the cells of the
grid.

  The blob does not improve from 50k to 100k either (0.010 to 0.013), where the cut is saturated -- every
  2³ block with mass is a gaussian, 33 877 of them -- and the rest are births: about nine voxels a gaussian
  is past what the fit uses well.
- The rays' mean |ΔT| (0.02–0.04) is mostly the 64 ratio-tracking estimates' own noise; the count beyond five
  standard errors falls with N (smoke2 344 → 32 of 4096).
- A grid given back has the input's topology, so it costs the path tracer what the original does (117–122 ms
  against 117 for smoke2). The gaussians are 64–66 B each in usdc: smoke2 at 50k is 3.2 MB against 30.5 MB of
  .vdb and 22.6 MB of NanoVDB on the device; the compact 23–39 B layout is proposal 104's.
- The fit's time is linear in N (smoke2: 5 s at 2k, 90 s at 50k, 179 s at 100k): the forward pass visits
  every gaussian a leaf, culled by its box. Binning the gaussians by leaf is what would make it leaves ×
  overlap instead.
- Below half a voxel a gaussian sampled at the voxel centres no longer holds the mass its integral says, and
  the EM step assumes it does: with `minStd` at 0.35 smoke2 stalled at 0.19 by 10k and the blob's error rose
  past 20k; at 0.5 both fell as above.

### What is not done

Sequences (proposal §3.5: advection by `vel`, slots kept between frames), a topology of its own for the way
back, the explosion (temperature) and bunny_cloud volumes (19 M voxels: the leaves' picture and the model
buffer are 1.3 GB at its size), splitting a gaussian over the size cap, binning for the forward pass, and the
raster of the gaussians as a medium (proposal 105).

### The forward pass binned by leaf (31 Oct)

The forward pass walked every slot for every leaf, culled by its box: leaves × gaussians, which made the
fit linear in N. It now walks each leaf's own list: every iteration a thread a gaussian counts the leaves its
box meets (atomics on integers), one group scans the counts in leaf order, a second pass fills the lists, and
a group a leaf sorts its list by slot in group memory (bitonic, up to 2048 entries), so a voxel adds its
gaussians in slot order and the result is the unbinned one to the bit: the fits below gave the same density
errors binned and not, and `athenea_aofx_tests "[vdb2splat]"` the same digits. `--no-bins` keeps the old pass
for a timing. smoke2, release build, the fit end to end (the GPU lock held; whether the Mac was in
interactive use is not known):

| N | unbinned | binned |
|---|---|---|
| 2k | 5.35 s | 2.60 s |
| 10k | 19.80 s | 2.50 s |
| 50k | 90.36 s | 1.97 s |

What is left grows with the gaussians' boxes and the voxels, not with leaves × N. The way back
(`splatToGrid`) and `rays` are still unbinned: they run once a fit.

### `athenea compare --min-alpha`

The relMSE of E1 above was taken over every pixel, most of them background, and Measure's relative error
divides by b² + 0.01, so a dark smoke on a dark ground read under 10⁻⁴ at every N. The Measure effect takes
`minAlpha` (in the uniform block's padding word, so a host that does not send it compares as before): the
differences only where the reference's alpha reaches it. A path traced volume's alpha is the fraction of
camera paths that collided in it, 1 − its transmittance, so 0.01 is where it lets through less than 99 %.
That holds under a sun alone: a visible dome is an opaque background (alpha 1 everywhere). A UsdLux
DistantLight's intensity is a radiance unless `inputs:normalize` is set, so the sun of intensity 3 the first
renders used lit the smoke by about 10⁻⁵; E1b's sun is normalized.

`test_transfer_zonal` (`athenea_aofx_tests "[zonal]"`) fails one assertion (`r[0] == 0`, 769) on the base
commit 5d5aede as on this branch: not this work's.

**Densify where the fit is worst.** Each densify round now gives `--split-share` (0.5) of its new slots to
splitting the gaussians answerable for the most residual -- Σ over their voxels of their share times the
squared residual, gathered with the gradient -- each into two along its longest axis, half a deviation either
side, the pair keeping the one's second moment; the rest are born at the worst voxels as before. smoke2 at
density ×16, the path trace masked to the smoke at 4096 paths (release, M5 Pro):

| | 2k | 10k | 50k | fit |

| before (no splits, 100 Adam steps) | 0.052 | 0.034 | 0.0166 | 2.0 s |
| after (splits, 300 Adam steps) | 0.046 | 0.024 | 0.0060 | 6.2 s |

The density error at 50k goes 0.064 → 0.038; splits alone (100 steps) gave 0.0555, more steps alone 0.055,
both 0.038. The bytes do not change (3.2 MB at 50k). The default stays 100 steps; 300 is what reaches 1 %.

**The explosion** (openvdb.org, 3.9 M voxels, density and temperature; its `v` is not read): density relative

| | mean density L2 | at frame 29 | mean flicker | at frame 29 | slots | mean move a frame | fit a frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Adam's are off in a warm frame: on a frame given twice, ten EM steps from the Adam-refined gaussians took the
error from 0.044 to 9.5, while Adam alone took it to 0.035; why EM is unstable there is not settled.

## A medium of gaussians in the raster (VOL105, 31 Oct)

Proposal 105 §3: the gaussians `athenea vdb2splat` writes (VOL103) drawn by the raster as the medium they are,
in the same sort as every other splat; the path tracer stays the reference.

### The design

**A medium is a cloud that carries a sigma a gaussian.** `primvars:athenea:splat:volume` and
`primvars:athenea:volume:sigma` on a ParticleField make `CloudLoader::uploadVolume` pack sigma, the temperature
and the albedo two words a gaussian (`GpuSplats::volume`); the file's `opacities` are not read, since validation
drops what is under 1/255 and a smoke is made of faint gaussians. The medium's constants -- the Volume's
`athenea:densityScale`, `athenea:albedo`, `athenea:anisotropy`, and an emission -- are primvars on the field and
ride on the instance (`render::SplatVolume`).

**Alpha is the exact optical depth of the pixel's ray.** With U the upper Cholesky factor of the precision in the
view and c the centre, for the pixel's ray r = ((x − cx)/fx, (y − cy)/fy, 1): u = U r, m = U c,
t* = u·m / |u|², d² = |t* u − m|², and τ = densityScale σ |r| ∫ G dt over the chord the 3.5-deviation ellipsoid
cuts from the ray -- exp(−d²/2) √(π/2a) [erf(k(t₁ − t*)) − erf(k(t₀ − t*))], a = |u|², k = √(a/2) -- clipped at
the camera and at the opaque layer under the splats, so smoke standing on a ground is integrated up to the ground.
α = 1 − exp(−τ). The record carries U (six floats), m and the peak extinction in fields the blend already loads
(the conic's w, the colour, the surfel words and the slot's `slopes` entry), marked `kVolumeMark`: no buffer
more, and the blend's other branches untouched. The transmittance is a product, so the order the depth sort puts
overlapping gaussians in changes how their radiances are weighed and never how much light gets through; with one
radiance for the whole medium (emission alone) the frame does not depend on the order at all.

**The tiles are the image of the ellipsoid**, the conic (cᵀPc − k)P − (Pc)(Pc)ᵀ in the ray's coordinates at the
level k where the optical depth falls under 1/1024 of the peak (or 3.5 deviations), a tenth wider than the cut,
so the float arithmetic of a far gaussian loses no pixel the blend would draw. A gaussian across the camera's
plane takes every tile. Where the record's centre is behind the opaque layer the walk does not stop at it: its
chord may still reach in front.

**The export lost the faint gaussians.** `vdb2splat`'s ParticleField was written through the cloud decode, which
drops a record of opacity under 1/255 and wrote its shape as zeros beside its sigma: of the 50k gaussians of the
smoke2 fit of E1b's densify round (`--density-scale` 1), 30 577 had scales (0, 0, 0). The grids given back were
right (they come from the device records), the files were not. The opacity written for a standard viewer is now
held at 1/254, and the E1 fits below were made again.

### Measured

Emission-absorption alone (albedo 0, a uniform emission of 1, no light): the medium sends L(1 − T) along a ray
whatever its order, so the raster and the path tracer through the grid the same gaussians give back must agree.
`athenea_usd_tests "[vdb2splat][raster]"`, a 12-gaussian mixture inside a 32³ box, 160 × 120, the path tracer at
2048 paths: mean 0.10486 against 0.10544, relMSE 9.1·10⁻⁴ over the frame (held to 5·10⁻³). The 8-bit p99 is 12
codes, the paths' noise in faint pixels once sRGB-encoded, and is not held.

### Light, shadows both ways, and the black body

**The radiance is baked a gaussian a frame** (`technique::VolumeSplatShading`, one dispatch a medium before the
raster, under a millisecond for 50k): the emission -- a constant, and a black body at the gaussian's temperature
from a table built on the device (Planck through Wyman's fit of the CIE curves, normalised to luminance one, times
σ_SB T⁴/π·10⁻⁶ as Cycles' Principled Volume scales it); each light's single scattering, Henyey-Greenstein at the
eye's direction from the centre, through the transmittance the cloud shadow map gives at the centre; a dome's
colour times the mean transmittance of the map's six dome directions; and Wrenninge's octaves for what scatters
more than once (`athenea:volume:octaves`, 4 by default: extinction towards the light, energy and anisotropy halved
at each). For a distant light the transmittance is the mean of three readings along the light through the
gaussian (Gauss-Hermite at −√3, 0, √3 deviations): a transmittance is convex in the depth, and read at the centre
alone a wide gaussian went dark.

**The medium casts into the map and reads it, in terms of its own.** A medium's gaussian adds its line integral
along the light into the texels of its 2D footprint -- the peak σ√(2π)√det Σ / √det Σ₂, the footprint the one a
surface's gaussian has there -- and its Fourier terms with it (`splat_shadow_volume.slang`). First into the
surfaces' words: the pawn behind the smoke then lost its lit side (the nearest caster in its texels was the smoke,
2 % of the slab is a few units of a dense smoke, and the step its own body is rang through the series) and went
dark, and the smoke's front was lit through the same bias. Now a texel keeps a medium's total and three Fourier
pairs after the surfaces' words (`ShadowMapJob::mediumCoefficients`, the count in the header's coefficients word,
second byte), a receiver's transmittance is the surfaces' read as before times the medium's at its depth, and the
transmittance chain a far floor reads is of both totals. A frame of splats alone builds the map where a medium is
among them. The medium's reach -- its centres' box widened by 3.5 widest deviations, reduced on the device -- is
what the map is sized from: the centres' box alone cut the far edge of a small mixture's shadow.

### Measured: E1 (proposal §6)

`volraster_e1.sh`, release build, Apple M5 Pro, one GPU job at a time under the shared lock
(other sessions' jobs queued between ours; whether the Mac was in interactive use is not known). The same
volume by three routes: (a) the path trace of the original grid, the truth; (b) the path trace of the grid its
gaussians give back; (c) the raster drawing the gaussians as a medium. A grey ground (a mesh), a normalized sun
of irradiance 3 at 40° and a dome of 0.1; the pawn twice beside it, as its meshes in (a) and (b) and as its TX
cloud in (c) -- A in the volume's shadow, B between the sun and the volume's foot. 1024², the path traces at 1024
paths and 8 bounces. The fits were made again after the export fix: smoke2 at 50k with splits and 300 Adam steps
(density relative L2 0.038), density scale 80 (E1b's ×4); the explosion at 50k (0.037), density scale 0.5.
Masked relMSE (`athenea compare`, PSNR in brackets): the smoke where the original, alone under the sun, has
alpha ≥ 0.01; the shadow where (a) is under 0.9 of the scene without the volume, the pawns' and the volume's
pixels left out.

| | smoke2: smoke | shadow | explosion: smoke | shadow |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (b) grid given back against (a) | 3.0·10⁻⁴ (45.8 dB) | 4.4·10⁻⁴ (44.4) | 2.4·10⁻⁴ (46.7) | 5.9·10⁻⁵ (52.6) |
| (c) raster, 4 octaves, against (a) | 0.025 (25.1) | 0.0094 (30.5) | 0.031 (24.2) | 0.0084 (31.0) |

| emission-absorption, (c) against (a) | 0.0047 (33.7) | -- | 0.0022 (36.6) | -- |
| emission-absorption, (b) against (a) | 0.0068 (30.9) | -- | 0.0018 (36.6) | -- |

Pawn A's mean with the volume over its mean without (the volume's shadow on it): 0.837 path traced, 0.787

original it is as close as the grid given back is (smoke2 nearer, 0.0047 against 0.0068: the grid samples the
gaussians at its voxels, the raster integrates them). The lit smoke misses what the path tracer's 8 bounces carry
off the ground and between the smoke's own gaussians beyond Wrenninge's octaves; its shadow on the ground is
within 1 % relMSE. The proposal's bars (1 % emission-absorption, 3 % single scattering) are met but for the
explosion's single scattering at 3.1 %.

ms a frame (1024², medians; the raster of 30 frames with no readback, the path trace of 5 frames of 64 paths):

| | raster, whole scene | raster, volume and ground alone | path trace, 64 paths, whole scene | the same, volume and ground alone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| smoke2 | 135.7 | 18.1 | 14 829 | 4 236 |
| explosion | 160.4 | 17.4 | 19 753 | 7 115 |

The whole scene's raster is the two pawns' TX clouds (1.6 M gaussians each); the medium, its shading and the
ground with the map are 17–18 ms, against 4.2–7.1 s for 64 paths of the path tracer (1024 paths are sixteen
times that). Sizes: the clouds are 3.05 MB (smoke2) and 3.15 MB (the explosion) in usdc, against 29.1 and
74.9 MB of `.vdb` and 22.6 and 23.0 MB of NanoVDB on the device; the cloud on the device is about 2 MB
(positions, shape and the medium's two words, 40 B a gaussian).

The test, `athenea_usd_tests "[vdb2splat][raster]"`: the 12-gaussian mixture under the sun over the ground,
single scattering (`octaves` 1) against the path tracer with no bounce: mean 0.2171 against 0.2239 (the ground
alone 0.2561), relMSE 0.013 over the frame (held to 0.03).

### What is not done

`UsdVol` turned into a medium on load (proposal §5: `HdAtheneaVolume` running vdb2splat, cached beside the
`.vdb`); the path tracer's own medium of gaussians (§2b) -- a medium cloud in a traced frame of splats alone is
left out, and composited by the raster where there are meshes; moments for an order-independent blend (§3, b) and
the flicker of the sort in an orbit; light bounced off a ground or a cloud into the medium (the path tracer's 8
bounces have it, and it is a large share of a smoke over a lit floor); a textured dome's image (a medium takes
its colour); a medium's shadow into a TX cloud's baked transfer (it multiplies the direct term through the map,
as an animated caster does); edits, levels of detail and `.athc` for a medium; the path tracer's emission from a
temperature field, without which the explosion's fire has no truth to be measured against; an orthographic
camera. A cloud drawn twice shares one radiance buffer, baked for the last instance's place. The [mips] case of
`athenea_usd_tests` (a floor four texels a pixel from the map, p99 26 against 8) fails the same on the base's
shadow-map code, built from this branch before the medium's terms: not this work's.

### After the volumes merge: the voxel's point, and E1 timed again (1 Nov)

The merge of `volumes` up to e5fec07 brought the trilinear lookup (cdff1cf), in which a voxel's value stands at
its index point ijk, OpenVDB's convention; the medium read the voxel a point fell in before, which put the value
at ijk + 0.5, and the fit was written to that: a voxel ijk spans [ijk, ijk + 1) and its value sits at its centre.
`athenea_aofx_tests "[vdb2splat]"` caught it -- the closed-form transmittance against ratio tracking went from a
mean |ΔT| of 0.0087 to 0.0171, 63 rays of 2048 beyond five standard errors against at most 4 -- half a voxel of
shift between the mixture and the medium it is measured through. The fit keeps its frame (the gaussians' records
are in index space plus half a voxel, `kVoxelCentre`), and the two places that leave it subtract the half voxel:
the closed form in `vsRays` and the world positions `vsExport` writes, so a ParticleField now stands where the
path tracer draws the grid. A grid given back is on the input's own topology and is read the same way as the
original, so the path traces of E1 do not depend on it. With it the case reads mean |ΔT| 0.0087 again.

E1's headline again on the merged branch (release, Apple M5 Pro, the shared GPU lock held, whether the Mac was
in interactive use not known; `vdb2splat_opt0.sh`). The fit is the median of three runs; the
