### The fit's time, kernel by kernel (1 Nov)

`--profile` waits for every kernel and prints each one's time (a breakdown: the waits make the fit some 15 %
slower than it is). At 50k and 300 Adam steps on smoke2 the kernels' 6.95 s were the gradient (`v2sBackward`, a
group of 64 a gaussian) 43 %, the forward pass 34 %, the births' bisection (24 counted passes a densify round
over every voxel) 5 %, building the leaves' lists every iteration 11 %. What was tried, each measured on its own
(`vdb2splat_opt1*.sh`; release, M5 Pro, the shared GPU lock, the Mac's interactive use not
known; the fit the median of three runs):

| change | smoke2 50k / 300 steps | relative L2 | kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (the merged branch) | 6.36 s | 0.03767 | |
| the gradient a wave of 32 a (gaussian, leaf) pair, over the voxels of the leaf inside its box, then each gaussian's pairs added in its own order | 6.38 | 0.03773 | became the next |
| and the lists kept over iterations, built over boxes widened by 2 voxels until one leaves its cells | 6.81 | 0.03773 | no: the lists are longer, the forward pass slower than the builds saved |
| the gradient summed by the forward pass's own group, the mixture in its registers, each pair reduced over the group | 7.37 / 6.34 (second form) | 0.03766 | no: a reduction a gaussian a wave costs what the reads saved |
| the forward pass's chunk walked to its entries, not its room (a leaf's list holds some forty gaussians and the loop ran 256) | 6.45 | 0.03773 | yes |
| a wave of the forward pass a 4³ block, a gaussian whose box misses it passed over; the exponential behind a branch; the attributes' sums only in the attribute steps | (in the line above) | bit for bit | yes |
| the births' threshold from two histograms of 2048 bins (the whole range, then the bin the count crosses in) instead of 24 counted passes | | | yes: `v2sUnder` 360 → 0 ms of the profile |
| eight bytes a voxel (rho^, rho) for what reads the mixture back -- the gradient, the births -- instead of the voxel's 16 and the model's 32 | 5.31 | 0.03773 | yes |
| the gradient a thread a pair, its voxels one after another | 5.21 | 0.03772 | yes (the explosion: 2.80 → 3.13 s, its large gaussians a thread's long loop) |
| no box check when the lists are rebuilt anyway (slack 0): 351 readbacks fewer | 5.24 | 0.03772 | yes; the readbacks cost nothing measurable |
| `--checkerboard`: each Adam step's gradient over the voxels of one parity, alternating, counted twice | 3.98 | 0.03949 | as an option: 4.7 % more error |
| the gradient's pairs split over 2 / 4 / 8 threads, each a run of the leaf's x rows (no thread on a whole leaf) | 5.31 / 5.49 / 5.98 | 0.0377 | no: the gradient's kernel 2.85 → 2.39 s at 8, its gather 0.25 → 1.49 s |

The fits after, against before (median of three each):

| | before s | after s | after, `--checkerboard` | relative L2 before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| smoke2 10k, 100 steps | 2.66 | 1.39 | | 0.1227 → 0.1226 |
| smoke2 50k, 100 steps | 2.44 | 1.84 | | 0.0620 → 0.0622 |
| smoke2 10k, 300 steps | 6.57 | 4.18 | | 0.1002 → 0.1002 |
| smoke2 50k, 300 steps | 6.36 | 5.21 | 3.98 (0.0395) | 0.0377 → 0.0377 |
| smoke2 100k, 300 steps | 6.75 | 5.73 | | 0.0233 → 0.0228 |
| explosion 50k, 100 steps | 3.85 | 3.13 | 2.66 (0.0369) | 0.0367 → 0.0367 |

Masked path traces (E1b's, 4096 paths) of the grids given back, after: smoke2 50k / 300 steps ×1 6.4·10⁻⁴ (6.4·10⁻⁴
before), ×16 5.9·10⁻³ (5.8·10⁻³), the explosion 5.3·10⁻⁴ (5.3·10⁻⁴); with `--checkerboard` 6.9·10⁻⁴, 6.2·10⁻³,
5.3·10⁻⁴. The bytes do not change (3.20 MB at 50k). `--no-bins` still runs the old gradient and forward pass
(smoke2 10k: 27.6 s, 0.1227). The sums are added in another order than before, so a fit is no longer the
previous one to the bit but to its error; a fit is still the same from run to run.

The target was half of 6.2 s at 50k and 300 steps with the error kept; the kept changes reach 5.21 s (−18 %), the
checkerboard 3.98 s (−37 %) at 4.7 % more density error. What is left: the gradient is 47 % of the kernels'
time and the forward pass 26 %, each a few dozen voxels of a leaf for every gaussian whose box meets it,
rebuilt every iteration (the lists' builds 13 %). Neither is limited by reading memory any more nor by the
readbacks; the evaluation itself is what is left.

On CUDA (an RTX 3070 Laptop under Windows, the vol-stream branch built there, its interactive use not known):
`athenea_aofx_tests "[vdb2splat]"` passes with Metal's digits (16 gaussians 0.00940, the blob 0.09861 / 0.06186
/ 0.03619, the rays' mean |ΔT| 0.00655, none beyond); smoke2 at 50k fits in 2.02 s at 100 steps (0.0623), 5.89 s
at 300 (0.03765) and 5.14 s with `--checkerboard` (0.0399), one run each, against the M5 Pro's 1.84 / 5.21 / 3.98.

The fit's knobs one at a time, then together, on smoke2 at 50k (`vdb2splat_opt2sweep*.sh`, one

target 0.030 within 1 %; the error of 50k gaussians before is reached by 40k (−20 % gaussians and bytes). The
defaults are not changed: `densifyEvery` counts iterations, so the same 80 leaves a warm sequence frame (30 steps)
no round at all, and the small fixtures of `athenea_aofx_tests` are not refitted with it; the schedule is
`--iterations 520 --checkerboard --init-fraction 0.7 --densify-every 80 --split-share 1 --max-block 32`. The
100-step line says the defaults themselves would gain (better and faster on smoke2), which wants the densify
rounds given as a count rather than a period first. Why EM after Adam diverges on a warm frame is not looked at
here.

## A volume sequence as video planes (vol-stream, 1 Nov)

`vol-raster` with `web-athv-video` merged in: a vdb2splat sequence -- warm frames, every gaussian in its slot,
carried by the grid's `vel` -- written as the `.athv` the sparrow's route streams, a ladder of budgets, and
decoded back into a medium the path tracer and the raster draw.

**The merge.** The two branches had each reshaped `lod::StreamingPool`: vol-raster with one store shared by
every streamed prim (`StreamingShare`, the payload joined), web-athv-video with chunk sources and live epochs.
The live sources' pool is kept; the shared store was not ported to it in the merge (Engine opened a store a
prim, as before the share, and its test was taken out; it is back since, below), and the curvature bit (6) of the `.athc`, the cut's residency count and the cut
of a live cloud (copied whole, in the instances' order: placed among the batched cuts it was taken for one of
them and the frame read past them) are carried over. `athenea_lod_tests` (bar the transfer case below),
`athenea_video_tests`, `athenea_volume_tests`, `athenea_usd_tests "[live]"`, `"[volume]"` and `"[vdb2splat]"`
pass (the live soak below aside).

**A medium's gaussian as a splat.** `vdb2splat --sequence --cloud f_####.ply` writes each frame's slots as 3DGS
splats (`vsExportPly`): place, deviations and rotation in the world, the albedo as the base colour, and the
medium's own values in the first rest coefficients of red -- ln σ in `f_rest_0` (held over −10, where a dead
slot sits as a speck at the origin, so a frame keeps every slot and the planes' range is not stretched), the
temperature in `f_rest_1`. `video-encode --each-a-frame` takes the files as a sequence (stable order, the
lossless geometry layer for place, scale and rotation, the rest through the HEVC luma planes, degree 1, 8 bits,
no chroma: colour in chroma averages four splats, which would average ln σ). `vdb2splat --sequence --from-athv`
decodes the video frame by frame through the hardware decoder and the planes kernels into a store
(`AthvFrames`, video-decode's loop) and `vsImportSplats` turns each splat back into a record -- the covariance
pulled into index space, its precision's Cholesky factor, σ = exp(f_rest_0) -- which is then given back and
judged as a fit is; `-o` writes the decoded frames as ParticleFields for the raster.

**Measured** (`volstream_e1.sh`, `volstream_e2run.sh`, `volstream_pt.sh`; release, M5 Pro,
VideoToolbox, the shared GPU lock, the Mac's interactive use not known). The blob-sequence fixture at 128³
(voxel 0.05, 30 frames, the blob carried by a known flow), its density as NanoVDB 17.1 MB a frame (2.4 MB as
`.vdb`); the ladder fitted warm at four budgets, encoded at quality 0.9, 30 frames a second, a geometry key every
30. Density relative L2 over the active voxels and flicker, means over the 30 frames; the f32 cloud is the fit's,
"decoded" what the video gives back:

| rung | MB a frame | Mbit/s at 24 / 30 | video / geometry layer MB | L2 f32 | L2 decoded | L2 decoded against f32 | flicker f32 / decoded | fit s a frame (warm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50k | 0.487 | 93.5 / 116.9 | 0.024 / 0.462 | 0.0193 | 0.0230 | 0.0111 | 0.251 / 0.278 | 0.19 |
| 20k | 0.196 | 37.6 / 47.0 | 0.010 / 0.186 | 0.0225 | 0.0244 | 0.0090 | 0.274 / 0.287 | 0.12 |
| 10k | 0.101 | 19.4 / 24.3 | 0.005 / 0.096 | 0.0234 | 0.0247 | 0.0079 | 0.273 / 0.280 | 0.10 |
| 5k | 0.053 | 10.1 / 12.6 | 0.003 / 0.050 | 0.0282 | 0.0288 | 0.0062 | 0.311 / 0.313 | 0.09 |
| 20k, quality 0.95 | 0.200 | 38.4 / 48.1 | 0.014 / 0.186 | | 0.0233 | 0.0058 | 0.281 | |
| 20k, geometry 11 / 8 / 8 bits | 0.130 | 25.0 / 31.3 | 0.010 / 0.121 | | 0.0256 | 0.0118 | 0.303 | |
| 20k, quality 0.6 | 0.188 | 36.1 / 45.1 | 0.002 / 0.186 | | 0.0730 | 0.0684 | 0.492 | |

Per picture (medians): planes laid 1.0–1.7 ms, encoded 2.3–3.7 ms, decoded by the hardware 1.0–2.2 ms and turned
back into gaussians 1.4–2.2 ms; the geometry layer's position error 33–36 µm (a voxel is 5 cm), rotation under

0.9 the video adds 3–20 % to the fit's density error and the geometry layer is 95 % of the bytes -- 9.3 B a
gaussian a frame at 50k, against 1 B for all the luma planes. 20k gaussians a frame stream at 47 Mbit/s against
17.1 MB a frame of NanoVDB (87 times) or 2.4 MB of `.vdb` (12 times).

Frame 15 path traced (E1b's light, 4096 paths, 512², masked where the original lets through less than 99 %) and
the decoded gaussians drawn by the raster as a medium, against the original's path trace:

| rung | PT, grid from the f32 cloud | PT, grid from the decoded video | raster of the decoded medium | raster ms a frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50k | 9.7·10⁻⁵ (51.4 dB) | 1.05·10⁻⁴ (51.2) | 0.030 (26.7) | 9.3 |
| 20k | 2.9·10⁻⁴ (46.7) | 2.9·10⁻⁴ (46.6) | 0.026 (27.3) | 9.2 |

(the original's path trace: 87.8 ms for 64 paths). The raster's error is its own lighting model's (single
scattering and octaves against 4 bounces, as in VOL105's E1), not the video's.

**Not done.** A real sequence (no animated `.vdb` was at hand: the explosion and smoke2 are single frames); the
NanoVDB Fp4/Fp8 of the same frames (only the f32 grid's size is compared); the rungs' keys aligned by rendition
in a ladder index (each rung is its own `.athv`, keys at the same frames because every rung keeps 30); the
geometry in the video (`--geometry-video`) for volumes. The
`.athc` transfer case crashed on reading back after the merge -- the live sources' chunk format did not carry
the curvature word, so the reader sliced a level's block short; it does now, and `athenea_lod_tests` passes
whole (37 cases). The live soak of `athenea_usd_tests "[live]"` (`test_live_qa`, epochs shown against epochs
pushed over a timed run) passed once and failed once on its last count, under the background priority the
GPU jobs run at; not followed.

**The shared store on the live sources' pool** (`vol-stream-share`). `lod::StreamingShare` is back, added to
the pool the live sources shaped rather than the other way round. A pool opened with a share takes no store of
its own; the first `cloud()` after a pool joined or left lays one out for all of them -- slots for the sum of
their budgets, made as the first pool's own store would be, the others taking its buffers and keeping their own
chunk flags and levels -- and every chunk leaves it. The payload is not joined to the levels as it was in
vol-raster: a pool of its own does not join it on this branch either, and a cut reads the store's extras by slot
and the levels' where they are. The first pool's update after the wants does every pool's: the chunks wanted,
most wanted first whichever pool's, against the store's cheapest slots, as one pool's update does. Each pool
keeps its loaders, its staging ring and its fence; a placement and the eviction it makes are recorded in the
placing pool's batch, submitted against that pool's fence, and a slot is placed at most once an update, so the
batches' order does not matter. A pool's `bytesPerFrame` holds for what it places. A frame that places nothing
submits nothing, `wait` or not. The engine opens every file-backed streamed prim into one share; a file laid out
unlike the others (another `ChunkFormat`) falls back to a store of its own. A live source is refused a share and
keeps its own store: its epochs are built in slots beside the one shown and flip whole, and a slot another cloud
may take at any frame would leave an epoch half placed. The test is back (`athenea_lod_tests "a .athc reads back*"`, "two clouds share one store, and the nearer has the
slots"): two copies of a cloud, one thirty units behind the other, each with the 8 slots that alone left chunks
missing -- the near one takes 13 of the 16 and the far one none in 2 rounds, as on vol-raster, and the frame after
adds no host wait. `athenea_lod_tests` passes whole (37 cases).
## NVENC: the video planes' encoder on CUDA (31 Oct)

`athenea video-encode` on Linux and Windows: NVIDIA's hardware HEVC encoder behind the same `VideoEncoder` as
VideoToolbox (`modules/video/src/Nvenc.cpp`), so the planes, the `.athv` and everything that reads it are unchanged.

### Design

- **Nothing linked.** The encoder library (`nvEncodeAPI64.dll`, `libnvidia-encode.so.1`) and the CUDA driver
  (`nvcuda.dll`, `libcuda.so.1`) are opened at run time by `platform::SharedLibrary` (new: `LoadLibraryA` /
  `dlopen`), `NvEncodeAPIGetMaxSupportedVersion` checked against the headers' API (12.2, a driver of 550.54.14 /
  551.76 or newer), then `NvEncodeAPICreateInstance`. A build runs where there is no NVIDIA driver; the factory
  says `Unsupported` with the reason. The types are FFmpeg's nv-codec-headers (`n12.2.72.0`, MIT), vendored in
  `third_party/nv-codec-headers`: `nvEncodeAPI.h` and `dynlink_cuda.h`, for the few CUDA driver entry points.
- **On the engine's context.** `EncoderSettings::device` (new) is the engine's device; on CUDA the session opens on
  its own `CUcontext` (`Device::native()`, the one gpu_host adopts) and copies on its stream. Without a device, or
  on Vulkan, it opens on the first device's primary context and takes host samples only.
- **The planes never reach the CPU.** The input is one pitched allocation (`cuMemAllocPitch`, luma then the second
  plane, NV12 or P010) registered once as `NV_ENC_INPUT_RESOURCE_TYPE_CUDADEVICEPTR` and mapped for each picture.
  `VideoEncoder::encodeDevice` (new; `takesDevice()` says where it works) takes a `DevicePicture` -- the
  buffers PlanesCodec laid the mosaic in (`EncodedPlanes::lumaDevice`, `chromaDevice`) -- and copies them in on the
  device (`cuMemcpy2DAsync`, device to device); `PlanesCodec::encode(..., readPlanes = false)` then skips the
  planes' read back. The host-span `encode` stays, the same copy from the host. Grey chroma is a `cuMemsetD8` /
  `D16` once, while no chroma is given.
- **What VideoToolbox gives.** HEVC Main (Main 10 at 10 bits), 4:2:0, `videoFullRangeFlag` 1 in the VUI (ffprobe:
  `color_range=pc`, `yuvj420p`), preset P4 with the high-quality tuning (low latency for `realTime`), B pictures,
  look-ahead and adaptive quantisation off: a frame in, its picture out, synchronously. `gopLength` and
  `idrPeriod` are the key interval and every key is forced IDR with its parameter sets; NVENC's Annex B is split
  into 4-byte lengths and the VPS, SPS and PPS go to `parameterSets`, as VideoToolbox's format description holds
  them. Constant quality is constant QP, `round(51 x (1 - quality))` for I and P (VideoToolbox's quality has no QP
  to map to; this is linear in the setting); a bit rate is VBR, the peak twice the average.
- **Checked where it cannot be decoded.** There is no NVDEC yet, so `--check` on Linux and Windows is refused,
  saying so. `video-encode --units FILE.athv` (new) replays another machine's units in place of the encoder: the
  NVENC file goes through VideoToolbox's decoder and the planes decode on the Mac, against the same source frames
  laid on the Mac. A pages directory now takes `.ply` pages where there is no `.spz`, because the Windows build
  has no zstd and so reads no SPZ: both machines read the same PLY pages.
- **A Windows build fix on the way:** `AttributeError::far` is `farSplats`; `far` is a macro under `windows.h`.

### Measured

The sparrow's flattened pages, frames 0-29 (300847 splats a frame, degree 3), as 3DGS PLY (converted from the SPZ
pages with Niantic's library, so both machines read the same values): 59 planes in a 4608 x 4480 mosaic, a key
picture every 30, Morton order a frame, group ranges, high parts beside. NVENC on an RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (Windows,
driver 621.01, CUDA device); VideoToolbox on the M5 Pro. Neither machine was known to be idle: whether either
was in interactive use is not known, and the Mac's jobs ran one at a time under the GPU guard. Times are
`video-encode`'s medians a picture, release builds. `lay` is the planes kernels with what is read back (on the Mac
the mosaic too; on CUDA only the ranges and side data); `encode` is the encoder call (NVENC: the device copy, the
encode, the lock). Errors are `--check`'s means in steps of each attribute's own quantisation (position: of the 16
bit one), through VideoToolbox's decoder on the Mac (NVENC's through `--units`), and the geometry error's median /
p99 position.

| 400 Mbit/s | VideoToolbox | 2.881 (2.678 + 0.203) | 691 | 11.6 | 53.5 | 14.3 / 10.2 / 8.29 / 12.6 / 9.20 / 10.3 | 79 / 244 |

- **At one bit rate NVENC is the better codec for planes**: 7 % fewer bytes than VideoToolbox and every
  attribute nearer (opacity 4.25 against 10.2 steps, position 10.2 against 14.3). By the quality ladder the same
  holds: NVENC at QP 36 (1.25 MB of video) is about as near as VideoToolbox at 0.5 (1.65 MB) on position and
  rotation and nearer on the rest. Neither holds the 400 Mbit/s asked over 30 pictures (the key picture is 8.5 MB
  on NVENC and 12.1 MB on VideoToolbox).
- **The settings do not mean the same.** NVENC's QP at a given `--quality` spends 1.6-2.5 times VideoToolbox's
  bytes; matching a VideoToolbox file's size takes about 0.1 less quality. A file's `quality` field says what was
  asked, not what either encoder made of it.
- **Encode time is the same order**: 37-76 ms a 4608 x 4480 picture on the laptop's NVENC, 51-72 ms on the M5
  Pro, both rising with the bits made. The device input saves the CPU's part: the same planes from host spans
  (a Vulkan device, so the planes go through the CPU: quality 0.4) took 68.5 ms to encode against 40.5 from
  device memory, and laying them 128 ms with the read back against 1.3 without.
- **The largest errors through `--units` are not the codec's.** NVENC's maxima stay at 115 position, 247
  opacity, 180 log scale and 214-216 rotation steps from QP 36 down to QP 0 (quality 1.0: 16.08 MB of video a
  frame, 115 ms; means 0.41 / 0.098 / 0.33 / 0.34 / 0.29 / 0.48 steps, positions 2.3 / 6.4 um), where
  VideoToolbox's own maxima fall with its quality (19-36 steps at 0.7). A few splats take another Morton rank on
  the Mac than they did on CUDA, so a decoded sample is measured against a neighbour: the order is computed again
  on each machine, and the means and percentiles are what to read across machines. A VideoToolbox file replayed
  through `--units` on its own machine gives its own `--check` figures to the last digit.
- **10 bits and colour in chroma** (quality 0.5; 10-bit errors in steps of the 10-bit and 20-bit quantisation):

### Densify rounds as a count, and the smallest deviation (1 Nov, round 2)

**Rounds as a count.** `--densify-rounds n` (the effect's `densifyRounds`) places round k after
floor(k x iterations / (n + 3)) of the iterations (EM and Adam together), none after 70 % as before, so the
schedule scales with the budget: 4 rounds over the default 140 iterations fall after 20, 40, 60 and 80 -- the
default's own -- and over 560 after 80, 160, 240 and 320, round 1's recipe. 0 (the default) keeps
`--densify-every`. A sequence's warm frames take their own period, `--warm-densify-every` (20, what they had), so
neither a count nor a long period of the full fit reaches them. Release, M5 Pro, the shared GPU lock, the Mac's
interactive use not known (`vdb2splat_r2a.sh`, median of three):

| | defaults (100 steps) s / L2 | recipe, every 80 s / L2 | recipe, 4 rounds s / L2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| blob 96³ 10k | 0.40 / 0.02691 | 1.03 / 0.01891 | 1.04 / 0.01891 |
| blob 50k | 0.46 / 0.01191 | 1.06 / 0.00115 | 1.05 / 0.00115 |
| smoke2 10k | 1.38 / 0.12261 | 4.79 / 0.09397 | 4.80 / 0.09397 |
| smoke2 50k | 1.83 / 0.06218 | 6.35 / 0.03038 | 6.35 / 0.03038 |
| explosion 10k | 2.20 / 0.07961 | 5.75 / 0.06118 | 5.75 / 0.06118 |
| explosion 50k | 3.12 / 0.03673 | 8.73 / 0.02408 | 8.73 / 0.02408 |

(the recipe: `--iterations 520 --checkerboard --init-fraction 0.7 --split-share 1 --max-block 32`). The count
gives the period's results to the digit. smoke2 50k at 300 steps: every 20 (11 rounds) 5.27 s / 0.03772, 4
rounds 5.62 s / 0.03680, 11 rounds as a count 6.06 s / 0.03802.

The blob sequence (128³, 30 frames, 20k, warm), mean over the frames:

| | frame 0 L2 | mean L2 | flicker | fit s a frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| defaults | 0.0199 | 0.02244 | 0.274 | 0.11 |
| recipe, every 80, warm frames every 80 (round 1's worry) | 0.0110 | 0.02378 | 0.293 | 0.16 |
| recipe, every 80, warm frames every 20 | 0.0110 | 0.02378 | 0.293 | 0.16 |
| recipe, 4 rounds | 0.0110 | 0.02378 | 0.293 | 0.16 |
| 520 steps, cut 0.7, 4 rounds (splits and blocks as default) | 0.0095 | 0.02285 | 0.283 | 0.15 |

A warm frame loses nothing to a long period here: it keeps every slot (none is pruned, so a round has no free
slot to give), and the rows with and without its rounds are the same. The recipe's better first frame does not
carry: the sequence's mean is worse (0.0238 against 0.0224), so the recipe is not made the default -- it is 3.5
times the fit's time, and the sequence is no better. Why is the next paragraph.

**The smallest deviation.** A warm frame's start is the frame before carried by the flow. On the fixture with a
rise alone of 1.5 voxels a frame, the carried start with no step after it (one step of rate 0) is as far from the
grid as no carrying at all on frames 1 and 3 (0.148 against 0.143) and exactly the first frame's error on frames 2
and 4 (0.019876): moved by a whole number of voxels the mixture matches, by a half it does not. The fit at the
default `--min-std` 0.5 matches the grid at the voxel centres, where it is measured, with gaussians that differ
between them; carried off the lattice they show it, and every warm frame spends its 30 steps undoing that (the
mean move of a slot is a deviation a frame, the noise the geometry layer of a stream then carries). `--min-std`
(new; the effect's `minStd`, 0.5 by default) on the same runs:

| `--min-std` | rise fixture, carried start: frames 0 / 1 / 2 | blob sequence (turn and rise): frames 1-4 | mean L2 | flicker |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | 0.0199 / 0.1480 / 0.0199 | 0.068 0.054 0.037 0.029 | 0.02244 | 0.274 |
| 0.75 | 0.0206 / 0.0555 / 0.0206 | 0.032 0.031 0.026 0.023 | 0.01889 | 0.229 |
| 1.0 | 0.0190 / 0.0205 / 0.0190 | 0.021 0.020 0.019 0.018 | 0.01645 | 0.201 |

On single volumes (median of three, 100 steps) 1.0 is not a default: blob 10k 0.0269 → 0.0260, blob 50k 0.0119
→ 0.0277, smoke2 10k 0.123 → 0.199, smoke2 50k 0.062 → 0.212, explosion 10k / 50k unchanged (0.0796 / 0.0369);
smoke2's detail is a voxel wide. The default stays 0.5; a smooth sequence carried by its flow takes
`--min-std 1.0` (vol-stream's ladder, below). Not done: a test of the fit off the lattice (the grid given back at
points between the centres), which is what would choose the floor per volume.

### Sequences with a simulation's velocity (1 Nov, round 2)

Two Mantaflow bakes (Blender 5.3): an explosion, 128 x 128 x 192, and a smoke plume, 80 x 80 x 160, 120 frames each
at 24 fps, `density`, `temperature`, `flame` and `velocity` -- a staggered (MAC) vec3 grid in cells a Mantaflow time
unit, active where the density is; the active voxels change every frame. What a sequence needed for them:

- **`--velocity NAME`** (default `vel`) and **`--velocity-units world|mantaflow`** with **`--fps`**: Mantaflow's
  cells a time unit, of which a frame is 0.1 x 25 / fps (0.10417 at 24) -- no voxel size enters; `world` keeps
  world units a frame over the voxel. A grid of class `staggered` (read from the header, `NanoGrid::staggered`)
  has each component on its voxel's lower face: the voxel's own is the mean of its two faces (`vsPackLeaves`).
- **The flow on the frame's own leaves.** The frame before's flow was packed on the frame before's leaves and read
  through the current frame's leaf map, so wherever the topology changed (every frame here) it was read from the
  wrong voxels or not at all. It is now laid on the current frame's active voxels when the frame is fitted, and a
  gaussian on a voxel with none takes the mean of its neighbours' within two voxels.
- **Flicker and slots kept every frame**: the frame before's original density resampled onto the current leaves
  (a new kind of `vsFixture`, `VolumeSplats::resample`) and its gaussians evaluated there; before, both were
  reported only when two frames had the same leaves. The blob fixture's figures are unchanged (0.02244 / 0.27405).
- **The deformation of a carried gaussian.** The flow's gradient at the edge of a sparse flow read the outside as
  zero -- a whole velocity over a voxel -- and F = I + dt grad u crushed gaussians there: the explosion's warm fit
  went to a relative L2 of 26.8. Now: one-sided differences where a neighbour has no flow; a step whose det F
  leaves (0.5, 2) or whose dt grad u is past 0.25 (Frobenius) carries the centre alone; otherwise F keeps the
  volume. With volume kept but every gradient taken, the carried start still drifted (explosion frames 20-27,
  no warm step: 0.68 after one frame, 3.4 after seven) -- turbulence a voxel wide sheared gaussians into needles;
  with the gate, 0.60 then 0.84, against 0.47 then 1.17 not carried. The blob fixture (a rigid turn) is under the
  gate: 0.02262 against 0.02244.
- **`--prune-mass`, `--warm-prune-mass`** (new; the effect's `pruneMass`, 1e-6): a warm frame keeps every slot,
  so its densify rounds have none to give to new density; a larger floor frees slots there.

Measured (release, M5 Pro, the shared GPU lock -- shared with another agent's jobs --, the Mac's interactive use not
known; 20k gaussians; `sim*.sh`), mean over the frames / last frame / flicker / fit s a frame:

| | explosion, frames 5-34 | plume, frames 30-59 |
|---|---|---|
| independent | 0.0235 / 0.061 / 0.061 / 0.24 | 0.0109 / 0.016 / 0.031 / 0.19 |
| warm, not carried (30 Adam steps) | 0.639 / 0.508 / 1.461 / 0.22 | 0.472 / 0.414 / 1.340 / 0.11 |
| warm, carried (before the fixes above) | 26.8 / 36.4 / 21.7 / 1.77 | 0.380 / 0.332 / 1.130 / 0.23 |
| warm, carried, 30 Adam steps (fixed) | 0.287 / 0.321 / 0.773 / 0.36 | |
| warm, carried, 10 EM + 60 Adam | 0.068 / 0.097 / 0.187 / 0.27 | |
| warm, carried, 40 EM + 100 Adam at 0.1, `--warm-prune-mass 1e-5` | 0.0320 / 0.057 / 0.089 / 0.38 | |

A warm frame does not keep up with these: the density changes too much in a frame (not carried, one frame later
the error is 0.47 on the explosion and 0.38 on the plume, from 0.017 and 0.009), and only a full fit's steps from
the carried start come near the independent fits -- 36 % further, with more flicker, and slower. More Adam steps
alone made it worse (60 steps 0.89 against 30 steps 0.78, both with `--warm-prune-mass 3e-5`, before the gate),
more EM better: the warm frame's Adam,
whose moments start at zero and whose steps are normalised, moves every parameter whatever its gradient. Not done:
EM-only warm frames; the carried start at a coarser floor (`--min-std`) for these; recycling slots by contribution
rather than mass.

### Bytes a gaussian: the compact record (1 Nov)

Proposal 104's lane, gaussians and quantisation only. `--quantise half|byte` quantises the fit's records
(`vsQuantRange`, `vsQuantise`) and makes everything after -- the way back, `--measure`, `-o` -- from what the
compact records decode to, so their cost is measured as a fit's is; `--compact` writes them (a 64-byte header
with the twelve ranges, the index-to-world map, the words). The centre over the cloud's box and ln σ over its
range in 16 bits each, the precision's factor as its diagonals' logs and its off-diagonals over the geometric mean
of the diagonals beside them (which the fit holds within ±2) in halves (24 B) or in bytes over their ranges (20 B),
Cd rgb8 and the temperature in 8 bits. Against NanoVDB's own quantisations of the same density grid
(`nanovdb_convert --fp16/--fp8/--fp4/--fpN -r 0.01`, turned back into floats on the same topology and measured
with `--against`). `vdb2splat_opt3.sh`; release, M5 Pro, the shared GPU lock, the Mac's
interactive use not known; masked path traces E1b's (4096 paths):

| | bytes | B a gaussian | density relative L2 | PT ×1 | PT ×16 (smoke2) or ×1 (explosion) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| smoke2 50k / 300 steps, usdc (f32 + halves) | 3.20 MB | 64 | 0.03772 | 6.4·10⁻⁴ | 5.9·10⁻³ |
| the compact record, halves | 1.20 MB | 24 | 0.03777 | 6.4·10⁻⁴ | 5.9·10⁻³ |
| the compact record, bytes | 1.00 MB | 20 | 0.03803 | 6.4·10⁻⁴ | 5.9·10⁻³ |
| smoke2 as NanoVDB f32 / Fp16 / FpN 1 % / Fp8 / Fp4 | 22.6 / 12.2 / 12.0 / 7.0 / 4.5 MB | | 0 / 1·10⁻⁵ / 2·10⁻⁴ / 0.0031 / 0.0523 | – / 6·10⁻⁹ / 4·10⁻⁸ / 1.3·10⁻⁶ / 1.6·10⁻⁴ | – / 9·10⁻⁹ / 2·10⁻⁸ / 7.9·10⁻⁶ / 8.6·10⁻⁴ |
| explosion 50k / 100 steps, usdc | 3.30 MB | 66 | 0.03673 | | 5.3·10⁻⁴ |
| the compact record, halves / bytes | 1.20 / 1.00 MB | 24 / 20 | 0.03674 / 0.03689 | | 5.3·10⁻⁴ / 5.3·10⁻⁴ |
| explosion as NanoVDB f32 / Fp16 / FpN / Fp8 / Fp4 | 23.0 / 12.4 / 11.0 / 7.2 / 4.5 MB | | 0 / 1·10⁻⁵ / 0.0010 / 0.0016 / 0.0261 | | – / 8·10⁻⁹ / 1.7·10⁻⁷ / 1.1·10⁻⁶ / 1.5·10⁻⁴ |

The explosion's temperature (density-weighted relative L2) 0.2306 f32, 0.2306 with halves and bytes. The compact
record costs the fit nothing measurable in halves and 0.8 % of its density error in bytes, at 37 % and 31 % of the
usdc's bytes; NanoVDB's Fp4 is 4.5 times the bytes of the 20-byte cloud and further from the grid in density
(0.052 against 0.038 on smoke2), but closer in the path trace (its error is noise at the voxels, the cloud's is
missing detail); at Fp8 the grid is seven times the cloud and close to exact.

Read back: `--from-compact` takes the file, puts its words on the device and decodes them there
(`vsDequantise`, the decode of `vsQuantise` from the words and the header's ranges alone) into records that are
then given back, measured and written as a fit's. The four files above give the grids of the fits that wrote
them to a relative L2 of 1–2·10⁻⁵ (the same density error to five digits: smoke2 0.03777 / 0.03803, the
explosion 0.03674 / 0.03689, its temperature 0.2306). A dead slot is a record of zero words. Not done: the
renderer reading the compact file itself (here it is the command's way in), entropy coding of the words.

### Anchored surfel gaussians (`.asg`), decoded on the device (8 Nov)

3Dspace's proposal 001 (accepted): a converted cloud is surfels, locally flat,
with its slow attributes the patch's, so it is kept as anchors -- a frame, a
centre, ranges, a material, a Cryptomatte id, a CPCA transfer mean and a
shadow pattern each, 200 bytes on the pawn -- and leaves of a few bits a
gaussian read against them (their bitstream v1, proposal 002). The pawn
(326 265 gaussians, 5 193 anchors, transfer 9 + 27, open directions 64 bits)
is 19.3 bytes a gaussian with everything, against 36 for the compact record.

`scene/asg_decode.slang` decodes it a thread a gaussian: a binary search over
the anchors' `first`, then the leaf's fields read from the bit stream (two
words a field), into the float records the exporter takes and the transfer,
shadow, Cryptomatte and thin-wall arrays. Against 3Dspace's own decoder
(`asg_io.py unpack`), gaussian by gaussian: positions within 7.5e-9, rotations
8e-6, transfer 1.5e-7, every Cryptomatte id and every open-direction bit the
same. Rendered (raster, 1920x1080, the default dome and sun, framed), the two
decodes differ by relMSE 2e-7 (57 pixels over two 8-bit levels, ties in the
sort); against the original pawn both give relMSE 5.6e-5, p99 relative 3.7%,
11 889 pixels over two levels of 2 073 600, PSNR 52.1 dB. The decode takes
9.0 ms on the M5 Pro for the whole pawn, timed from the host (about 28 ns a
gaussian, 1.8 ms for a chunk of 65 536), before any work on it.

The first revision kept no unit, no index and no Cryptomatte manifest; without
the `ior` (1.5) the same decode rendered at relMSE 7.2e-4 against the
reference. Revision 2 keeps them in the header (and the manifest as a
section), and the shadow patterns as the primvar's own bytes. Read from it,
the decode against the original `pawn_gs.usdc`, both in metres, is the figure
above: relMSE 5.6e-5, PSNR 52.1 dB; the decode, 8.1 ms on the M5 Pro (Metal),
2.37 ms on an RTX 3070 laptop through CUDA and 2.32 ms through Vulkan (about
7 ns a gaussian; 0.5 ms a chunk of 65 536), the CUDA decode the same as the
reference's value for value. (3Dspace's own
`.usdc` files author no `metersPerUnit`, which USD then takes as 0.01; the
original authors 1.) Not done: the builder on the device, `.athc` chunks of anchors,
streaming, levels of detail, curvature, skinned clouds.

### The geometry layer of a volume stream, a third of the bytes (1 Nov, round 2)

Round 1's ladder spent 95 % of its bytes on the lossless geometry layer: 9.3 B a gaussian a frame at 16-bit
positions, 10-bit log scales and rotations, each frame a residual from the one before. Two things shrink it: the
fit's own noise from frame to frame, and the layer's precision and predictor. Release, M5 Pro, VideoToolbox at
quality 0.9, the shared GPU lock, the Mac's interactive use not known; the blob-sequence fixture (128³, 30 frames,
a geometry key every 30); `volstream_g1.sh` ... `volstream_g7.sh`, outputs under
`opt/vs3`, `opt/vs4`.

| round 1: residual from the frame before, 16 / 10 / 10 bits | 0.196 | 0.0244 | 0.0090 |
| the motion carried on (`--geometry-predict 2`) | 0.192 | 0.0244 | |

The flow is a rigid turn and rise, which the run's rigid motion predicts, yet a predicted frame costs nearly a

### Bricks: a volume larger than the device (1 Nov)

The whole Disney cloud (1.49 G active voxels, 1.89 M leaves and 789 k active tiles, 2.93 GB of `.vdb`) was refused
by memory: the fit's working buffers are some 60 bytes a voxel of its leaves (~110 GB), and reading it whole takes
~12 GB of host memory. `vdb2splat --tile-dir` fits it a brick at a time.

**The design.** The fit's error is local -- a voxel's value is the gaussians within 3.5 deviations of it -- so a
grid splits into spatial bricks whose fits are independent once each sees what lies about it. Considered and set
aside: splitting by Morton runs of leaves (the effect wants a box; runs make ragged boxes whose surface is all
margin) and streaming leaves through one fit (every Adam step visits every voxel: a fit of 1.49 G voxels through a
16 GB pool would page the whole grid in and out ~140 times).
- *The plan* is made from the tree's structure alone (`io::readVdbCells`, OpenVDB's delayed loading: 4.3 s and
  376 MB for the whole cloud): leaf-sized cells -- each leaf, each active tile cut into its 8³ cells -- cut by a
  k-d split at the median cell along the longest side, on cell planes, until a brick read with a margin of
  `--tile-margin` voxels (32) holds at most `--tile-cells` cells (from `--device-mb`: ~48 KB of pool a cell).
- *A brick is read alone*: `readGrid(name, box)` on a delayed-loading file seeks over every leaf outside the box
  and decompresses the ones inside (an eighth of the whole cloud: 0.8 s, 378 MB); the clip is then exact in index
  space. Host memory is the structure plus one brick.
- *Three passes*, every brick's result a file in the directory (a run stopped -- `--tile-seconds`, a timeout, a
  kill -- goes on from the brick it had not finished; this is what keeps each GPU job under ten minutes):
  1. sums (`vsBoxSums`): the core's mass, the mass read, the core's energy;
  2. the fit, of N × (the core's mass over the whole's) × (mass read over the core's) -- the fit also spends on the
     margin -- keeping the gaussians whose centre lies in the core (`vsSelect`);
  3. the seams' pass (`--tile-refine`, 30 Adam steps): each brick again, warm (the effect's `Previous`, slot for
     slot, no densify round, no prune) from every gaussian of pass 2 whose box meets what it reads, the core's kept.
  `--measure` gives each core back from the gaussians whose box reaches it and adds the squared sums: the whole
  grid's relative L2, the same number a whole-grid way back gives (checked on a 128³ blob: 0.06312 both ways).
  `--back --back-grid` gives the mixture back on another grid read whole -- another resolution of the volume,
  through `vsTransform` (the precision mapped K⁻ᵀ P K⁻¹ and factored again).

**Why the seams' pass.** The plain stitch left a seam. On the half cloud at 50k (4 bricks, margin 32) each brick's
own fit was 0.12–0.16 relative L2 over what it read, and the stitched mixture 0.199 against 0.152 unbricked, with a
bright band along the boundary in a close-up path trace: a core gaussian near the boundary was fitted beside its
brick's margin gaussians, which are thrown away, and the neighbour's core gaussians that replace them were fitted
beside other ones -- the tails overlap twice. A margin of 64 voxels (1.78 cells read a cell) only got to 0.183 at 88
s of fits. Fitting each brick again with its neighbours' own gaussians in its margin removes it: 30 steps 0.1518,
60 steps 0.1496. The sweep is Jacobi (every brick starts from pass 2), so the bricks' order decides nothing.

**Measured, the half cloud** (188 M voxels, 461 463 leaves; 50k; release build, M5 Pro, the shared GPU lock;
untiled = round 2's run, the same camera, light and 1024 paths; peak = `/usr/bin/time` peak footprint, which on
unified memory counts the device's buffers):

| | gaussians | fits, s | density L2 | masked PT relMSE (PSNR) | close-up masked PT | peak MB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| unbricked (`--device-mb 16384`) | 50000 | 51.2 | 0.1522 | 5.49·10⁻⁴ (44.59) | 2.32·10⁻⁴ | 16658 |
| 4 bricks, plain stitch | 50884 | 61.8 | 0.1991 | | 1.27·10⁻³ | 8916 |
| 4 bricks + seams' pass 30 (`--device-mb 8192`) | 50889 | 61.8 + 15.7 | 0.1518 | 5.66·10⁻⁴ (44.48) | 2.90·10⁻⁴ | 5244 (8799 with the half read whole for `--back`) |

Bricked, each brick's reading adds ~2.2 s twice (sums, fit) and the seams' pass once; the measure is 16.8 s. The
budget comes out 1.8 % over N (the margin's share of the gaussians is not exactly its share of the mass).
Images: `vdb2splat/opt/img/tile_half50_full.png`, `tile_half50_close_seam.png` (close-up across the boundary:
original, unbricked, plain stitch with its band, seams' pass), `tile_half50_close_seam_zoom.png`.

**Measured, the whole cloud** (1.49 G voxels; `-n 200000 --device-mb 10240`, margin 32, 30 seams' steps; 32
bricks of at most 218 453 cells, 1.46 cells read a cell; four GPU jobs of two commands, each command beginning no
brick after 200 s, resumed from the directory):

| | |
|---|---|
| plan | 3 122 022 cells (1 890 760 leaves, 789 002 active tiles); the structure read in ~4 s |
| sums pass | 32 bricks, 2.1–3.2 s each (a brick's read: the tree's structure, then its ~150 k leaves) |
| fits | 533.6 s (11.8–19.6 s a brick), a read 2.7–6.5 s each; the pool held 3.5–5.3 GB |
| seams' pass | 141.9 s; 185 122 → 184 812 gaussians |
| density relative L2 (brick by brick, 1.49 G voxels) | 0.1259 (bricks 0.085–0.193), largest difference 1.23; 110 s |
| given back on the half resolution's topology | 107.5 s; 0.1270 against the half's own density (its own 50k fit: 0.152) |
| peak footprint / RSS a job | 10.7 / 7.2 GB (sums and fits), 8.6 / 5.2 (fits, seams), 6.8 / 5.2 (measure), 8.6 / 5.5 (the half read whole for the way back) |
| sizes | `.vdb` 2930 MB; NanoVDB density ~4.4 GB (estimated from the half's 590 MB by cells); usdc 11.8 MB; compact record 3.7 MB (20 B a gaussian) |

A first try at `--device-mb 14336` (16 bricks, pool 8.4 GB) peaked at 17.6 GB of footprint -- the leaves' picture
(16 B a voxel of the brick) and the brick's grid sit beside the pool -- and was stopped; 10240 keeps it under 11 GB.
The budget lands short: a brick's fit spends more on its margin than the margin's share of the mass (the margin's
outer face is a cut through dense cloud, an edge the fit chases), so of 200k asked 185k were kept. The fits now feed
back what the bricks before kept: each brick aims at its share of the budget less what its predecessors fell short
by, and scales its read budget by the ratio of kept to mass-predicted kept so far: the half at 50k in 4 bricks then
keeps 49 897 (was 50 889) at 0.15226 against the unbricked 0.15215, fits 64.7 + 18.2 s; in 37 bricks of at most
30 000 cells (2.06 cells read a cell), 50 121 kept after the seams' pass at 0.16245 (fits 110.8 + 32.2 s, a peak
footprint of 1.7 GB): small bricks cost error (+7 %) and time, as their margins are a larger share of what is read,
so a brick should be as large as the pool allows.

The whole cloud's original is not path traced (its NanoVDB, ~4.4 GB, read whole needs ~12 GB of host memory first):
its gaussians are judged on the half resolution's topology against the half original, at its camera, light and
1024 paths. Masked PT relMSE 5.16·10⁻⁴ (PSNR 44.98) -- the half's own 50k fits: 5.49·10⁻⁴ unbricked, 5.66·10⁻⁴
bricked; in the close-up 3.40·10⁻⁴ (the half's bricked 50k 2.90·10⁻⁴). No boundary of the 32 bricks shows
(`vdb2splat/opt/img/tile_whole200k_full.png`: half original, half bricked 50k, whole 185k given back on the half;
`tile_whole200k_close.png`, the same close-up as above). The PT of the grid given back peaked at 5.7 GB.

## NVDEC: the video planes' decoder on CUDA (1 Nov)

`athenea video-encode --check`, `video-decode` and the live stream on Linux and Windows: NVIDIA's hardware HEVC
decoder behind the same `VideoDecoder` and `LumaTextures` as VideoToolbox (`modules/video/src/Nvdec.cpp`), so a
round trip is checked on the machine that encoded it.

### Design

- **Nothing linked, as NVENC.** The decoder library (`nvcuvid.dll`, `libnvcuvid.so.1`) is opened at run time by
  `platform::SharedLibrary`; its types are `dynlink_cuviddec.h` and `dynlink_nvcuvid.h` from the same
  nv-codec-headers tag (`n12.2.72.0`, MIT, NVDEC API 12.2). The CUDA driver's entry points the two codecs share
  moved to `src/Cuda.h` / `Cuda.cpp` (loaded and `cuInit`'ed once a process); NVENC's own loader keeps only its
  library. Where neither Apple nor Linux/Windows, `src/CodecNone.cpp` answers `Unsupported` for all three
  factories.
- **On the engine's context.** `createHardwareDecoder(codec, bits, device)` takes the engine's device (new,
  defaulted to none, VideoToolbox ignores it): on CUDA the decoder, its parser and a `cuvidCtxLock` live on the
  device's own `CUcontext` and copy on its stream; without one, on the first device's primary context (the one
  slang-rhi's CUDA device uses).
- **A unit in, its picture out.** The unit's 4-byte lengths are rewritten as start codes, the parameter sets
  before a key frame's (`annexB`, which now also takes a unit and its sets), and given to NVDEC's parser as one
  packet with `CUVID_PKT_ENDOFPICTURE` and no display delay, so the sequence, decode and display callbacks all
  run inside that call and the picture is out when it returns. The sequence callback makes the decoder (again
  only when the size changes): NV12, or P016 at 10 bits (the 10 bits high, as P010), cropped to the display
  area, and refuses a stream that is not HEVC 4:2:0, whose bit depth is not the header's, or whose SPS says
  video range -- NVDEC hands the samples over as coded, so nothing would be stretched, but a file then reads
  the same on both decoders.
- **The frame outlives the decoder's surfaces.** The picture is mapped (`cuvidMapVideoFrame64`), copied on the
  device (`cuMemcpy2DAsync`, luma then the second plane) into a pitched allocation the `DecodedFrame` owns,
  and unmapped. The allocations are pooled per picture size, so a decode allocates only while more frames are
  alive than before; VideoToolbox's pixel buffers are held the same way.
- **Textures of the device.** A CUDA array cannot alias linear memory, so `LumaTextures::wrap` makes an
  R8Unorm (R16Unorm at 10 bits) texture and, at 8 bits, an RG8Unorm one for the second plane, takes their
  `CUarray` from slang-rhi's native handle and copies the frame in (device to array, on the device's stream).
  The planes decode reads them as it reads VideoToolbox's. Nothing is read back: the samples go decoder ->
  device memory -> texture -> the planes kernels.

### Measured

RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (Windows, driver 621.01, CUDA backend), release build; whether the machine was otherwise in
use is not known. The sparrow's PLY pages, frames 0-29, as in the NVENC section: NVENC encodes, NVDEC decodes in
the same process (`--check`), against the Mac's `--units` replay of NVENC's file through VideoToolbox (the
NVENC section's figures). Means in steps of each attribute's quantisation, position error median / p99:

| setting | decoded by | position / opacity / log scale / rotation / DC / rest, mean steps | max steps (position / opacity / rotation) | position um, median / p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| quality 0.5 (QP 26) | VideoToolbox, `--units` on the Mac | 4.15 / 1.67 / 3.49 / 4.35 / 3.80 / 3.91 | 115 / 247 / 214 | 24 / 56 |
| quality 0.5 (QP 26) | NVDEC, `--check` on CUDA | 4.148 / 1.666 / 3.491 / 4.351 / 3.804 / 3.910 | 29.4 / 47.9 / 40.2 | 23.5 / 55.8 |
| `--bits 10` (P010 / P016) | VideoToolbox, `--units` | 17.1 / 11.6 / 15.1 / 18.3 / 16.0 | -- | 6.4 / 14.0 |
| `--bits 10` | NVDEC, `--check` | 17.10 / 11.55 / 15.11 / 18.33 / 15.95 / 16.26 | 113 / 158 / 201 | 6.4 / 14.0 |
| `--chroma --sh-degree 0` | VideoToolbox, `--units` | 4.15 / 1.65 / 3.50 / 4.35 / 11.0 | -- | 24 / 56 |
| `--chroma --sh-degree 0` | NVDEC, `--check` | 4.149 / 1.653 / 3.498 / 4.354 / 11.03 | 29.4 / 35.9 / 44.4 | 23.5 / 55.8 |

- **The same samples.** HEVC decoding is exact, so the two decoders give the same pictures; the means agree to the
  third digit and the position errors to the micrometre. The maxima are what differs: through `--units` a few
  splats took another Morton rank on the Mac than on CUDA and were measured against a neighbour (the NVENC
  section's reading); measured where the order was computed they fall from 115-247 to 29-48 steps at 8 bits.
  Every position high part came back exact in every run.
- **The volume ladder's 20k rung** (quality 0.9, `--order stable --geometry --geometry-key 30 --sh-degree 1`, the
  NVENC section's settings; the same PLY frames, checked equal by hash): 0.197 MB a frame (video 0.010), means
  0.219 / 0.692 / 0.054 / 0 / 0 / 0.797 steps, position 33.2 / 51.2 um, every high part exact. The same NVENC file
  replayed on the Mac (`--units --check`, VideoToolbox) gives every figure to the last digit, maxima included
  (0.50 / 12.1 / 0.12 / 0 / 0 / 13.6 steps), but a rotation p99 of 0.041 degrees against 0: a 20k-splat stable
  order is the same on both machines, so here nothing is measured against a neighbour.
- **Decode time** (medians a picture, p95 in brackets; `video-decode` is the stream already written, the same
  file on both machines; the Mac's under the shared GPU lock, its interactive use not known):

| stream | VideoToolbox, M5 Pro | NVDEC, RTX 3070 Laptop |
|---|---:|---:|
| sparrow, NVENC quality 0.5 (4.45 MB of video a picture, 4608 x 4480), `video-decode` | 34.0 (37.2) | 40.8 (42.7) |
| the same, inside `--check` (beside NVENC's encode) | -- | 43.5 (88.5) |
| `--bits 10`, inside `--check` | -- | 41.8 (88.9) |
| `--chroma --sh-degree 0` (1.58 MB, 2048 x 1920), inside `--check` | -- | 13.7 (27.7) |
| 20k rung (0.010 MB, 512 x 832), inside `--check` (the Mac's through `--units`) | 2.77 (3.95) | 0.73 (0.99) |

  The decode includes the unit's rewrite to Annex B, the map and the device copy out of the decoder's surface
  (about 31 MB at 4608 x 4480, not timed apart); it grows with the bits, as VideoToolbox's does (16 ms at 1.68 MB,
  45 ms at 5.89 MB in the sparrow table). Inside `--check` the p95 doubles, the decoder sharing the device with
  NVENC's encode and the planes kernels; alone (`video-decode`) it is 42.7 ms. The planes -> gaussians kernel
  after it took 3.1-3.3 ms at 4608 x 4480 (2.75 on the Mac). On the large pictures the laptop's NVDEC is 20 %
  slower than the M5 Pro's decoder; on the small ones, where a call's fixed cost is what is measured, four times
  faster.
- Tests: `athenea_video_tests` on the Windows machine (CUDA): 10 passed, the round trip through NVDEC among them
  (skipped before for want of a decoder). On the Mac: 9 passed, 1 skipped (VideoToolbox takes host samples only),
  as before.

### Not done

- Linux: built and run on Windows only; the path differs in the library names alone (`libnvcuvid.so.1`).
- The frame's two copies (surface -> the frame's memory -> a texture): a frame held as a mapped surface would save
  the first, but mapped surfaces are few and a live stream holds frames past the next decode; a texture over the
  frame's memory would save the second, which slang-rhi's CUDA backend does not offer (its textures are arrays).
- The textures are made for each frame; reusing the last frame's when the caller has let them go is not done.
- A device of another backend (Vulkan) gets a decoder but no textures (`Unsupported`): that would take the
  frame's memory exported to the other API, as gpu_host does for buffers.

The Mantaflow explosion (vdb2splat's section "Sequences with a simulation's velocity", frames 5-34, 20k) as a
stream with the same layer (`sim10.sh`):

| | fit mean L2 / flicker / s a frame | MB a frame | Mbit/s at 24 / 30 | decoded L2 / flicker |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| independent fits | 0.0235 / 0.061 / 0.23 | 0.204 | 39.2 / 49.0 | 0.0461 / 0.131 |
| warm, carried, a full fit's steps, `--warm-prune-mass 1e-5` | 0.0321 / 0.090 / 0.38 | 0.187 | 36.0 / 45.0 | 0.0461 / 0.133 |

Stable slots save 8 % of the bytes at the same decoded error: on this explosion the layer's residuals are the
fit's own moves, as on the blob before the floor; and the codec doubles the fit's error (11/6/6 bits and
quality 0.9 were chosen on the blob, whose gaussians are larger).

The plume (frames 30-59, 20k) the same way -- after a fix: a dead slot (one frame here had one) was written with an
opacity logit of −20, which the loader drops (it keeps 1/255 and over), so `video-encode --order stable` refused
the frame ("frame 12 has 19999 gaussians, the first 20000"); a dead slot is now written at the live ones' floor,
1/254, its ln σ still −10:

| | fit mean L2 / flicker / s a frame | MB a frame | Mbit/s at 24 / 30 | decoded L2 / flicker |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| independent fits | 0.0109 / 0.031 / 0.19 | 0.189 | 36.3 / 45.3 | 0.0558 / 0.201 |
| warm, carried, a full fit's steps, `--warm-prune-mass 1e-5` | 0.0144 / 0.043 / 0.27 | 0.194 | 37.2 / 46.5 | 0.0341 / 0.120 |

On the plume the stable slots are what the stream keeps: 3 % more bytes and 39 % less decoded error, though the
independent fits are closer before the codec -- a slot of an independent fit is another gaussian each frame, and
the layer's residuals from one to the next are coarse at 11/6/6 bits.

Finer settings on the same warm-slot frames (encode and decode only, `sim13.sh`): quality 0.95 with 12 / 7 / 7
bits is 0.220 MB a frame on the plume (decoded L2 0.0223, flicker 0.075) and 0.214 on the explosion (0.0373,
0.106); 12 / 8 / 8 at 0.9 is no better (0.0238 / 0.0382 at 0.223 / 0.216 MB); round 1's 16 / 10 / 10 with the
frame-before prediction at 0.95 is 0.29 MB for 0.0178 / 0.0341. For these grids 12 / 7 / 7 at 0.95 is the one
to stream: 12 % more bytes than 11 / 6 / 6 at 0.9 for a third less error on the plume.

## A medium on the web player (vol-web, 1 Nov)

The browser draws ordinary 3DGS splats; a medium of gaussians (proposal 105) is drawn by its optical depth
instead. The route kept is the simplest correct one: the light is baked by the engine, the alpha is computed by
the player.

- **The light, baked per frame by the engine.** `ATHENEA_VOLUME_PLY` writes, from any frame that draws a medium,
  the medium's gaussians with the radiance `VolumeSplatShading` baked for them (emission from the temperature by
  the black body, each light's single scattering through the cloud shadow map, the dome, Wrenninge's octaves) as
  a 3DGS PLY (`technique/volume_splat_ply.slang`). Nothing new is computed: the colour is exactly what vol-raster
  draws, so a browser frame and an engine frame differ only by how they composite. With an isotropic phase
  (`anisotropy` 0, the default) the radiance does not depend on the eye, so one bake serves every view. The
  colour is display-referred (Reinhard a channel, then sRGB): the video quantises colour over its range in 8
  bits, and a linear HDR range (fire at 30, smoke at 0.05) would leave the smoke a few levels. Each splat is
  written to the record it came from (the loader's `origin`), so a sequence's slots keep their places.
- **The alpha, by the player.** `video-encode --volume S` marks the file (header flag bit 8, S at offset 88);
  ln sigma travels in red's first rest coefficient as `vdb2splat --cloud` already put it. The player draws a
  splat with tau = S sigma sqrt(2 pi) / sqrt(dᵀ Σ⁻¹ d) (the exact line integral of the 3D gaussian along the
  eye's ray under the affine projection) times the projected Gaussian, alpha 1 − exp(−τ g). vol-raster's erf
  over the 3.5-sigma chord differs from it by under 0.6 % of the mass, more only with the camera inside a
  gaussian.
- **Rejected:** baking the alpha into a 3DGS opacity (an opacity is per splat, the optical depth depends on the
  view direction for an anisotropic gaussian, and a flat-topped 1 − exp(−τ g) is not o·g for τ past ~0.3);
  linear HDR colour in the video (above).
- **A sequence's temperature.** `vdb2splat --sequence` now reads `--temperature`'s grid on fitted frames (cold
  and warm), as a single frame does; an empty grid (a fire not lit yet, or out) counts as none.

### The explosions as streams, measured (1 Nov)

EmberGen's sample VDBs (JangaFX, CC0), no velocity grid. Release, M5 Pro, VideoToolbox, the shared GPU lock;
density scale 0.03, a key light (2, normalised, 1°) and a dim blue dome (0.05), the black body at
600 + 2400 t kelvin times 40 (t EmberGen's temperature, 0 to about 2).

- **Warm fits fail without a flow.** Gasoline explosion, 50k, warm from frame 2: density L2 0.056 (cold) ->
  0.20 -> 0.30 -> 0.44 by frame 6, and the warm fit's time grew from 0.5 to 35 s a frame by frame 22: the
  fireball outruns slots that can only be refined where they stand. Every frame is fitted on its own
  (`--independent`): 50k L2 0.096 at 1.81 s a frame, 20k 0.132 / 1.60 s, 10k 0.159 / 1.20 s (frames 4-99);
  mid-air explosion 0.099 / 2.30 s, 0.135 / 1.83 s, 0.161 / 1.45 s (frames 3-98); aerial explosion (24 M voxels a
  frame) 50k 0.161 / 12.1 s.
- **Order.** Independent fits share no slots and no count (49 998 to 50 000), so the geometry layer cannot
  predict (`--order stable` refuses them): every frame is a geometry key. Positions in the video over 256-splat
  boxes cost the error: at q0.7 the decoded density L2 is 0.313 against 0.129 with the geometry layer, for 0.382
  against 0.490 MB a frame. The rest's plane holding ln sigma wants q0.7 or more (q0.5: 0.266 with exact geometry).
- **The ladders** (geometry layer every frame 11/6/6, q0.7, sh-degree 1): 50k 0.490 MB a frame (118 Mbit/s at 30),
  20k 0.201 (48), 10k 0.104 (25), decoded L2 0.129 / 0.154 / 0.178 on the gasoline; the mid-air explosion within
  3 % of it. Encode 21.5 / 10.8 / 6.8 s for 96 frames.
- **The light against a path trace.** Gasoline frame 60, 50k, 512²: vol-raster with the fire off against the path
  trace of the original VDB (1024 paths, 4 bounces; the path tracer reads the density only, so no fire there),
  masked: relMSE 0.0171, PSNR 29.6 dB, SSIM 0.977, the raster 23 % brighter on the mean (Wrenninge's octaves
  against 4 real bounces). vol-raster frame with the fire 9.3 ms.
- **The bake** costs one `athenea stage` process a frame, 3.5 s, almost all of it start-up and the stage's
  load: 96 frames in 5.6 min a rung.
- **A spatial order does not save it** (`video-encode --cells`, gasoline 50k, q0.7, 11/6/6): cubes of 16 units,
  each owning its most gaussians over the sequence, gave 271 457 slots a frame (5.4x) and 0.616 MB at L2 0.135;
  one cube (the box's Morton rank, padded to 50 000) 0.508 MB at 0.140 predicting from the frame before, 0.486 MB
  at 0.148 with rigid runs -- against 0.490 MB at 0.129 with every frame a key. An independent fit places every
  gaussian anew, so the k-th of a cube is another gaussian the next frame and its residual costs a key.
- **All in video** (`--geometry-video`, 50k, q0.7): 0.887 MB a frame at L2 0.284 in each frame's order, 0.877 at
  0.341 in the box's Morton rank: the folded planes carry the positions of gaussians that jump frame to frame.
- **The browser against the engine** (gasoline frame 64, 50k, the same camera, masked, display values): blending
  the stream's display colours 0.012 relMSE (26.2 dB); undoing Reinhard in the decoder, blending linear radiance
  in float and applying Reinhard after, as the engine does, 0.0056 (29.8 dB).
- **Not done:** a slot order across independent fits (a GPU matching of each frame's gaussians to the frame
  before), which would let the geometry layer predict and cut its 0.37 MB a frame at 50k; a bake inside
  `vdb2splat` (no process a frame); fire in the path tracer, to judge the emission too.

**vol-stream merged, the web route under test** (1 Nov). vol-web carries vol-stream's velocity reading, advection
on changing topology, per-frame flicker and slots, the dead slot at 1/254 and NVDEC; the temperature a sequence's
fit reads is packed with the density, the flow laid on each frame's own leaves as vol-stream does. Release build,
M5 Pro: video 9 passed / 1 skipped (the device-memory encoder), aofx [vdb2splat] 3/3, volume 8/8, technique
[vdb2splat] 1/1, lod 37/37, usd [lod] 7/7, usd [volume] 13/13. New: `volume_ply_bake` (a stage of two media
baked into two PLYs through `ATHENEA_VOLUME_PLY`, each one record a gaussian and loaded back whole; 17.8 s) as
the fixture of `volume_ply_encode` (`video-encode --volume --cells --order stable --geometry --check` over the
two; 3.3 s), and the .athv round trip now holds the volume flag and its density scale.

**`video-encode --slots`** (1 Nov). A warm fit keeps each gaussian in its slot but its pool fills over the first
frames (the Mantaflow plume's first frame holds 9 662 gaussians, its 50k pool full from about frame 30) and a
frame may leave its last slot or two unused, so `--order stable` refused it ("frame 1 has 34024 gaussians, the
first 9637"). `--slots N` lays every frame out as N slots, its own first in their order and the rest dead specks
at the origin, as `vdb2splat --cloud` writes a dead slot (video_cells.slang's videoPadSlots). Checked by
`volume_ply_encode_slots` (two frames of 300 gaussians as 400 slots, decoded again, 2.2 s).
A dead slot `--slots` or `--cells` lays is a speck (log deviation ln 1e-6, as `vdb2splat --cloud` writes one): at
a deviation of one unit, the 10 363 dead slots of the plume's first 20k frame, all at the origin, would add an
optical depth of about 20 there (ln sigma -10, density scale 20).

**Our own simulations on the web player** (1 Nov, Blender Mantaflow bakes with their velocity). Warm stable slots
carried by the flow (40 EM + 100 Adam at 0.1, prune 1e-5), the light baked (`ATHENEA_VOLUME_PLY`, a z-up stage),
encoded with `--order stable --slots N`, the geometry layer at 12 / 7 / 7, video at quality 0.95, a key a second.
- **Which prediction.** On the plume's 120 frames at 20k: rigid runs (order 3) 0.285 MB a frame, decoded L2
  0.0404; linear (2) 0.288, 0.0431; the frame before (1) 0.275, 0.0431. Order 1 is the smallest and the web
  player decodes it (it has no order 3); the ladders use it.
- **Which rungs.** The plume's 50k pool fills slowly from a first frame of 9 662 gaussians and decodes no closer
  than 20k (0.0413 against 0.0404) at 2.6 times the bytes: its ladder is 20k / 10k, frames 1-90 (from about frame
  96 the smoke spreads flat on the domain's wall): 0.278 / 0.138 MB a frame (53 / 26 Mbit/s at 24 frames a
  second), decoded L2 0.0355 / 0.0440 (fit 0.0247 / 0.0328). The fireball's 50k does decode closer (frames 3-62:
  0.0499, 20k 0.0670, 10k 0.0985) at 0.706 / 0.261 / 0.123 MB a frame. For comparison, the EmberGen ladders
  (independent fits, the layer exact every frame, quality 0.7) are 0.20 MB a frame at 20k for a decoded L2 of
  0.154 (gasoline).
- **Not done:** order 3 in the web player; a fit whose first frame fills the pool (the plume's first frames are
  a small puff); fire whose flame grid does not fill the fireball (Mantaflow's flame here glows flat at any
  temperature mapping).

### The fireball's 50k rung on a phone (1 Nov)

A phone's Safari reported "Decoder failure" on the fireball's 50k rung (1024 x 896, level 3.1, `hvc1.1.6.L93.B0`)
and then drew nothing. Every published rung of every explosion ladder was decoded picture by picture through
WebCodecs on the Mac (Safari and Chrome, VideoToolbox, the player's own codec string and coded size): all decode,
none fails. Each rung's SPS level matches its codec string and its picture size (3.0 for 512 x 832, 3.1 for
1024 x 896, 4.0 for the all-in-video 1024 x 1280); every picture is within the sparrow's phone ladder's largest
(1024 x 960). What sets the fireball's 50k apart is its bit rate: quality 0.95, predicted pictures as large as its
keys (median 0.23 / 0.28 MB), 48 Mbit/s of video at 24 a second against 26-33 for the other explosions' 50k rungs
and 16 for the sparrow's top rung, the one stream seen to play on a phone (all-intra). Level 3.1 allows 10 Mbit/s;
the encoder writes the level from the picture's size alone. Whether the phone's decoder fails on that is not
known: no phone was at hand.

The player did not recover from any decoder failure: the failed decoder is closed, and closing it again at the
next key threw, so no new decoder was made. It now makes a new one at the next key, and a rung that fails twice
steps the ladder down (athv-player.js / athv-live.html, the web player's repository).

The same frames at lower video qualities (geometry layer unchanged, 0.456 MB a frame):

| quality | MB a frame (video + side) | video Mbit/s at 24 | decoded L2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.95 (published) | 0.706 (0.250 + 0.456) | 48.0 | 0.0499 |
| 0.9 | 0.669 (0.213 + 0.456) | 40.9 | 0.0514 |
| 0.8 | 0.613 (0.157 + 0.456) | 30.1 | 0.0613 |
| 0.7 | 0.578 (0.122 + 0.456) | 23.4 | 0.0800 |

The 20k rung (0.0670) decodes nearly as close as 50k at 0.8, so the rung stays at 0.95 until a phone shows that
its rate is what fails.

### Order 3 in the web player, and where it pays (1 Nov)

The web player (`athv-player.js`) now decodes the geometry layer's order 3 (FORMAT.md §8d) in its WGSL kernel.
Positions use the integer cluster motion. Rotations take the float steps in the engine's order of operations, with
Metal's rounding (half away from zero).

**Against the engine.** `video-decode --dump-state` writes the engine's state words for a frame. The player's
state words were read back after decoding the same stream to the same frame (Mac, Chrome and Safari give the same
words):

| stream | frame (from its key) | positions, scales | rotation words apart | codes apart |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| plume 20k, keys every 24 | 60 (12 after the key) | exact | 32 of 20 000 (0.16 %) | 18 by one, at most 3 |
| sparrow 150k, motion, keys staggered over 60 | 60 (all 61 frames) | exact | 61 of 149 714 (0.04 %) | 38 by one, at most 4 |

The words that differ are rotation steps that round the other way: sines, cosines and exponentials differ between
the two compilers. The difference carries to the next key, as §8d allows. Rounding half to even instead of away
from zero gave more differences (40 and 306), and normalising with `inverseSqrt` changed nothing.

**Where it pays.** Each published ladder was re-encoded at order 3 with otherwise the same options:

| stream | order 1 Mbit/s at 30 | order 3 | decoded quality, order 1 / order 3 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| sparrow 150k (all-intra q0.4, chroma, 11/8/8, keys 30) | 147.8 | 100.5 | close PSNR 34.17 / 34.15, flicker 3.06 / 3.07 |
| sparrow 75k | 76.6 | 57.4 | 29.34 / 29.33, flicker 4.89 / 4.89 |
| sparrow 40k | 44.9 | 34.4 | -- |
| sparrow 20k | 25.9 | 20.0 | -- |
| sparrow 10k (15 576) | 21.7 | 16.9 | 26.02 / 26.02, flicker 5.62 / 5.62 |
| plume 20k (90 frames, 12/7/7, q0.95) | 66.7 | 67.1 | density L2 0.0355 / 0.0366 |
| plume 10k | 33.1 | 33.2 | 0.0440 / 0.0455 |
| fireball 20k (60 frames) | 62.7 | 63.0 | 0.0670 / 0.0677 |

- **The sparrow** is a rig whose 256-runs move rigidly. Its order-3 ladder is 23-32 % smaller at the same picture.
- **The simulated media** have warm slots carried by a velocity field, so a run does not move as one body. Order 3
  is 0.2-0.6 % larger there and a little worse, and those ladders stay at order 1.
- **Independent fits** (the EmberGen explosions) have no stable order, so they have no prediction at all.

**The ground explosion (EmberGen, CC0).** Frames 20-115 were fitted independently and baked with density scale
0.05, emission 6 and K = 800 + 1200 flames. They were encoded as the gasoline was: each frame in its own order,
the geometry layer every frame at 11/6/6, video q0.7, keys every 30. The fits vary by a few gaussians a frame
(49 948 - 50 000), and the first frame sized the pictures. Every later frame with more gaussians then took a
second picture of its last few tens, which is no key where the ladder needs one. With `--max-picture 1024x896` the
pictures are sized for the first frame and a twentieth more, so each frame is one picture.

| rung | fit L2 (f32) | decoded L2 | MB a frame (video + side) | Mbit/s at 30 (video alone) |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 50k | 0.1175 | 0.156 | 0.469 (0.096 + 0.373) | 112.6 (23.0) |
| 20k | 0.2044 | 0.227 | 0.195 (0.043 + 0.152) | 46.7 (10.3) |
| 10k | 0.2732 | 0.288 | 0.103 (0.023 + 0.079) | 24.7 (5.5) |

- **Not done:** order 3 for media with velocity-carried slots (a per-run fit weighted by the velocity, or smaller
  runs); bit-exact float steps across compilers (an integer rotation step would make them exact).

## Several views from one load of a stage (7 Nov)

`athenea stage` drew one camera a process, so a turntable paid the stage's load
every frame: the USD, its textures, the dome, the kernels' compiles and the
acceleration structures. splat2mesh measured it on the dwarf (80 000 faces,
five 4096² textures, an HDRI dome): 45.8 s a 1080² frame in raster, 107 s path
traced at 96 paths a pixel, nearly all of it load. `--cameras FILE` and
`--turntable N` draw every view from one `StageRenderer`, writing one EXR each.

**Measured** on the dwarf, M5 Pro, release build:

| | three views, 540², rt, 32 paths, denoised | 24 views, 1080², raster |
|---|---|---|
| a process a view | 29.4 s (9.8 s a view) | 45.8 s a view (splat2mesh's figure) |
| one process | 16.1 s: first view 5.9 s, then 3.4 s | 18.5 s in all: first view 3.0 s, then 0.56 s median |

A view drawn this way is the view a process of its own draws: the same eye
through `--eye` and through `--cameras` gives the same raster image, and the
first path traced view is identical; later ones differ by the path seed only
(mean 4 × 10⁻⁴), since the seed runs on across a process's frames.

## A transfer baked on a cloud that has no mesh (7 Nov)

splat2mesh makes glass with no mesh: surfels on the level set of the opacity
field of a capture's glass gaussians, with their normals from its gradient.
mesh2splat's bake cannot take them: it path traces triangles, and the path
tracer meets a cloud only as a shadow (`PathTracer.cpp`, `kSplats`). The
crystal drawn in raster with no transfer came out chrome, and with
mesh2splat's transfer of a marching-cubes mesh it swirled.

**Design.** `athenea splat-transfer` (`CmdSplatTransfer.cpp`,
`rt/rt_splat_transfer.slang`) uploads every ParticleField of the stage, has
the splat ray tracer build its structures (`GaussianRayTracer::prepare`,
`shadowScene`, the hardware route), and traces them with the shadow query's
own rule: each particle at its peak along the ray (`shadowAlpha`). Two
passes:

- **Direct half and open directions,** for every gaussian of every cloud (a
  met particle's direct half is what the second pass reads): `grid²` rays
  over the octahedral grid, the direct half by the same quadrature the path
  tracer uses with cells -- each ray's transmittance times cos / pi times its
  cell's solid angle (4 / grid² |w|₁³) times the basis -- and a cell's bit
  open where the mean transmittance of its rays is over a half.
- **Indirect half and reflected field,** for the cloud baked: each ray of the
  facing hemisphere keeps the eight nearest particles it meets and blends
  them front to back; each met particle sends its albedo times its own
  direct half (one bounce). The field is that light under a white sky
  (albedo times the direct constant term times sqrt(4 pi)) projected with the
  cell's solid angle, then divided by the closed directions' own projection
  and projected again, as mesh2splat's bake does (`m2sFieldOverClosed`).

A ray starts off its gaussian's surface by `--offset` of its widest sigma, on
its own side, so it neither takes the gaussian itself nor grazes its
neighbours. A sheet is then open on both sides, which is what a sheet in
space sees; a closed shell is closed inwards by its far side. Outputs are
written at each gaussian's record in the file (`GpuSplats::origin`), so a
record dropped on loading keeps zeros and the arrays have the file's length.

**Checked.**

- A flat sheet of 101 × 101 surfels: every cell open; the direct half's
  constant term 0.28210 (Y₀ = 0.28209), the z term 0.3261 (0.4886 × 2/3 =
  0.3257), the zonal second-degree term 0.1584 (0.3154 / 2 = 0.1577).
- The paint test cloud (272 907 gaussians, ball and ground) baked again from
  its own gaussians, against mesh2splat's transfer of its meshes: direct half
  relMSE 0.0004, open-direction bits 99.7 % the same (95.8 % open against
  95.7 %), indirect half the same mean (0.0022 against 0.0021) with relMSE
  0.27 (mesh2splat's is path traced and noisier). The reflected field is not
  the same: on the ball's lower half, which reflects the ground, it reads the
  ground's radiance under a white sky as 0.9, mesh2splat's as 0.4 -- the
  ground's stored albedo is 1, the path tracer's bounce is off the scene's
  ground material, and which is right is not settled without the source
  scene. Rendered by the raster from the test camera under the studio dome,
  the two clouds differ by relMSE 0.025, SSIM 0.974, the mean within 1 %;
  what differs is the ball's lower half and its rim.
  Settled (8 Nov): the floor (`tests/data/tx/ground.usda`) has no material,
  only `displayColor` 0.45 0.40 0.35, which the path tracer shades and
  mesh2splat's bake bounces off; mesh2splat converted it white, the albedo of
  no material, so the field traced over the gaussians read a white floor.
  An unbound mesh now converts as the renderer draws it (its one
  `displayColor`, else 0.18). On the ball's 2 490 gaussians facing down, the
  reflected field's first coefficient: mesh2splat 0.864, splat-transfer 1.675
  before and 0.734 after; the 15% left is the path tracer's further bounces.
  Held by a test (`splat_transfer_renders_like_mesh2splat`): the paint scene
  converted whole and baked again by splat-transfer, both rasterised with the
  meshes off, under the stage's pale dome and sun relMSE 0.0026 and under a
  tinted sky without a sun 0.0049, the means 1.9% apart; held at 0.01 and 3%.
- With the rays started a quarter of a sigma off the surface, they grazed the
  ground's neighbouring gaussians, and its field read the bright ground at
  the horizon (0.28 median against mesh2splat's 0.08 from a sigma off). One
  sigma is the default; two changes nothing more.
- splat2mesh's dragon (269 609 glass surfels and 215 843 gaussians of its
  body): 2 min 9 s for the glass, 1 min 38 s for the body, on the Mac's GPU
  (about 500 million rays a pass at grid 32). The glass's open directions
  are 99 % on the side its normals face. In raster the crystal no longer
  swirls; it reads more silver than glass.

**A solid glass, seen through.** Baked as an opaque surface, the dragon's
crystal had its directions behind its surface closed by its own far side, and
its field there showed its own shell: in raster it read as polished silver
and showed nothing behind it (splat2mesh, after the user's "it is not
transparent"). The path tracer bakes a transmitting surface over the whole
sphere, a sample behind it bent in by the index and the path sent on through
the glass. The bake now does the same where the prim's
`primvars:athenea:splat:ior` is over 1: a ray behind the surface is bent by
`refractInto` and passes the glass's own particles, and the field is over the
sphere. A first version also opened the glass's cells behind it (47.4 % open,
30 % in front): the dragon's body showed through the crystal, but it read
dark grey. The raster's lens (`splat_relight`, "a solid glass is a lens")
reads the field along the eye's ray through the glass and expects it to hold
what comes through under a white sky -- the glass's throughput, the sky where
nothing stands -- and draws the bent sky in proportion; the field held only
what the rays met, so every open way through read closed and dark. As the
path tracer bakes it now: the cells behind a glass closed by its own far face
(13.8 % open, 99 % in front), and its field behind it the throughput (the
dielectric's Fresnel at entry, squared for the two faces, and the tint twice)
times what the bent ray meets plus what is left of the white sky past it,
those directions counted closed for the field's normalisation. In raster the
crystal then reads a light lilac glass, near the path traced one, a little
milky where the path tracer shows the scene through it. 3 min 33 s for the
glass.

**The far face.** Seen from the front, splat2mesh's lighter crystal (82 892
surfels) still read dark mauve in raster where the path traced one is light
lilac: the ray bent in went on straight to the dragon's dark body behind it,
where the path tracer bends it again at the far face, out to the room. The
bake now finds that face -- the nearest of the glass's own particles of real
opacity along the bent ray -- and bends the ray out there through that
particle's normal (reflecting it where total internal reflection holds it),
with that face's Fresnel in the throughput; what the ray meets past it is
what the field holds. From splat2mesh's camera the crystal reads a light,
see-through lilac, near the path traced frame. A ray reflected at the far
face is followed once, not through further bounces inside.

**The lens, ball or slab.** With its curvature computed from the level set's
Hessian (median |k| about 15 /m on its flat faces), splat2mesh's crystal read
lilac and see-through in raster, but its large prism still swirled in rings.
The raster's lens (`splat_relight`'s `lensExit`) takes the far face from a
sphere of the mean curvature, and that sphere's exit does not depend on its
radius: the far normal is `t1 * 2 cos + n`, the chord over the radius being
`2 cos` whatever the radius. Any curvature over zero turns the room over as a
whole ball does, none leaves it straight as a slab, and on a facet whose
curvature is noise about zero the neighbours flipped between the two. The
bake now asks the far faces it already meets which the glass is: over the
ways through, each far face's normal against the ball's far normal and
against the slab's (`-n`), and the lens curvature written is the closer's --
the prim's own where the ball wins and it is convex, else `2 / thickness`
from the head-on thickness, and zeros where the slab wins. No new stream: the
web player and the Unreal plugin read the curvature already. On the crystal
(82 892 gaussians) 23 196 took the ball and 59 696 the slab, at no cost to
the bake (2 min 17 s); from splat2mesh's camera its large prism shows the
room straight through its facets instead of rings, and the frame costs the
same (3.38 s against 3.31 s before, medians of three of the whole `athenea
stage` run, load included). What a slab leaves out is a prism's own deviation, its faces not
parallel; some rings stay at the crystal's foot, where the path traced frame
has rings of its own.

**Not done.** A prism's deviation in the raster's lens (two faces not
parallel); more than one reflection inside the glass; a bounce off a met coat or metal (its specular share); more than one
prim a run; a test in the suite (the checks above were run by hand); a
ComputeBvh route for devices with no ray queries.


## The release on three systems, and CUDA from the package on Linux (8 Nov)

0.5.0 is the first release whose Blender add-on is packaged for macOS, Linux
and Windows, one zip a system whose manifest names that platform alone
(`package-blender-addon.sh` on macOS and Linux, `.ps1` on Windows).

- **CUDA on Linux without a toolkit.** slang-rhi looks for NVRTC under
  `CUDA_PATH`, `/usr/local/cuda*` and `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` only, as a
  file called `libnvrtc.so`. The Linux archive carried NVRTC in its `lib/` but
  nothing pointed there, so a machine with the driver alone could not open
  CUDA (0.3.0 had the same gap). The engine now points `CUDA_PATH` at a
  package root whose `lib/libnvrtc.so` and `include/cuda_runtime.h` exist, as
  it did on Windows for `bin\nvrtc64_120_0.dll`; `ATHENEA_CUDA_RUNTIME` gives
  `package.sh` that `lib/` and `include/`.
- **No symbolic links in the add-on.** Blender unpacks an extension with
  Python's `zipfile`, which writes a link as a small file holding its target.
  On Linux every library goes in as a copy under the name it is loaded by
  (its soname, or `libnvrtc.so`), and the script stops on a link.
- **The Windows add-on** carries what `dumpbin /dependents` finds hdAthenea
  loading that is neither in Blender's `blender.shared` nor in `System32`,
  Slang's GLSL modules, DXC, and CUDA's runtime and headers in `plugin\usd`.
## Blender on Windows: the exit, the flatten, what F12 gathered, the OpenFX bundle (25 Oct)

The issues the Windows run of 19 Oct left (#40 to #43), on the same laptop (RTX 3070 Laptop GPU, CUDA, Blender 5.3
beta), with the path tracer on the compute BVH (*Path tracing on CUDA through the compute BVH*, 24 Oct). Each was
reproduced with `tests/blender` scripts run headless against the build tree's plugin.

**#41, Blender's 0xC0000409 on its way out.** 0xC0000409 is how Windows ends a process that calls `abort()`, and two
different faults reached it through the same door: slang-rhi asserting on a failed CUDA call.

- *The process context outlived the driver.* A command run inside the host (`athenea_mesh2splat`,
